stem: Cloud Kicks wants a report to categorize accounts into small, medium, and large based on the dollar value found in the Contract Value field. Which feature should a Platform Administrator use to meet this request?

options.text: Group Rows
Filter Logic
Detail Column
Bucket Column

sourceExplanation: A Bucket Column allows a Platform Administrator to group report records into meaningful categories—such as Small, Medium, and Large—based on ranges of a numeric field like Contract Value. This can be done directly within the report without creating a formula field, making it ideal for categorizing dollar values. Key takeaway: Remember: bucketing is configured inside the report builder, so no schema change (formula field) is needed; buckets work on numeric, picklist and text fields. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Group Rows organizes records based on the exact value of a field. It does not allow defining custom value ranges (for example, dollar thresholds for small, medium, and large). • Option B: Filter Logic controls how multiple filters are evaluated (AND/OR). It limits which records appear in the report but does not categorize or label data. • Option C: A Detail Column simply displays field values in the report. It does not provide any grouping or categorization functionality.

stem: Universal Containers wants to ensure that cases are routed to the right people at the right time, but there is a growing support organization. The business wants to be able to move people around and adjust the work they get without having to request extra assistance or rely on the administrator teams. Which tool allows the business to control its own assignment of work?

options.text: Case Assignment Rules
Email-to-Case
Omni-Channel
Lead Assignment Rules

sourceExplanation: Omni-Channel allows the business to dynamically route work to the right people at the right time based on agent availability, capacity, and skills. Supervisors can adjust routing, move people between queues, and control workload distribution without needing ongoing help from administrators, which is ideal for a growing support organization. Key takeaway: Omni-Channel supervisors can change agent capacity, skills and queue membership themselves, which removes the dependency on administrators for day-to-day routing changes. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Case Assignment Rules assign cases only at creation or update time based on static criteria. Any change to routing logic typically requires administrator involvement, making them less flexible for frequent business-driven adjustments. • Option B: Email-to-Case only converts incoming emails into cases. It does not manage who receives the work or how it is distributed. • Option D: Lead Assignment Rules apply only to leads, not cases, and do not support dynamic workload management for support teams.

stem: Cloud Kicks is concerned that not everyone on the sales team is entering key data into accounts and opportunities that they own. Also, the team is concerned that if the key information changes, it does not get updated in Salesforce. A Platform Administrator wants to get a better understanding of their data quality and record completeness. What should the administrator do to accomplish this?

options.text: Explore AppExchange for data quality and record completeness solutions.
Create a report for Accounts and Opportunities highlighting missing data.
Subscribe the sales reps to a monthly report for accounts and opportunities.
Configure the key fields as required fields on the page layout.

sourceExplanation: Creating reports that highlight missing or incomplete key fields allows the Platform Administrator to analyze data quality and record completeness across the organization. This provides visibility into where data is missing, who owns the records, and which fields are not being maintained, helping identify patterns and areas for improvement. Key takeaway: Start data quality work by measuring it: a report with filters such as "Field equals blank" reveals incompleteness before you decide on enforcement tools. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Third-party tools may help, but they are not required to understand current data quality. Salesforce reporting can provide the needed insight without additional cost or complexity. • Option C: Subscribing users to reports helps with monitoring, but it does not by itself give the administrator a structured way to analyze and assess overall data quality. • Option D: Making fields required enforces future data entry but does not help the administrator understand existing data quality issues or completeness gaps.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has two different sales processes: one for business opportunities with four stages and one for partner opportunities with eight stages. Both processes will vary in page layouts and picklist value options. What should a Platform Administrator configure to meet these requirements?

options.text: Different page layouts that control the picklist values for the opportunity types
Separate record types and sales processes for the different types of opportunities
Validation rules that ensure that users are entering accurate sales stage information
Public groups to limit record types and sales processes for opportunities

sourceExplanation: Salesforce uses record types to support multiple business processes on the same object. By creating separate record types and associating each with its own sales process, the Platform Administrator can define different stage picklist values (4 stages vs. 8 stages), assign different page layouts per record type, and control which users see which process. This fully meets the requirement for different stages, layouts, and picklist options. Key takeaway: Rule of thumb: different processes (stage or status values) = record types + business processes; different fields = page layouts assigned by record type and profile. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Page layouts control field placement and visibility but do not control picklist values like Opportunity Stage. Picklist values are controlled by sales processes, not layouts. • Option C: Validation rules enforce data quality but do not create or manage multiple sales processes, stages, or layouts. • Option D: Public groups are used for sharing, queues, and access control. They do not control record types, sales processes, or page layouts.

stem: Cloud Kicks has hired a new sales executive who wants to implement a document merge solution in Salesforce. How should a Platform Administrator implement this solution?

options.text: Download the solution from AppExchange.
Install a package from the Partner Portal.
Create a managed package in AppExchange.
Configure the package from Salesforce Setup.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce does not provide a native document merge solution that meets advanced business needs. AppExchange offers many prebuilt, supported document merge solutions (such as tools for generating contracts, proposals, and quotes). Downloading a solution from AppExchange is the fastest, recommended, and scalable approach for implementing document merge functionality. Key takeaway: When a common business need is not native (document generation, e-signature), the exam expects you to look for an AppExchange solution first. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: The Partner Portal is used by ISVs and partners to manage their own solutions, not by customers to install applications. • Option C: Creating a managed package is done when building and distributing a custom app, not when implementing an existing document merge solution. • Option D: Setup is used to configure features and installed packages, but it does not provide a document merge solution by itself.

stem: How should a Platform Administrator view Currencies, Fiscal Year settings, and Business Hours in Salesforce?

options.text: User Management Settings
Company Settings
Custom Settings
Feature Settings

sourceExplanation: Company Settings in Salesforce Setup is where organization-wide configurations are managed. This includes Currencies, Fiscal Year, and Business Hours, all of which apply across the entire org and define how Salesforce operates at a company level. Key takeaway: Company Settings (Company Information, Fiscal Year, Business Hours, Holidays, Language and Locale) hold org-wide configuration, not user-specific settings. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: These settings control users, profiles, roles, and permissions. They do not manage org-wide operational settings like currency or fiscal calendars. • Option C: Custom Settings store custom application data for use in automation and code. They are not used to configure core company-wide features. • Option D: Feature Settings organize configuration pages for specific Salesforce features (such as Sales or Service), but Currencies, Fiscal Year, and Business Hours are not configured there.

stem: A VP of sales needs to report on records owned by individuals in various parts of the role hierarchy. The organization-wide default is set to Private. What should a Platform Administrator configure to achieve this?

options.text: Field-Level Security
Sharing Rules
Permission Sets
Restriction Rules

sourceExplanation: With the organization-wide default set to Private, users can only see records they own (and those shared with them). Sharing Rules allow a Platform Administrator to grant record access automatically to users based on role hierarchy, roles, or groups. This enables the VP of Sales to report on records owned by users in different parts of the role hierarchy without changing ownership or OWD settings. Key takeaway: With a Private OWD, sharing rules open access horizontally or to groups; the role hierarchy only opens access upward to managers. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Field-level security controls visibility and edit access to individual fields, not access to records themselves. • Option C: Permission sets grant additional object and field permissions, but they do not provide record-level access when OWD is Private. • Option D: Restriction rules are used to limit access to records users would otherwise be able to see. They cannot be used to expand access.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has created an approval process for time-off requests. Which two automated actions are available for the administrator to add as part of the approval process?

options.text: Field Update
Email Alert
Chatter Post
Autolaunched Flow

sourceExplanation: Salesforce approval processes support several built-in automated actions that can occur when a request is submitted, approved, rejected, or recalled. • Field Update allows the administrator to automatically update fields on the time-off request record (for example, updating status to Approved or Rejected). • Email Alert enables automatic notifications to be sent to employees, managers, or HR when the approval status changes. Key takeaway: Approval process actions are Field Update, Email Alert, Task and Outbound Message; flows and Chatter posts are not native approval actions. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: While Chatter posts can be triggered by some automation tools, they are not a standard automated action type within approval processes. • Option D: Approval processes do not directly support launching flows as an approval action. Flows must be triggered separately (for example, using record-triggered automation).

stem: At Cloud Kicks, sales reps use discounts on the opportunity record to help win sales on particular products. When an opportunity is won, they then have to manually apply the discount to the related opportunity products. The sales manager has asked if there is a way to automate this time-consuming task. What should a Platform Administrator use to deliver this requirement?

options.text: Approval Process
Formula Field
Flow Builder
Prebuilt Macro

sourceExplanation: Flow Builder can automate record updates when specific events occur. In this case, a record-triggered flow can run when an Opportunity is marked Closed Won and automatically apply the discount from the Opportunity record to the related Opportunity Products, eliminating the need for manual updates by sales reps. Key takeaway: Updating related child records when a parent changes is a classic record-triggered flow use case (Get Records → Loop → Update Records). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Approval processes are used to approve or reject records, not to synchronize or copy values between related records. • Option B: Formula fields calculate values dynamically but cannot write values back to other records, such as Opportunity Products. • Option D: Macros are used in Service Cloud to automate repetitive user actions, not to perform backend data updates across related records.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks is setting up a new Salesforce instance. The business requirements mandate that the marketers are given access to opportunities in order to maintain the campaign relationships on each opportunity. The administrator decides to assign the Marketing User profile. What should the administrator do next to achieve this requirement?

options.text: Edit the object permissions to include Opportunity.
Add a custom permission set to include Opportunity.
Edit the role to enable Sales access.
Configure the assigned apps to include Opportunity.

sourceExplanation: The Marketing User profile does not include access to Opportunities by default. Best practice in Salesforce is to avoid modifying standard profiles and instead use permission sets to grant additional access. By creating and assigning a custom permission set with Opportunity access, the administrator can meet the requirement while keeping the profile intact and scalable. Key takeaway: Best practice: never edit standard profiles; extend access with permission sets or permission set groups. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This would require modifying the standard Marketing User profile, which is not recommended and reduces flexibility for future changes. • Option C: Roles control record visibility through the role hierarchy, not object-level access. Editing roles will not grant access to Opportunities. • Option D: Apps only control navigation and visibility of tabs, not whether a user has permission to access an object.

stem: Cloud Kicks has implemented an Employee Agent to answer benefits questions for its employees. How should a Platform Administrator prevent the agent from responding to staff members' questions about the CEO's private health plan and benefits?

options.text: Configure assignment rules to assign the agent to employee data.
Ensure the users' permissions and field-level security restrict access to the CEO's health plan.
Modify the agent's instructions and guardrails to block questions related to the CEO's health plan.
Train the agent on employee health plans instead of the CEO's health plan.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, data security always takes precedence over automation or AI behavior. By using permissions, sharing rules, and field-level security, the Platform Administrator ensures that the Employee Agent cannot access sensitive records such as the CEO's health plan. Even if the agent is asked a question, it will not have visibility into restricted data, preventing accidental disclosure. Key takeaway: AI agents respect the running user's security: if a user cannot access data through sharing and FLS, the agent cannot expose it either. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Assignment rules determine who owns or is routed records, but they do not prevent an agent from accessing restricted data once it exists. • Option C: This may reduce the risk, but it is not a reliable security measure, because agents cannot enforce data-level security—restricted records must be secured at the Salesforce data level. • Option D: Training affects AI knowledge and response quality, but it does not prevent access to sensitive records if permissions allow it.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has the Case object set to private. The support manager raised a concern that reps have a broader view of data than expected and can see all cases on their group's dashboards. What is causing reps to have inappropriate access to data on dashboards?

options.text: Dashboard Filters
Public Dashboards
Dashboard's running user
Dashboard Subscriptions

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, a dashboard displays data based on the running user. If the dashboard is set to run as a user with broader access, such as a manager or system admin, all users who view the dashboard will see the data that the running user can access—regardless of their own sharing settings. This explains why support reps are seeing more cases than expected on their group dashboards even though the Case object is set to Private. Key takeaway: Dashboards run as a specific user unless they are dynamic; always check "View Dashboard As" when users see more data than expected. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Filters only narrow or segment data for the dashboard; they do not override sharing rules or object-level access. • Option B: Making a dashboard public controls who can view the dashboard, but it does not change what data is visible; the running user still dictates record visibility. • Option D: Subscriptions only allow users to receive scheduled emails of dashboard snapshots; they do not affect data access in Salesforce.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to leverage roll-up summaries on the Account object. Which standard object supports this roll-up summary natively?

options.text: Opportunity
Contact
Case
Campaigns

sourceExplanation: Roll-up summary fields allow you to aggregate data from related child records on a parent record. In Salesforce, Accounts can natively have roll-up summaries of Opportunities, because there is a master-detail relationship (or the standard Account → Opportunity relationship supports this aggregation). You can sum, count, or find min/max values of Opportunities directly on the Account. Key takeaway: Account supports native roll-up summaries of Opportunities (and some other related objects) even though it is not a true master-detail relationship. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: The relationship between Account and Contact is a lookup, not a master-detail. Standard roll-up summary fields cannot be created on lookup relationships without using automation or declarative tools like Flow or AppExchange packages. • Option C: Cases are related to Accounts via a lookup, so native roll-up summaries are not supported. • Option D: Campaigns are related to Leads and Contacts, not Accounts via a master-detail relationship. Therefore, roll-up summaries on Account for Campaigns are not supported natively.

stem: Which two actions should a Platform Administrator perform with Case escalation rules?

options.text: Send email notifications.
Change the Case Priority.
Reopen the Case.
Reassign the Case.

sourceExplanation: Case escalation rules automate actions when cases meet certain criteria and are not resolved within a specified time. The two standard actions supported by escalation rules are: • Send email notifications: Automatically notifies the case owner, manager, or a queue when a case is escalated. • Reassign the Case: Moves the case to a different user or queue as part of the escalation process. Key takeaway: Escalation rule entries can reassign the case and notify users; changing priority or other fields requires additional automation. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Escalation rules do not allow modifying field values like Priority. Changing a field would require a workflow, process builder, or flow. • Option C: Escalation rules cannot change the status of a case. Reopening a case requires manual action or automation outside the escalation rule.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants emails received from customers to generate cases automatically. How should a Platform Administrator ensure that the emails are sent to the correct queue?

options.text: Create an escalation rule to send cases to the correct queue.
Use a custom email service to set the owner of the case upon creation.
Utilize a flow to identify the correct queue and assign the case.
Configure Email-to-Case so emails are delivered to the correct queue.

sourceExplanation: Email-to-Case is the standard Salesforce feature for automatically converting incoming emails into cases. When configuring Email-to-Case, the administrator can assign the incoming emails to a specific queue based on criteria such as support type or email address. This ensures that cases are created with the correct ownership from the start. Key takeaway: Email-to-Case routing addresses can set Case Origin and Priority, and assignment rules then place the case in the right queue. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Escalation rules only act after a case is created and has not been resolved within a set timeframe. They cannot control the initial assignment when the email first generates the case. • Option B: While possible, a custom email service is more complex and requires Apex development. Email-to-Case provides this functionality natively without code. • Option C: Flows can update ownership after the case is created, but Email-to-Case allows direct assignment during creation, which is more efficient and reliable.

stem: Leadership at Cloud Kicks wants to go beyond knowing how long a case has been open for, to knowing how long a case has sat with different teams. Which tool gives a Platform Administrator the ability to track the time a case sits and provide relevant reporting?

options.text: Escalation Rules with Business Hours
Record-Triggered Flows with Business Hours
Case Assignment Rules with Business Hours
Milestones with Business Hours

sourceExplanation: Milestones are part of Salesforce Entitlement Management and are designed to track specific service targets, such as response or resolution times, within defined business hours. Milestones can track how long a case spends in a particular stage or with a specific team, providing detailed insights for reporting and SLA compliance. Key takeaway: Milestones measure time against service targets and can be reported on; combining them with business hours gives accurate SLA reporting. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Escalation rules only trigger actions (like notifications or reassignment) when a case breaches a time threshold. They do not provide detailed tracking of time spent per stage or team for reporting purposes. • Option B: Flows can automate updates or actions but cannot natively calculate or report on time spent per team without significant custom logic. • Option C: Assignment rules control ownership when cases are created but do not track the duration a case spends with teams.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks needs to export a file of closed won opportunities from the last 90 days. The file should include the Opportunity Name, ID, Close Date, and Amount. What should the administrator use to export this file?

options.text: Data Loader
Data Import Wizard
Data Cloud Connection
Data Export Service

sourceExplanation: Data Loader is a Salesforce tool that allows administrators to export large volumes of data with specific filters and selected fields. It supports exporting records like closed won opportunities from the last 90 days, including the Opportunity Name, ID, Close Date, and Amount, and allows you to save the results as a CSV file for reporting or analysis. Key takeaway: Data Loader supports SOQL-filtered exports with selected fields; the Import Wizard cannot export and the weekly Data Export exports all records. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: The Data Import Wizard is used to import data into Salesforce, not to export data. • Option C: This is used for connecting external data sources to Salesforce (Data Cloud) and is not intended for exporting standard object data like opportunities. • Option D: Data Export Service creates scheduled or manual full exports of Salesforce data, but it exports entire objects or selected fields without easy filtering by criteria like "closed won in the last 90 days". Data Loader is better for targeted exports.

stem: The Cloud Kicks CFO requires any opportunity over $100,000 to be automatically sent to them, so they can sign off on the record before the deal closes. Which feature should a Platform Administrator use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Submit for Approval button
Einstein Next Best Action
Apex Triggers
Flow Approvals

sourceExplanation: To automatically submit opportunities over $100,000 for the CFO's sign-off: • A Record-Triggered Flow runs whenever an Opportunity is created or updated. • The flow checks if Amount > $100,000. • If true, it uses the "Submit for Approval" action inside the flow to automatically launch a pre-configured Approval Process. This approach combines automation with Salesforce's standard approval mechanism, achieving a fully declarative solution that meets the "automatically" requirement. Key takeaway: Approvals can be orchestrated in Flow; a record-triggered flow can automatically submit records meeting criteria so users do not need to click Submit for Approval. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This button is manual; a user must click it, which does not satisfy automatic submission. • Option B: Provides recommendations, not enforced approvals. • Option C: This is a code-based solution; unnecessary when Flow can handle it declaratively.

stem: Universal Containers wants to implement collaborative selling where multiple roles work together on customer accounts. Sales reps need full access to their assigned accounts, while customer support reps and sales engineers need access to opportunities and cases related to specific accounts they support. The sales manager wants to streamline the process by automatically adding the same team members to multiple accounts. Which feature should a Platform Administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Set up default account teams with specified access levels for different team roles.
Create sharing rules to grant access to opportunities and cases for support teams.
Configure role hierarchy to automatically grant account access to the appropriate teams.
Use permission sets to provide additional access to account-related records.

sourceExplanation: Account Teams in Salesforce are designed for collaborative selling. They allow multiple users to work on the same account while giving each user specific access levels to the account and its related records. Default account teams allow administrators to automatically add team members with predefined roles and access levels whenever an account is created or assigned, streamlining the process across multiple accounts. Key takeaway: Default account teams let each user define their usual team with roles and access levels, then add it automatically to accounts they own. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Sharing rules can give access based on criteria or ownership, but they cannot define collaborative account teams or automatically add multiple team members with specific roles. • Option C: Role hierarchy grants access upwards in the hierarchy, but it cannot provide selective access for multiple team members across different roles. • Option D: Permission sets control object- and field-level access, not record-specific collaborative access like account teams provide.

stem: A Platform Administrator wants to customize the navigation menu for users in the Salesforce mobile app. The organization has not yet implemented any Lightning apps for mobile use. Which statement about the Mobile Only app navigation is correct?

options.text: Lightning pages and Visualforce pages automatically appear in the Mobile Only navigation menu without requiring tabs to be created first.
The Mobile Only app can be customized to show different navigation menus for different user profiles and permission sets.
The first four items in the Mobile Only navigation menu appear both in the navigation menu and in the navigation bar at the bottom of the screen.
The Mobile Only app automatically includes all standard Salesforce objects in the navigation menu based on user permissions.

sourceExplanation: In the Salesforce mobile app, the Mobile Only app provides a default navigation menu for users who do not yet have custom Lightning apps. When customizing the navigation menu, the first four items in the navigation menu are pinned to the navigation bar at the bottom of the mobile screen for easy access. Remaining items appear in the menu list, accessible via the hamburger icon. Key takeaway: In the mobile app, the first four items of the navigation menu also appear in the bottom navigation bar. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is false. Only tabs (standard or custom) can be added to the navigation menu. Lightning pages or Visualforce pages must be exposed via a tab first. • Option B: Mobile Only app navigation is the same for all users. Profile-specific navigation customization is only available in Lightning apps. • Option D: False. Only selected items appear by default; not all standard objects are automatically included.

stem: At Cloud Kicks (CK), cases are being assigned a default Case Owner and showing a Created By and Last Modified By that is not expected. CK wants to change this to an integration user to alleviate confusion with the business. What should a Platform Administrator edit to change this in Salesforce?

options.text: Process Automation Settings
Debug Logs
Support Processes
Support Settings

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, Support Settings control default behaviors for cases, including the Default Case Owner: The user or queue that owns new cases if no other assignment rules apply. By changing the Default Case Owner in Support Settings to an integration user, new cases will show that user as the owner, and the Created By / Last Modified By fields will reflect the integration user, reducing confusion for the business. Key takeaway: Support Settings contain the Default Case Owner and the Automated Case User used for web-to-case, email-to-case and auto-response rules. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This section controls general automation features like workflow, process builder, and approval processes. It does not define default case ownership. • Option B: Debug logs are used for troubleshooting automation or code execution, not changing default ownership or system behavior. • Option C: Support Processes define which case stages are available and are not used to assign default ownership.

stem: A sales rep at Ursa Major Solar has launched a series of networking events. They are hosting one event per month and want to be able to report on Campaign ROI by month and series. How should a Platform Administrator set up the Campaign to simplify reporting?

options.text: Create individual Campaigns that all have the same name.
Configure Campaign Member Statuses to record which event Members attended.
Use Campaign Hierarchy where the monthly events roll up to a parent Campaign.
Add different record types for the monthly event types.

sourceExplanation: Campaign Hierarchies allow multiple related campaigns to be linked together under a parent campaign. For a series of monthly networking events, each monthly event can be a child campaign and the parent campaign represents the overall series. Salesforce automatically rolls up metrics such as member responses, costs, and revenue to the parent campaign. This setup simplifies reporting on ROI by month (child campaigns) and by series (parent campaign) without manual aggregation. Key takeaway: Campaign hierarchies roll up statistics (leads, contacts, opportunities, value won) from child campaigns to the parent. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Duplicate names do not establish relationships, so reporting on the series as a whole would be difficult. • Option B: This tracks attendance at individual events, but does not allow ROI roll-up or aggregation across multiple events. • Option D: Record types control page layouts and picklist values, not how campaigns are grouped or rolled up.

stem: A Platform Administrator needs to create a new prompt template to automatically summarize customer cases for a sales team. The administrator wants to dynamically populate the response with data from the case record. What should the administrator use to display real Salesforce data in an agent response from a prompt template?

options.text: Flow
Picklists
Agent Instructions
Merge Fields

sourceExplanation: Merge Fields allow prompt templates to dynamically pull data from Salesforce records (like Cases, Opportunities, or Accounts) and insert it directly into the response generated by an agent. For example, a case summary prompt template can use merge fields to include Case Number, Subject, Status, or Description in the AI-generated summary without manual input. Key takeaway: Merge fields in Prompt Builder ground the prompt with record data at run time, which personalizes the generated response. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Flows automate processes and can update records, but they do not directly populate prompt templates with dynamic record data. • Option B: Picklists are used for selecting values in fields, not for dynamically inserting record data into AI-generated responses. • Option C: Agent Instructions provide guidance to the agent but cannot dynamically pull Salesforce record data into a prompt template.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has set up a junior administrator as a delegated administrator in Salesforce. What should the Platform Administrator consider regarding delegated administrators?

options.text: Delegated administrators can unlock users but cannot reset passwords.
Delegated administrators can update field-level security on standard objects.
Delegated administrators cannot modify permission sets.
Delegated administrators cannot assign users to profiles.

sourceExplanation: Delegated administrators in Salesforce have limited administrative privileges within a specified role or subset of users. They can manage users, reset passwords, unlock users, and assign users to certain groups or roles, but they cannot modify permission sets—this includes creating, editing, or deleting permission sets—because permission sets define access across the org and are considered a system-level security setting. Key takeaway: Delegated administrators can manage users in specified roles, assign specified profiles and permission sets, and manage custom objects, but cannot create or modify permission sets. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: False. They can reset passwords and unlock users for users within their delegated scope. • Option B: False. They cannot modify field-level security on standard objects; that remains a system administrator function. • Option D: False. They can assign users to profiles that are within their delegated administration scope.

stem: Ursa Major Solar classifies its accounts as Silver, Gold, or Platinum Level. When a new case is created for a Silver or Gold partner, it should go to the Regular Support Queue. When an account is Platinum Level, it should automatically go to the Priority Support Queue. What should a Platform Administrator use to achieve this?

options.text: Escalation Rules
Assignment Rules
Case Rules
Workflow Rules

sourceExplanation: Case Assignment Rules in Salesforce automatically route cases to the correct user or queue when they are created. In this scenario, the administrator can create a rule that evaluates the Account Level (Silver, Gold, Platinum) when a new case is created. Cases for Silver or Gold accounts can be routed to the Regular Support Queue and cases for Platinum accounts can be routed to the Priority Support Queue. This ensures cases are automatically assigned to the appropriate support queue without manual intervention. Key takeaway: Case assignment rules route new cases based on criteria such as related account fields; escalation rules act later based on time. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Escalation rules only act after a case has been created and remains unresolved for a specified time. They cannot assign a case immediately at creation based on account level. • Option C: There is no standard Salesforce feature called "Case Rules." Case assignment logic is handled by Assignment Rules. • Option D: Workflow Rules can perform field updates or notifications but cannot assign a record to a queue automatically based on criteria.

stem: How should a Platform Administrator provide users with individualized views of data on a dashboard?

options.text: Add a Dashboard Filter to change the dashboard view.
Create a Dynamic Dashboard.
Set View Dashboard As to Me.
Set View Dashboard As to Another person.

sourceExplanation: A Dynamic Dashboard allows a single dashboard to display data tailored to the viewing user. Each user sees data as if they are the running user, without needing separate dashboards for every user. This is ideal for providing individualized views of accounts, opportunities, or cases on a shared dashboard. Key takeaway: Dynamic dashboards show each viewer their own data according to their security settings, avoiding one dashboard per user. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Filters let users manually adjust what is displayed, but they do not automatically personalize data per user. • Option C: This makes the dashboard static for all viewers, showing only the data the admin sees, not individualized views. • Option D: Similar to above, this makes the dashboard display data for a specific user, but it is not dynamic for multiple users.

stem: A sales rep has a list of 300 accounts with contacts that they want to load at one time. Which tool should a Platform Administrator utilize to import the records to Salesforce?

options.text: Dataloader.io
Manual Import
Data Import Wizard
Data Loader

sourceExplanation: The Data Import Wizard is ideal for importing up to 50,000 records at a time for standard objects like Accounts and Contacts. Since the sales rep has 300 accounts with contacts, the Data Import Wizard can efficiently handle this volume without requiring any installation and provides an easy-to-use interface for mapping fields and importing related records. Key takeaway: For fewer than 50,000 records of standard objects such as accounts and contacts, the Data Import Wizard is the simplest tool and can match duplicates. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: While Dataloader.io is a third-party tool capable of importing large volumes of data, it is not required for only 300 records, and the Data Import Wizard is simpler for smaller imports. • Option B: Manual entry is too time-consuming and error-prone for hundreds of records. • Option D: Data Loader is intended for very large data volumes (typically over 50,000 records) or when complex automation is required. For 300 records, it is overkill.

stem: Once an opportunity reaches the negotiation stage at Cloud Kicks, the Amount field becomes required for sales users. Sales managers need to be able to move opportunities into this stage without knowing the amount. How should a Platform Administrator require this field during the negotiation stage for sales users but allow their managers to make changes?

options.text: Make the field required for all users.
Assign the Administrator profile to the managers.
Configure a validation rule to meet the criteria.
Create a formula field to fill in the field for managers.

sourceExplanation: Validation rules allow a Platform Administrator to enforce field requirements conditionally. In this case, a validation rule can require the Amount field to be filled only when the Opportunity Stage is "Negotiation" AND the user is a sales rep. Managers can be excluded from the rule using a condition like NOT($Profile.Name = "Sales Manager"), allowing them to move opportunities without entering the amount. This approach provides flexible, profile-based enforcement. Key takeaway: Validation rule formulas can reference $Profile or $Permission to apply requirements only to certain users. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This would prevent managers from bypassing the requirement, which does not meet the business need. • Option B: Giving managers an Administrator profile is overkill and unnecessary, and it introduces security risks. • Option D: Formula fields are read-only and cannot populate required fields for validation purposes; this does not satisfy the requirement.

stem: Which Salesforce feature allows a Platform Administrator to automate the routing of records to specific users for review and decision-making based on predefined criteria?

options.text: Assignment Rules
Validation Rules
Approval Process
Schema Builder

sourceExplanation: An Approval Process in Salesforce automates the routing of records (like Opportunities, Cases, or custom objects) to specific users or groups for review and decision-making based on predefined criteria. It ensures that records follow a structured approval workflow, with options for automatic notifications, field updates, and final approvals or rejections. Key takeaway: Approval processes route records to approvers, lock them during review and perform actions on approval or rejection. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Assignment rules automatically assign records to users or queues, but they do not include a review and approval workflow. They are for routing ownership, not decision-making. • Option B: Validation rules enforce data quality by preventing records from being saved if criteria are not met. They do not route records or manage approvals. • Option D: Schema Builder is used for visualizing and editing objects, fields, and relationships, not for automating record routing or approvals.

stem: The Cloud Kicks sales team has asked that two of the fields that appear on the Opportunity cards in Kanban view be changed to make the cards more meaningful. Which feature should a Platform Administrator access to make this change?

options.text: Record Type
Compact Layout
Page Layout
Kanban Settings

sourceExplanation: Compact Layouts control which fields appear in record highlights and in Kanban cards. By modifying the compact layout for the Opportunity object, the administrator can select the two fields that will display on the Kanban view cards, making them more meaningful for the sales team. Key takeaway: Kanban card fields come from the object's compact layout (assigned compact layout). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Record types define different business processes, page layouts, and picklist values for a record, but they do not control which fields appear on Kanban cards. • Option C: Page layouts control field placement on the full record page, but not the fields displayed in Kanban cards or highlights. • Option D: Kanban settings allow administrators to choose which field determines the lanes (e.g., Stage or Status) and summarize values, but they do not allow changing the fields shown on the cards.

stem: Ursa Major Solar wants to assist users with a guided expense report process to simplify submissions, routing, and authorizations. Which two tools should a Platform Administrator use to build this solution?

options.text: Validation Rule
Quick Action
Flow Builder
Approval Process

sourceExplanation: To create a guided expense report process that handles submissions, routing, and authorizations: • Flow Builder: Can build a guided, step-by-step experience for users to submit expense reports. Flows can collect data, perform calculations, and route records automatically. • Approval Process: Automates the authorization and approval steps after submission. The expense report can be routed to managers for approval with automated notifications and final approval/rejection actions. Key takeaway: A screen flow provides the guided experience, and an approval process handles multi-step review; they are often combined. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Validation rules enforce data quality but do not guide users through processes or automate approvals. • Option B: Quick Actions are shortcuts to create or update records, but they do not provide a full guided experience or automated approval workflow.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Universal Containers needs an automated way to delete records based on field values. Which automated solution should the administrator use?

options.text: Flow Builder
Automation Studio
Mass Delete Records
Flow Orchestration

sourceExplanation: Flow Builder in Salesforce can be used to automate record deletions based on specific criteria. By creating a Scheduled Flow or Record-Triggered Flow, the administrator can define the conditions (field values) that determine which records should be deleted and have the flow perform the deletion automatically without manual intervention. Key takeaway: Scheduled flows can find records by criteria and delete them in bulk on a schedule. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This is part of Salesforce Marketing Cloud, not Salesforce CRM, and is used for marketing automation, not record deletion in the core CRM. • Option C: Mass Delete Records is manual, requires administrator intervention, and cannot be scheduled or automated. • Option D: Flow Orchestration is designed to manage multi-step, multi-user processes, not for automated record deletion.

stem: A sales manager at Cloud Kicks would like a dashboard to emphasize some important data and tell a more compelling data story to the sales reps. How should a Platform Administrator achieve this for the sales manager?

options.text: Use a Text Widget.
Assign a new Task to each rep.
Use the Highlights Panel.
Send out a mass email.

sourceExplanation: Text Widgets on a dashboard allow the administrator to add context, explanations, or emphasis directly on the dashboard. The sales manager can use text widgets to highlight key insights, provide instructions, or tell a more compelling data story alongside charts and metrics, making it easier for sales reps to understand and act on the data. Key takeaway: Dashboard text and image widgets add context and highlight key messages next to charts. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Tasks create actionable items but do not enhance the dashboard or communicate insights visually. • Option C: The Highlights Panel displays key field values on a record page, not on a dashboard. It does not help tell a story or emphasize dashboard data. • Option D: Emails can notify users but do not integrate with the dashboard to visually emphasize data or tell a story.

stem: Cloud Kicks has an administrator team that manages the org. The company has asked for a small subset of leadership users to have Modify All access, like the administrators have. How should the administrator team accomplish this?

options.text: Assign the standard Platform User profile to the leadership users and edit the permissions to Modify All access.
Assign the standard System Administrator profile to the leadership users that includes the Modify All access.
Assign the standard User profile to the leadership users and add a custom permission set with Modify All access.
Clone the standard User profile to the leadership users and assign a Modify All role to grant access.

sourceExplanation: To give a subset of users broad access without making them full administrators, a custom permission set can be created to grant "Modify All" permissions on specific objects. Assigning this permission set to leadership users gives them the necessary access while keeping them on a standard User profile, limiting other administrative permissions. This approach is declarative, secure, and scalable, unlike assigning full System Administrator profiles, which would grant unnecessary permissions. Key takeaway: Permission sets let you grant powerful permissions such as View All or Modify All to a subset of users without giving them the System Administrator profile. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Standard profiles cannot be edited, so you cannot add "Modify All" permissions to a Platform User profile. • Option B: This would grant full admin access, not just Modify All, which is more access than the business requested. • Option D: Roles control record-level access, not object-level "Modify All" permissions. Cloning a profile without properly adding permissions would not achieve the required Modify All access.

stem: Senior leadership wants to be notified of any opportunities over $250,000 with more than a 75% probability of closing. Which feature should a Platform Administrator set up to facilitate this?

options.text: Guidance for Success
Big Deal Alerts
Reports and Dashboards
Similar Opportunities

sourceExplanation: Big Deal Alerts are a Salesforce feature specifically designed to notify key stakeholders when opportunities meet certain criteria, such as amount and probability. By setting up a Big Deal Alert, senior leadership can receive real-time email notifications when opportunities exceed $250,000 and have a probability greater than 75%. Alerts can be targeted to specific users or groups without requiring manual monitoring. Key takeaway: Big Deal Alerts can notify recipients when an opportunity exceeds an amount and probability threshold; only one alert can be active per org. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This provides sales coaching and best practices in Salesforce but does not send alerts based on opportunity criteria. • Option C: Reports can track opportunities and dashboards can visualize them, but they do not automatically notify users when criteria are met unless combined with subscriptions, which is less direct than Big Deal Alerts. • Option D: This feature suggests opportunities similar to a given one to help sales reps, but it does not trigger notifications for leadership.

stem: Sales reps at Ursa Major Solar are having difficulty managing deals. The leadership team has asked a Platform Administrator to help sales reps prioritize and close more deals. What should the administrator configure to help with these issues?

options.text: Einstein Search Personalization
Einstein Lead Scoring
Einstein Opportunity Scoring
Einstein Activity Capture

sourceExplanation: Einstein Opportunity Scoring analyzes historical opportunity data and predicts the likelihood of closing a deal. It provides a score for each opportunity (high, medium, low) to help sales reps prioritize deals, insights into factors influencing the score, guiding reps on actions to improve their chances of closing, and focused recommendations that help increase win rates and accelerate sales cycles. Key takeaway: Einstein Opportunity Scoring gives a score and top factors that influence each deal, helping reps prioritize. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Improves search results for users, but it does not provide deal prioritization or scoring. • Option B: Scores leads, not opportunities, so it helps with lead qualification but does not guide opportunity management. • Option D: Automatically logs emails and events to Salesforce, which improves activity tracking but does not prioritize opportunities or provide scoring.

stem: Users at Cloud Kicks are reporting different options when updating a custom picklist on the Opportunity object based on the kind of opportunity. Where should a Platform Administrator update the option in the picklist?

options.text: Related lookup filters
Record type
Picklist value sets
Fields and relationships

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, custom picklist values can vary based on the record type assigned to a record. By updating the picklist values for a specific Opportunity record type, the administrator can ensure that users see only the relevant options for that kind of opportunity. This is the standard way to provide context-specific picklist choices on the same object. Key takeaway: Picklist values available to users are controlled per record type in Object Manager > Record Types > picklist value editing. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Lookup filters restrict which records can be selected in a lookup field, not which picklist values appear. • Option C: Value sets define a shared list of picklist values across multiple objects or fields, but they do not control record-type-specific values. • Option D: This is where you define the picklist field itself, but record-type-specific values are managed in the record type configuration, not at the field level.

stem: An administrator at DreamHouse Realty needs to create customized pages for the Salesforce mobile app. Which two types of pages should a Platform Administrator build and customize using the Lightning App Builder?

options.text: App page
User page
Record page
Dashboard page

sourceExplanation: Using Lightning App Builder, a Platform Administrator can create and customize pages for the Salesforce mobile app. The types of pages supported for mobile customization include: • App page: Provides a custom landing page for a mobile app, which can include multiple components and layout sections to guide users. • Record page: Customizes the layout of individual records (e.g., Account, Opportunity, Case) in the mobile app, allowing administrators to control which fields, related lists, and components appear to mobile users. Key takeaway: Lightning App Builder creates App pages, Home pages and Record pages; there is no "user page" or "dashboard page" type. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Salesforce does not support creating standalone "User pages" in Lightning App Builder for mobile. User records can be displayed on Record pages, but there's no separate user page type. • Option D: Dashboards are built using the Dashboard Builder, not Lightning App Builder, and cannot be directly created or customized as a Lightning page for mobile apps.

stem: Universal Containers (UC) has a private sharing model for Opportunities and uses Opportunity teams. Criteria-based sharing rules are not used. A sales rep at UC leaves the company, and their user record is deactivated. The rep is later rehired in the same role. A Platform Administrator activates the old user record. The user is added to the same default Opportunity teams but is no longer able to see the same records the user worked on before leaving the company. What is the likely cause?

options.text: The stage of the opportunity records was changed to Closed Lost.
The record type of the opportunity records was changed.
The records were manually shared with the user.
Permission sets were removed when the user was deactivated.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, when a user is deactivated, any manual sharing granted specifically to that user is removed. When the user is later reactivated, those manual shares are not automatically restored, even if the user is added back to default Opportunity teams. Default Opportunity teams only grant access to records that the user owns or new records created after activation, not to previously manually shared records. Since UC uses a private sharing model and no criteria-based sharing rules, manual shares were the original way the user gained access to other Opportunities. Once removed upon deactivation, access is lost. Key takeaway: Deactivating a user removes manual shares and team memberships; they are not restored when the user is reactivated. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Changing the stage does not revoke access. Access depends on ownership and sharing rules, not opportunity stage. • Option B: Record types affect page layouts and picklist values, not record visibility or access. • Option D: Permission sets control object- and field-level permissions, not record-level access. Removing them does not explain why previously shared records are no longer visible.

stem: Cloud Kicks uses the standard Account Type field to indicate different account tiers. Users find this confusing, so management has asked that the field be changed to read "Tier" on the page layouts. How should a Platform Administrator implement this change?

options.text: Edit the Type field and change the name.
Use Rename Tabs and Labels.
Build a custom field called Tier and delete Type.
Create a global picklist value set.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce allows administrators to change the display label of standard fields without altering the underlying field or data. Using Rename Tabs and Labels, the administrator can change the Account Type field label to "Tier" on page layouts, reports, and other UI elements, maintain all existing data, picklist values, and functionality associated with the standard field, and make the change quickly and declaratively without creating a new field or migrating data. Key takeaway: Rename Tabs and Labels changes the label of standard fields and tabs everywhere without changing the API name. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Standard fields cannot have their API names changed. Only the label can be renamed, which is done through Rename Tabs and Labels. • Option C: This approach would require data migration and updating all references to the old field. It's unnecessary when only the label needs to change. • Option D: Picklist value sets manage the values within a picklist, not the field label itself.

stem: A Platform Administrator is building an agent to nurture leads. How does Agentforce SDR help?

options.text: Generate a dynamic call script and talking points for the human sales reps to use.
Autonomously negotiate pricing with the lead and close the final deal.
Analyze the performance of human sales reps and provide coaching tips.
Answer the lead's questions with responses that are grounded in company data.

sourceExplanation: Agentforce SDR is designed to act as a conversational AI assistant for sales development. Its main capability is to interact with leads and provide answers based on trusted company data, helping nurture leads efficiently without the human rep having to manually research each response. This ensures responses are accurate and aligned with company policies or data, leads receive timely answers, improving engagement, and sales reps can focus on higher-value tasks while the agent handles data-driven interactions. Key takeaway: Agentforce SDR engages inbound leads autonomously, answering questions grounded in CRM data and booking meetings for human reps. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This describes guidance tools for reps, not the AI's primary role in interacting with leads autonomously. • Option B: Agentforce SDR does not handle deal closing or pricing negotiations. • Option C: Performance coaching is not a feature of Agentforce SDR; it focuses on lead interaction.

stem: Universal Containers' Platform Administrator has been asked to create a many-to-many relationship between two existing custom objects. Which two steps should the administrator take when enabling the many-to-many relationship?

options.text: Create a junction with a custom object.
Create two master-detail relationships on the new object.
Create URL fields on a custom object.
Create two lookup relationships on the new object.

sourceExplanation: To create a many-to-many relationship in Salesforce between two custom objects, a junction object is required. The steps are: • Create a junction object (custom object) – This object acts as the intermediary that connects the two existing objects. • Create two master-detail relationships on the junction object – Each master-detail relationship links the junction object to one of the two objects being connected. This enables many-to-many functionality, as each record in one object can relate to multiple records in the other through the junction object. Key takeaway: A junction object with two master-detail relationships creates a many-to-many relationship; the first master-detail created becomes the primary. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: URL fields are used for links, not for establishing relationships between objects. • Option D: Lookup relationships allow one-to-many relationships, but they do not enforce a true many-to-many relationship the way master-detail relationships on a junction object do.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Universal Containers has a screen flow that helps users create new leads. When Lead Source is "Search Engine", the administrator needs to require the user to choose a specific search engine from a picklist. If Lead Source is not "Search Engine", this picklist should be hidden. What is the most efficient way for the administrator to complete this requirement?

options.text: Use a conditional filter in the screen element to only show the Specific Search Engine field only when Lead Source is "Search Engine".
Use Assignment elements; one for when Lead Source is "Search Engine" and one for everything else.
Create a picklist for Specific Search Engine, and set conditional visibility so that it is only shown when Lead Source is "Search Engine".
Configure a picklist for Specific Search Engine, and use a validation rule to conditionally show only when Lead Source is "Search Engine".

sourceExplanation: In Screen Flows, you can make fields appear dynamically using conditional visibility: • Create the Specific Search Engine picklist. • On the screen element, set conditional visibility so the picklist is only displayed when Lead Source equals "Search Engine". • You can also make the field required only when it is visible, which satisfies the requirement efficiently. This approach is declarative, simple, and avoids unnecessary branching, making it the most efficient solution. Key takeaway: Conditional visibility on screen components shows or hides fields based on other inputs without extra screens or decision elements. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is similar in concept, but in Flow, conditional visibility is the standard, supported way to control field display; "conditional filter" isn't a Flow feature. • Option B: Using assignments would require multiple screens or branches, which is unnecessarily complex compared to conditional visibility. • Option D: Validation rules cannot control visibility in a Flow; they only enforce data correctness after submission.

stem: The Activity Timeline is missing from the Account record page. What should a Platform Administrator do to correct this?

options.text: Add the standard Activities component to the Account Lightning record page.
Update the user's permission to allow Edit access to the Activity Timeline.
Run a report to verify whether any activities have been logged for that Account.
Add a button for the Activity Timeline in the Object Manager for the Account object.

sourceExplanation: In Lightning Experience, the Activity Timeline appears through the standard Activities component on the record page. If it's missing, the Platform Administrator should open the Account record page in Lightning App Builder, add the standard Activities component to the page layout and activate/save the page. Once added, users will see the Activity Timeline for Tasks, Events, and Emails on the Account. Key takeaway: The Activities component (Activity Timeline) is added to Lightning record pages with Lightning App Builder. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: There is no separate permission specifically for showing the Activity Timeline; visibility depends on the page layout component and object access. • Option C: This only checks existing data, but it does not make the timeline appear on the page. • Option D: Activity Timeline is not a button; it is a page component, so adding a button will not display it.

stem: A Platform Administrator wants to limit the kinds of reports their users can create. Which tool should the administrator use?

options.text: Hide Report Types
Report Folder Sharing
Standard Report Types
Joined Report

sourceExplanation: The Hide Report Types feature allows a Platform Administrator to control which report types are available to users when creating reports. By hiding specific report types, users are restricted to only the report types the admin allows. This ensures consistency, prevents errors, and aligns reporting with business requirements. Key takeaway: Hiding report types in the report type selector limits what users can build without deleting the report types. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Controls who can view or edit reports in specific folders, but does not limit which report types users can create. • Option C: Standard report types are predefined by Salesforce. Admins can't prevent users from seeing them individually; they would need to use Hide Report Types to limit access. • Option D: Joined reports are a report format, not a tool to restrict report creation. Users can still access allowed report types to create joined reports.

stem: Agentforce is escalating cases to the support team, but the support team complains they have no context and have to ask the customer to repeat everything. Which configuration issue is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The support team members are missing the Agentforce User permission set.
The support team's case page layout is missing the agent history component.
The agent's instructions are preventing the history and context from being saved.
The handoff is creating a new case instead of transferring the existing session.

sourceExplanation: When Agentforce escalates a case, the existing conversation context and history must be transferred along with the case. If the handoff is configured to create a new case instead of transferring the current session, the support team will not see the previous messages or context, forcing them to ask the customer to repeat information. Key takeaway: A proper escalation transfers the existing messaging session and transcript to the human agent so context is preserved. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Missing permissions may prevent access to Agentforce features, but it does not cause the loss of conversation context during handoff. • Option B: While adding the history component improves visibility, the primary issue is that a new case is created, so there is no history to display at all. • Option C: Instructions guide the agent's behavior but do not control session persistence or case handoff.

stem: A Platform Administrator creates a custom text area field on the Account object and adds it to the service team's page layout. The service team manager loves the addition of this field and wants it to appear in the highlights panel so that the service reps can quickly find it when on the Account page. How should the administrator accomplish this?

options.text: In the Account object manager, create a custom compact layout.
Make the field required and move it to the top of the page.
Create a new page layout and a new section titled highlights panel.
From the page layout editor, drag the field to the highlights panel.

sourceExplanation: The Highlights Panel in Lightning Experience displays fields based on the compact layout, not the standard page layout. To make the new custom text area field appear there: • Go to Account → Object Manager → Compact Layouts. • Create a new compact layout (or edit an existing one). • Add the custom text area field to the layout. • Assign the compact layout to the profiles of the service team so it appears in their Highlights Panel. Key takeaway: The highlights panel shows the first fields of the compact layout; create a custom compact layout and assign it as primary. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Changing field order on the page layout affects the record page but does not impact the Highlights Panel, which uses the compact layout. • Option C: Highlights Panel is not a page layout section. It automatically shows fields from the compact layout. • Option D: You cannot drag fields into the Highlights Panel from the page layout editor; it is controlled solely by the compact layout.

stem: A Platform Administrator for Cloud Kicks has created a screen flow to help service reps ask the same set of questions when customers call in with issues. This screen should be visible from cases. How should the administrator distribute the screen flow?

options.text: Page Layout
Home Page
Lightning Page
Component Filter

sourceExplanation: To make a screen flow available on a record page, such as a Case, the administrator should: • Open Lightning App Builder for the Case Lightning Page. • Add a Flow component to the page. • Select the screen flow to display. This ensures that when service reps open a Case, they can access the flow directly on the record page for a guided, consistent process. Key takeaway: Screen flows are surfaced on record pages with the Flow component in Lightning App Builder and can receive the record Id as input. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Page layouts control fields and sections on the record page but cannot embed screen flows. • Option B: Adding a flow to the Home Page makes it globally accessible, but it would not appear directly on the Case record. • Option D: Component filters control visibility of components on a Lightning Page but do not distribute the flow themselves.

stem: Ursa Major Solar's Platform Administrator is editing the page layout for a new custom object. A text area field is accidentally removed from the page layout, and it needs to be restored to the page layout. What are two methods for achieving this goal?

options.text: Clone the layout from a different profile and use save as.
Restore original page layout from a sandbox.
Restore from the recycle bin within 15 days.
From the fields palette, drag the field into the same position.

sourceExplanation: • Restore original page layout from a sandbox: If the page layout in the sandbox still contains the field, the administrator can recreate or copy the layout from the sandbox into production. This method restores the original layout configuration, including the missing field. • From the fields palette, drag the field into the same position: In the page layout editor, the field can be dragged back from the fields palette into the section it was removed from. This is the simplest method if the administrator remembers where the field should go. Key takeaway: Removed fields are never deleted from the object; they stay in the page layout palette and can be dragged back. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This could work if another profile has the correct layout, but it is not guaranteed to restore the exact original layout for the profile in question. • Option C: The Recycle Bin stores deleted records, not removed fields from page layouts, so it cannot recover a missing field.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks would like to use Salesforce to start tracking details around its marketing efforts. They would like to track details around emails, trade shows, and webinars. Additionally, each of these initiatives will need to track different types of information. How should the administrator accomplish this?

options.text: Create a custom report type with relevant fields.
Create a custom field on the Campaign object for the type of initiative.
Create record types and page layouts for each type of campaign.
Use campaign hierarchies to organize campaign types.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce Campaigns can represent different marketing initiatives (emails, trade shows, webinars), and each type may need different fields and layouts. By creating record types for each campaign type, you can define unique page layouts for each type to capture the information specific to that initiative, and users see only the relevant fields when creating or editing a campaign. This approach provides flexibility and structure for diverse marketing activities while keeping all campaigns in a single object. Key takeaway: Record types on Campaign let each campaign type use its own layout and picklist values. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This allows for reporting on campaigns, but it does not control how fields are captured or displayed for different campaign types. • Option B: A single field can indicate the campaign type, but all fields remain on the same layout, making it cumbersome to track different details for different initiatives. • Option D: Campaign hierarchies organize related campaigns, but they do not provide different fields or layouts for different types of campaigns.

stem: A Platform Administrator created a new prompt template and is testing it. Every time the administrator tests the template, it gives a different response. Why is the prompt template giving different responses each time it's run?

options.text: Prompt Builder caches the large language model's response, so the prompt is only sent once for every template the administrator creates.
Every time the administrator runs a prompt template in Prompt Builder, it creates a unique call to the large language model.
The prompt is only sent to the large language model after the administrator deploys the template to a live agent, not when the prompt is run in the builder.
Prompt Builder runs a simulated call to the large language model to save on costs, so the prompt is never sent to the actual model.

sourceExplanation: Prompt Builder interacts with a large language model (LLM), which is inherently probabilistic. Each time a prompt is executed, a new request is sent to the model, generating a response based on the prompt and context. Because LLMs can produce different outputs even for the same prompt, the responses may vary each time. This variability is expected behavior and allows for dynamic, natural-sounding responses. Key takeaway: Large language models are non-deterministic; each run is a new request, so responses vary slightly even with the same prompt. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: There is no caching of responses in Prompt Builder; each execution sends a fresh request to the model. • Option C: Prompt Builder runs actual calls to the model during testing, so deployment is not required for responses. • Option D: Prompt Builder does not simulate responses; it uses the real LLM, which is why responses can differ.

stem: Management at Universal Containers would like to share dashboard components with their team in Chatter but currently does not have access to this capability. How should a Platform Administrator make this functionality available to management?

options.text: Enable reporting snapshots.
Select Download Chart on the component.
Set View Dashboard As to the dashboard viewer.
Enable dashboard feed tracking.

sourceExplanation: Dashboard feed tracking allows users to share dashboard components directly in Chatter. By enabling this feature, management can post specific components from dashboards to Chatter groups or users, team members can see visual data updates and collaborate without needing full dashboard access, and it makes sharing quick and contextual, improving visibility of key metrics. Key takeaway: Feed tracking on dashboards enables users to post dashboard component snapshots to Chatter. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Reporting snapshots capture data at specific points in time but do not allow sharing dashboard components in Chatter. • Option B: Downloading a chart allows a static file download, not live sharing in Chatter. • Option C: This controls whose data is displayed on the dashboard but does not enable Chatter sharing.

stem: Sales reps miss key fields when filling out an opportunity record through the sales process. Reps need to move forward in stages but are unable to enter a previous stage. Which three options should a Platform Administrator use to address this need?

options.text: Mark fields required on the page layout.
Use Flow to mark fields required.
Configure Opportunity Path.
Use validation rules.
Enable guided selling.

sourceExplanation: • Mark fields required on the page layout: Ensures that key fields cannot be left blank when users are entering or editing opportunities. This prevents missing data without restricting the sales process unnecessarily. • Configure Opportunity Path: Opportunity Path can highlight key fields and guidance for each stage. It helps sales reps know what fields to complete before moving to the next stage. • Use validation rules: Validation rules enforce business-specific requirements for fields based on stage or other criteria. They allow admins to require fields only in certain stages or under certain conditions, providing more flexibility than page layout-required fields. Key takeaway: Path displays key fields and guidance per stage, while required fields and validation rules enforce data entry. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Flows can enforce required fields, but this is more complex than using page layouts or validation rules for standard opportunity entry. • Option E: Guided selling is a premium feature in Salesforce CPQ and is not standard for enforcing field completion in the opportunity sales process.

stem: What is an Agentforce use case in a sales organization?

options.text: Generating cold calls
Automating all marketing content
Providing basic web bot chats
Automating Lead Qualification

sourceExplanation: Agentforce in a sales organization is designed to help sales development and qualification processes. It can interact with leads using AI-driven conversations, ask qualifying questions and gather lead information, and route qualified leads to human sales reps for follow-up. This helps the sales team focus on high-value leads rather than spending time on initial qualification. Key takeaway: Lead qualification (answering questions, qualifying, scheduling meetings) is a core Agentforce sales use case. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Agentforce does not make calls autonomously; it assists reps with lead qualification and conversation guidance. • Option B: Marketing content creation is outside the scope of Agentforce, which is focused on sales interactions. • Option C: While Agentforce can chat with leads, it is not limited to basic web bots; its primary use case is lead qualification.

stem: Cloud Kicks needs to be able to show different picklist values for sales and marketing users. Which two options meet this requirement?

options.text: Two permission sets, one record type, one picklist
One record type, two profiles, one picklist
One page layout, two record types, one picklist
Two page layouts, one record type, two picklists

sourceExplanation: To show different picklist values for different user groups (sales vs. marketing) in Salesforce, you can control picklist values by record type. • Option C: Using one page layout, two record types, and one picklist allows you to assign different picklist values to each record type. Then, assign each record type to the appropriate user profile (sales or marketing). • Option D: Using two page layouts, one record type, and two picklists means you can create two separate picklist fields (e.g., "Sales Picklist" and "Marketing Picklist") and assign them to different page layouts.
