You can then assign each page layout to a different profile via the record type (if using the same record type, you would need to control page layout assignment by profile, which is possible but less common than using separate record types). Key takeaway: Picklist values can differ by record type (one picklist, multiple record types) or by using different fields displayed on different layouts. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Two permission sets and one record type with one picklist will not create different picklist values for different users; permission sets cannot control record-type-specific picklist values. • Option B: One record type, two profiles, and one picklist will show the same picklist values for all users assigned to that record type, regardless of profile. Profiles do not control picklist values—record types do.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has a flow in production that is supposed to create new records. However, no new records are being created. What is causing the issue?

options.text: The flow is inactive.
The flow URL is deactivated.
The flow is Read Only.
The flow trigger is missing.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, flows must be active in order to run in production. If a flow is inactive, it cannot execute, and any actions it is supposed to perform—such as creating records—will not occur. Activating the flow ensures that it responds to triggers or user actions as designed. Key takeaway: Only active flow versions run; after saving a new version, always activate it. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Flows are not run via URLs in standard production use unless it's a screen flow launched from a URL, which is rare. This would not affect record-creating flows triggered by automation. • Option C: A read-only flow would not be able to update or create records, but standard record-triggered flows that are configured to create records are not read-only by default. • Option D: If the flow is properly activated, missing triggers would prevent execution, but the most common reason in this scenario is that the flow is simply inactive.

stem: A sales manager receives a URL to a Dashboard folder containing several dashboards. However, when the sales manager clicks on the URL, a message appears stating, "We couldn't find the record you're trying to access." What is the reason for this?

options.text: The sales manager does not have the correct permission set.
The sales manager needs the correct sales user profile.
The Dashboard folder is set to Private.
View access has not been granted to the Dashboard folder.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, dashboards are stored in folders, and access to the folder controls who can see the dashboards inside it. If a user receives a URL but sees the message "We couldn't find the record you're trying to access", it typically means the dashboard folder is private or restricted, and the user does not have view or edit access. Granting View access to the folder for the sales manager (via folder sharing) resolves the issue. Key takeaway: Folder sharing controls access to dashboards; a user without at least View access on the folder cannot open its dashboards. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Folder access is controlled by sharing settings, not permission sets. • Option B: Profiles do not control dashboard folder access; any profile can access a folder if it's shared with them. • Option C: While this is true if the folder is private, the more precise reason is that the sales manager has not been granted access. Private folders must be explicitly shared to allow viewing.

stem: A Platform Administrator needs to configure an approval process for the sales team when opportunities that meet particular conditions are closed. How should the administrator make sure the right records are included in the process?

options.text: Add Specific Entry Criteria.
Use Dynamic Forms to display a button.
Create a screen flow.
Add a validation rule to the opportunity.

sourceExplanation: When configuring an approval process in Salesforce, entry criteria determine which records are eligible for approval. By setting Specific Entry Criteria, the administrator can specify conditions such as Opportunity Stage = Closed or Amount > X. Only records that meet these conditions will be submitted into the approval process, ensuring the right opportunities are routed for review. Key takeaway: Approval process entry criteria define which records can be submitted, preventing unqualified records from entering the process. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Dynamic Forms control field and section visibility on a page layout, not which records enter an approval process. • Option C: Flows can automate submissions but do not replace the entry criteria that define which records are eligible for an approval process. • Option D: Validation rules enforce data integrity, but they cannot control which records are submitted for approval.

stem: A Platform Administrator has reviewed an upcoming critical update. How should the administrator proceed with activation of the critical update?

options.text: Allow the critical update to auto-activate in a sandbox.
Activate the critical update in production.
Activate the critical update in a sandbox.
Allow the critical update to auto-activate.

sourceExplanation: When a Salesforce critical update is announced, best practice is to test the update in a sandbox first. This allows the administrator to evaluate the impact on existing processes, customizations, and integrations. Any issues can be resolved before affecting production users. Once confirmed that there are no negative impacts, the update can safely be activated in the production environment. Key takeaway: Always test critical updates (release updates) in a sandbox before activating them in production. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Critical updates do not auto-activate; they must be manually activated to test. • Option B: Activating directly in production without testing risks breaking existing functionality. • Option D: Some critical updates auto-activate after a Salesforce-specified date, but administrators should proactively test in a sandbox rather than relying solely on auto-activation.

stem: A Platform Administrator assigned a custom profile based on the Minimum Access named Salesforce profile to a group of new users and assigned them several existing permission sets. However, when the users log in, they do not see the Lightning interface. Which action should the administrator take to give the users access to the Lightning interface?

options.text: Enable the Enhanced Interface for User Access Policies.
Add Lightning component to a layout.
Create a page in Lightning App Builder with the org as default.
Assign a permission to enable Lightning Experience User.

sourceExplanation: Access to Lightning Experience is controlled by the "Lightning Experience User" permission. Even if users have a custom profile and multiple permission sets, without this permission, they will not see the Lightning interface. The administrator can grant this permission by editing the profile and enabling Lightning Experience User, or creating or assigning a permission set that includes the Lightning Experience User permission. Key takeaway: The "Lightning Experience User" permission is required for users to access Lightning Experience. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is not a real Salesforce setting; it does not control Lightning access. • Option B: Adding a component affects specific pages, not the overall interface access for users. • Option C: Creating a Lightning page does not grant users access to the Lightning Experience itself.

stem: The VP of sales at Cloud Kicks has a standard sales profile and is receiving an error message that prevents them from saving an opportunity. A Platform Administrator attempted the same edit without receiving an error. How should the administrator troubleshoot this issue?

options.text: Log in as a system administrator to troubleshoot.
Use 'Login as' to log in as the user.
Use an AppExchange product to troubleshoot.
Ask the user for their password so the admin can log in as the user.

sourceExplanation: The "Login as" feature allows a Platform Administrator to impersonate the user without needing their password. This lets the admin see exactly what the user sees, including any permission or field-level restrictions. It helps identify why the VP of Sales is receiving an error that does not appear for the admin. Common issues could include field-level security, page layout restrictions, validation rules, or required fields. Key takeaway: Login-As lets an administrator reproduce a user's issue with their exact permissions; users may need to grant access if administrators cannot log in as any user. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Logging in as yourself does not replicate the user's profile and permissions, so you won't see the same error. • Option C: While some apps provide auditing or logging, the quickest and most direct method is Login as. • Option D: This is against Salesforce security best practices and not necessary because "Login as" exists.

stem: A Platform Administrator is creating a new action instruction for an agent. This action, named createCase, is designed to generate a new Salesforce Case record based on the user's conversation with the agent. Which set of Action Instructions should the administrator use for the createCase action, according to best practices for action instructions?

options.text: "This action provides the ability to create a new case record in the Salesforce system. Its function is to simply save customer information as a record. Use this when the user wants to create a case."

"Use this action to create a new Salesforce Case record. The goal is to document a customer's issue in the system. Use this when the user's intent is to create a formal record of their problem or question."
"Creates a new case record in the system for any type of customer inquiry. The purpose of this is to ensure a record of the interaction is saved."
"The createCase code snippet is configured to create a case. It runs in the background to handle the user's request to log a new issue. Its purpose is to solve the customer's issue."

sourceExplanation: Best practices for Agentforce Action Instructions emphasize that instructions should be clear and concise, goal-oriented, user-focused, and free of technical jargon. The correct option clearly states what the action does (creates a Salesforce Case record), explains the purpose (to document a customer's issue formally), and tells when to use the action (when the user intends to create a formal record of their problem or question). Key takeaway: Good action instructions say what the action does, its goal, and when to use it, in plain language. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Too generic; lacks context about why or when the action should be used. • Option C: Too broad; does not clearly explain when this action is appropriate for the agent. • Option D: Includes technical implementation details, which should be avoided in action instructions intended for agent guidance.

stem: Cloud Kicks has a custom object called Shipments. The company wants to see all the shipment items from an Account page. When an Account is deleted, the shipments should remain. Which type of relationship should a Platform Administrator make between Shipments and Accounts?

options.text: Accounts should have a lookup to Shipments.
Shipments should have a master detail to Accounts.
Shipments should have a lookup to Account.
Accounts should have a master detail to Shipments.

sourceExplanation: A lookup relationship is appropriate when the child record (Shipment) can exist independently of the parent (Account). When an Account is deleted, the Shipments should remain, which is a key requirement in this scenario. Lookup relationships allow flexible associations without enforcing cascading deletions. Key takeaway: Lookup relationships keep child records when the parent is deleted; master-detail deletes children with the parent. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Lookup relationships are typically created on the child object, not the parent, to reference the parent. • Option B: Master-detail relationships cascade deletion by default. If the Account is deleted, the Shipment records would also be deleted, which does not meet the requirement. • Option D: You cannot create a master-detail on the parent to a child object. Master-detail is always defined on the child object.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters uses a custom Invoice object to collect customer payment information from an external billing system. The Billing System field needs to be filled in on every Invoice record. How should a Platform Administrator ensure this requirement?

options.text: Create a flow to update the field.
Require the field on the record type.
Define an approval process for the field.
Make the field universally required.

sourceExplanation: Making the field universally required (the "Required" checkbox on the field definition in Object Manager) enforces the requirement everywhere records are saved: the user interface, the API, Data Loader and integrations. Because Invoice records come from an external billing system through an integration, only a field-level (universal) requirement guarantees the Billing System value is always populated. Key takeaway: Universal requirement is enforced for UI, API and imports; page layout requirement applies only to the user interface. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A flow could set a value, but it cannot guarantee a correct Billing System value is supplied by the integration; it does not enforce the requirement. • Option B: Record types do not have a "required" setting; requiring a field on a page layout only applies to the UI, not to API/integration loads. • Option C: Approval processes route records for sign-off; they do not enforce that a field is populated.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Universal Containers is asked to restrict login access for users to specific hours and specific IP addresses to help minimize the risk of bad actors getting into the org. Which setting should the administrator update to accomplish this?

options.text: The user's profile
The user's role
Company Settings
Custom permission sets

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, login access restrictions—such as allowed login hours and allowed IP ranges—are configured at the profile level. Login Hours restrict the times during which users can log in, and IP Range restricts the IP addresses from which users can access Salesforce. Applying these settings to a profile ensures all users with that profile are subject to the same restrictions, helping improve security. Key takeaway: Login hours and login IP ranges are profile settings (IP ranges can also be enforced on every request). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Roles control record-level access, not login access. • Option C: Company Settings (like company-wide defaults) affect organization-wide configurations but cannot restrict individual users' login hours or IPs. • Option D: Permission sets grant additional permissions but cannot enforce login hours or IP restrictions.

stem: A group of sales reps can view each other's orders on a report; however, they would like a report to view just their own orders. What should a Platform Administrator do to set up a report for the sales reps?

options.text: Filter by Opportunity Owner equals $USER.
Save the report in a private folder for the user.
Set Organization Wide Defaults of Order object to Private.
Set the Opportunity Filter for Primary as True.

sourceExplanation: Using a report filter with Owner = $USER dynamically limits the report results so that each sales rep only sees records they own. When each rep runs the same report, Salesforce automatically substitutes $USER with the current logged-in user, showing only their own orders. Key takeaway: $USER-style dynamic filters ("My opportunities"/Owner = current user) let one shared report show personalized results. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This controls who can access the report, not which records appear in the report. • Option C: This changes overall record visibility across the org and is unnecessary (and potentially disruptive) just to control report output. • Option D: This has no impact on restricting orders to the current user.

stem: A Platform Administrator has been asked to change the data type of an auto number to a text field. What should the administrator be aware of before changing the field?

options.text: Existing field values will be deleted.
Existing Auto Number field to Text is prevented.
Existing field values will remain unchanged.
Existing field values will be converted.

sourceExplanation: When Salesforce allows a field type change (in supported scenarios), existing data is preserved and remains the same after the change. Salesforce does not delete or automatically modify existing values unless explicitly required by the new data type. The key concept tested here is data preservation awareness. Key takeaway: Converting an Auto Number field to Text keeps existing values; converting Text back to Auto Number generates new numbers. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Salesforce does not delete data automatically during a field type change. • Option B: While Auto Number fields have limitations, this option is misleading for this question and not the expected exam answer. • Option D: Salesforce does not "convert" Auto Number values into new formats; values stay as-is.

stem: DreamHouse Realty has an approval process. A manager attempts to approve a record but receives an error. What should a Platform Administrator do to troubleshoot this issue?

options.text: Add a delegated approver for the next approver in the process.
Review the page layout to ensure the fields updated in the process are visible.
Check if the user in the next approver is inactive or missing.
Update the field-level security to view on fields that are updated in the process.

sourceExplanation: Approval processes depend on valid, active users at every approval step. If the next approver is inactive, deleted, or not properly defined, Salesforce throws an error when a manager tries to approve the record. One of the first troubleshooting steps for approval errors is to verify the next approver exists and is active. Key takeaway: Approval errors often come from inactive or missing approvers; keep approvers active or use queues and delegated approvers. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Delegated approvers are optional and do not resolve errors caused by inactive or missing users. • Option B: Page layout visibility does not affect approval process execution. • Option D: Approval processes run in system context; field-level security does not block them.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants users to only be able to choose the opportunity stage Closed Won if the Lead source has been selected. How should a Platform Administrator accomplish this goal?

options.text: Configure a validation rule requiring Lead source when the stage is set to Closed Won.
Make Lead source a dependent picklist to the Opportunity Stage field.
Change the Opportunity Stage field to Read Only on the page layout.
Make the opportunity stage a dependent picklist to the Lead source.

sourceExplanation: A validation rule can enforce conditional logic at save time. By configuring a rule such as Stage = Closed Won AND Lead Source is blank, Salesforce will prevent users from saving the record unless Lead Source is populated when the opportunity is moved to Closed Won. This directly matches the requirement. Key takeaway: Validation rules express "if X then Y must be filled" conditions; dependent picklists only filter available values. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Dependent picklists control available values, not whether a field must be filled in. • Option C: This would block users from changing the stage entirely, not enforce Lead Source completion. • Option D: This reverses the dependency and still doesn't enforce the requirement that Lead Source must be selected.

stem: A sales rep has left the company, and a Platform Administrator has been asked to re-assign all their accounts and opportunities to a new sales rep and keep the teams as is. Which tool should the administrator use to accomplish this?

options.text: Mass Transfer Records
Data Loader
Data Import Wizard
Dataloader.io

sourceExplanation: The Mass Transfer Records tool is designed specifically for this scenario. It allows a Platform Administrator to reassign ownership of Accounts and Opportunities from one user to another while keeping existing account and opportunity team members intact. It's fast, admin-friendly, and does not require exporting or importing data. Key takeaway: Mass Transfer Records changes ownership of accounts (and related opportunities, cases, contacts) while keeping team settings when chosen. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: While it can update record owners, it does not preserve account and opportunity teams by default and requires CSV handling. • Option C: This tool is for importing new records or basic updates, not for mass ownership reassignment with team preservation. • Option D: Similar to Data Loader, it requires external processing and does not inherently maintain teams.

stem: Universal Containers requires that when an opportunity is closed won, all other open opportunities on the same account must be marked as Closed Lost. Which automation solution should a Platform Administrator use to implement this request?

options.text: Flow Builder
Quick Action
Flow Orchestration
Outbound Message

sourceExplanation: Flow Builder (specifically a record-triggered flow) is the best tool to handle this requirement. When an Opportunity is updated to Closed Won, the flow can automatically find all other open Opportunities on the same Account and update them to Closed Lost. This type of cross-record, conditional update is exactly what Flow Builder is designed for. Key takeaway: Record-triggered flows can update other records on the same account (Get Records + Loop + Update). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Requires a user to manually trigger it; the requirement needs automatic enforcement. • Option C: Used for multi-step, human-centric business processes, not simple data updates. • Option D: Sends data to an external system and cannot update Salesforce records.

stem: Cloud Kicks is working on a rebrand. In which two areas of the Salesforce mobile app can a Platform Administrator customize the branding?

options.text: Header background color
Loading page logo
Popups header color
Record background color

sourceExplanation: In the Salesforce mobile app, a Platform Administrator can apply branding through Mobile App Branding settings. These allow customization of: • Header background color, which appears across the mobile app UI. • Loading page logo, which displays when the app launches. These options support company rebranding and provide a consistent visual identity in the mobile experience. Key takeaway: Mobile branding allows the brand color, loading page background color and loading page logo. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Salesforce does not provide a setting to brand popup headers in the mobile app. • Option D: Record page backgrounds are not configurable for branding purposes.

stem: Which task is especially suited for Agentforce?

options.text: Multi-step processes that need adaption to change
Static document generation
Single-step predefined processes
Tasks without decision-making

sourceExplanation: Agentforce is designed for dynamic, intelligent automation that can reason, adapt, and make decisions across multiple steps. It excels in scenarios where the process flow may change based on context, inputs, or outcomes—something rigid automation tools struggle with. Key takeaway: Agentforce excels at multi-step tasks requiring reasoning and adaptation; simple fixed tasks are better handled by flows. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This is better handled by templates or document automation tools. • Option C: These are more efficiently handled by simple automation like flows or actions. • Option D: Agentforce's value comes from decision-making and adaptability, which aren't needed here.

stem: A Platform Administrator is designing a prompt template for a new agent. The agent's purpose is to help service reps troubleshoot technical issues by providing concise, step-by-step instructions. Based on best practices for creating effective prompts, which approach should the administrator use when writing this prompt?

options.text: Write a detailed prompt with multiple nested conditions to cover all the major troubleshooting scenarios.
Use natural, easy-to-understand language and clear, concise instructions to guide the AI's behavior.
Use specific technical terms and abbreviations to ensure the AI understands the specialized domain.
Focus on providing high-level, theoretical concepts so the AI has the flexibility to respond creatively.

sourceExplanation: When designing prompts for AI agents, clarity and simplicity are key. Using natural language and step-by-step instructions helps the AI understand the task and produce actionable, accurate responses. For troubleshooting, concise guidance ensures service reps can follow instructions without confusion. Key takeaway: Prompts should be clear and concise, in natural language, describing the task, tone and expected output. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Overly complex prompts can confuse the AI and reduce response quality; simplicity is preferred. • Option C: While domain knowledge is important, excessive jargon can reduce clarity for both the AI and end-users. • Option D: This is too abstract for troubleshooting tasks; the AI needs actionable, practical steps rather than creative interpretations.

stem: What are three characteristics of a master-detail relationship?

options.text: The master object can be a standard or custom object.
Each object can have up to five master-detail relationships.
Permissions for the detail record are set independently of the master.
The owner field on the detail records is the owner of the master record.
Roll-up summaries are supported in master-detail relationships.

sourceExplanation: • Master can be standard or custom: the master (parent) object in a master-detail relationship can be a standard object such as Account or a custom object. • Detail ownership follows the master: detail records have no owner of their own; the Owner field is inherited from the master record, and sharing/security is controlled by the master. • Roll-up summaries are supported: roll-up summary fields on the master can aggregate detail data (COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX). Key takeaway: A custom object can have up to 2 master-detail relationships and up to 40 total relationships. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: A custom object can have at most two master-detail relationships, not five. • Option C: Access to detail records is controlled by the master record; permissions are not set independently.

stem: A new agent is being developed to help customer service reps process customer requests for a replacement product. The agent needs to call an action that takes two inputs: productID: An 18-character ID for the product being replaced; reasonCode: A three-digit code representing the reason for the replacement. Which set of agent instructions should a Platform Administrator use for these inputs, according to best practices for Agentforce instructions?

options.text: Instructions for productID: "The 18-character ID of the product. Retrieve this from the conversation history or the user's input. Required." Instructions for reasonCode: "A three-digit code that specifies the reason for replacement. This is required only when the product ID is present."
Instructions for productID: "ID from the product record." Instructions for reasonCode: "Code for the reason."

Instructions for productID: "The product ID. Retrieve this from the conversation history or the user's input." Instructions for reasonCode: "The three-digit replacement reason. This is required when the product ID is present."
Instructions for productID: "The 18-character ID of the product." Instructions for reasonCode: "A numerical code."

sourceExplanation: Good Agentforce input instructions describe the expected format precisely, say where the agent should obtain the value, and state whether the input is required. Option A does all three: it specifies the 18-character format of productID, tells the agent to retrieve it from the conversation history or the user's input, marks it as required, and explains when reasonCode is required. Key takeaway: Input instructions should cover format, source of the value and whether the input is required. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Too vague; it gives no format, no retrieval guidance and no requirement information. • Option C: It omits the 18-character format and does not state that productID is required, so the agent has less guidance than in Option A. • Option D: It describes the format only partially and gives no retrieval or requirement guidance ("a numerical code" is ambiguous).

stem: Which two solutions is a Platform Administrator able to find on AppExchange to enhance their organization?

options.text: Customers
Communities
Consultants
Components

sourceExplanation: On AppExchange, a Platform Administrator can find: • Consultants: Experts and consulting partners who can help implement or optimize Salesforce solutions in your organization. • Components: Prebuilt apps, Lightning components, or integrations that can be installed to extend Salesforce functionality. Key takeaway: AppExchange offers apps, components, Flow solutions, Bolt solutions, data sets and consultants. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: AppExchange does not provide access to customer accounts; it's a marketplace for apps, components, and consulting services. • Option B: While Salesforce has Community Cloud (Experience Cloud), AppExchange itself does not provide communities—it provides solutions to enhance communities.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to ensure that every client has support based on the level of service that has been agreed on in the sales cycle. There are tiers to this support model: Gold, Silver, and Bronze. What should a Platform Administrator create to ensure that this is part of every client's account once they become a client?

options.text: Routing Configuration for each client
Case Assignment Rules for each client
A flow to assign Entitlements
Email-to-Case for each service level

sourceExplanation: Entitlements in Salesforce track the level of support a customer is entitled to (Gold, Silver, Bronze). By creating a flow, a Platform Administrator can automatically assign the correct entitlement to an Account once it becomes a client. This ensures that support processes consistently reflect the agreed-upon service level without manual intervention. Key takeaway: Entitlements define support levels; flows can automatically create the appropriate entitlement when an account becomes a customer. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Routing controls which agent or queue handles a case, but it does not assign or enforce the service level itself. • Option B: These only determine case ownership or assignment, not entitlements or service tiers. • Option D: Email-to-Case only converts emails into cases; it doesn't assign entitlements or enforce support tiers.

stem: Ursa Major Solar (UMS) wants a place within Salesforce to discuss sensitive records. UMS would like to be able to add new members but does not want non-members to be able to see any information about the forum. What should a Platform Administrator configure to achieve this?

options.text: Private Slack Channel
Chatter Public Group
Chatter Unlisted Group
Chatter Private Group

sourceExplanation: A Chatter Unlisted Group is ideal for sensitive discussions because: • Only members can see the group exists and view its content. • New members can be added by the group owner or manager. • Non-members cannot see posts, members, or any group information, ensuring complete privacy. Key takeaway: Unlisted groups are visible only to members and administrators, which suits sensitive discussions. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Slack is external to Salesforce and would not natively integrate for Salesforce record-level discussions. • Option B: Anyone in the org can see the group and its posts, which is not suitable for sensitive information. • Option D: Members can see the group exists, but the Unlisted Group adds an extra layer of secrecy by hiding it from non-members.

stem: Users at DreamHouse Realty are only allowed to see opportunities they own. Leadership wants an enterprise-wide dashboard of all open opportunities in the pipeline so that users can see how the company is performing at any point in time. How should a Platform Administrator create the dashboard without changing any sharing settings?

options.text: Create a dashboard with the running user set as someone who can see all opportunities.
Build individual dashboards for profiles that need to see the enterprise results.
Update the dashboard folder settings to manager for the sales reps role.
Add a filter to the dashboard to filter the opportunities by owner role.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, dashboards respect the permissions of the "running user" unless set to "dynamic dashboards." By setting the dashboard's running user to a user with access to all opportunities (e.g., a manager or system admin), the dashboard can display enterprise-wide opportunity data to leadership without changing individual users' sharing settings. Key takeaway: A dashboard running as a user with broad access shows company-wide data to viewers without changing sharing. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This is inefficient and unnecessary; one dashboard with the proper running user suffices. • Option C: Folder permissions control who can view the dashboard, not the data the dashboard displays. • Option D: Filtering by owner role won't give full enterprise-wide visibility; it still respects each user's access.

stem: Ursa Major Solar wants to automatically notify a manager about any cases awaiting a response from an agent for more than 2 hours after case creation. Which feature should a Platform Administrator use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Formula field
Case Escalation Rule
Omni-Channel Supervisor
Assignment Rule

sourceExplanation: Case Escalation Rules are designed to automatically monitor cases and take actions when certain conditions are met, such as a case not being updated or responded to within a specified time. In this scenario, the rule can: • Check if a case has not received a response for 2 hours. • Automatically notify the manager or escalate the case according to the defined actions. Key takeaway: Escalation rules evaluate age of cases (with business hours) and can notify or reassign. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Can calculate values but cannot trigger notifications or automate actions based on elapsed time. • Option C: Provides real-time monitoring of agents' workload but does not automatically notify managers about response delays. • Option D: Controls who a case is assigned to when created, but it does not handle timed notifications or escalations.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has a new flow that automatically sets field values when a new account is created. The flow is launched by a process, but the flow is not working properly. What should a Platform Administrator do to identify the problem?

options.text: Set up email logs and review the send error logs.
Review debug logs with the flow logging level.
Use the native debug feature in Flow Builder.
View the Setup Audit Trail and review for errors.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce's Flow Builder includes a native debug feature that allows a Platform Administrator to: • Run the flow step-by-step in a test mode. • See the input values, decisions, and actions taken by the flow. • Identify exactly where and why the flow is failing, even when it's launched by a process. Key takeaway: Flow Builder's Debug lets you run the flow and inspect each element's inputs and outputs. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Email logs track email sends and delivery, unrelated to flow execution. • Option B: While technically possible, it's more complicated and less focused than using Flow Builder's native debug tool. • Option D: Audit Trail tracks metadata changes, not runtime flow errors.

stem: Which two data loss considerations should a Platform Administrator keep in mind when changing a custom field type from Text to Picklist?

options.text: There will be no data loss with use of a global value set.
Any list view based on the custom field is deleted.
Auto updates will be made to Visualforce references to prevent data loss.
Assignment and escalation rules may be affected.

sourceExplanation: • List views may be deleted: When you change a custom field type from Text to Picklist, Salesforce may delete or invalidate existing list views that reference that field because the field's data type has changed and might no longer match the criteria. • Assignment and escalation rules may be affected: Rules that reference the field's value (e.g., for routing or assignment) can break or behave unexpectedly if the field type changes, since Picklist values are controlled and may not match previous Text values exactly. Key takeaway: Changing field types can cause data loss and break references; review dependent list views and rules first. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is not guaranteed; converting from Text to Picklist can lead to data truncation or mismatch if existing Text values don't match the picklist options. • Option C: Salesforce does not automatically update code references, including Visualforce, Apex, or integrations, when changing field types.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to initiate expense reports from Salesforce to the external HR system. Managers and directors need to review this process. Which two tools should a Platform Administrator configure?

options.text: Quick Action
Approval Process
Outbound Message
Email Alert Action

sourceExplanation: • Approval Process: Allows managers and directors to review and approve expense reports before they are sent to the external HR system. Provides a structured, automated approval workflow with notifications and routing. • Outbound Message: Automatically sends data from Salesforce to the external HR system once the record is approved. Works as part of workflow or approval actions to integrate Salesforce with external systems. Key takeaway: Approval processes support Outbound Message actions to send data to external systems after approval. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: While useful to create or submit records, it does not handle approvals or automatic integration with external systems. • Option D: Sends email notifications but cannot send structured data to external systems or enforce approval logic.

stem: Ursa Major Solar has its business hours set from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM for the reps that are on Pacific Time. The reps on Eastern Time need business hours set to start 3 hours earlier to cover for support. How should a Platform Administrator solve for this issue?

options.text: Allow the reps to set business hours manually.
Adjust the current business hours to accommodate the Eastern time zone.
Create one set of business hours per time zone.
Set temporary business hours for each time zone.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce allows multiple sets of business hours, so you can define different working hours for different time zones. By creating separate business hours for Pacific Time and Eastern Time, each rep group will have accurate coverage according to their local time, ensuring proper case escalation and service level tracking. Key takeaway: Multiple business hours can be created and associated with escalation rules, entitlements and cases. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Users cannot set their own business hours; this is configured at the org level. • Option B: Changing the existing set would affect all reps, not just Eastern Time reps. • Option D: Temporary hours are for short-term changes, not ongoing time zone differences.

stem: DreamHouse Realty (DHR) wants a templated process with a mortgage calculator that generates leads for loans. DHR needs to complete the project within 30 days and has maxed out its budget for the year. Which AppExchange item should help a Platform Administrator meet the request?

options.text: Flow Solutions
Bolt Solutions
Lightning Community
Lightning Data

sourceExplanation: Flow Solutions on AppExchange provide prebuilt automation processes that can include things like mortgage calculators, lead generation flows, and other guided steps. They are designed for fast deployment, which aligns perfectly with DHR's 30-day deadline and budget constraints. A Platform Administrator can import and configure these flows without building everything from scratch. Key takeaway: Flow Solutions on AppExchange provide pre-built, often free, flows that can be installed and adapted quickly. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: These are broader templates for apps and experiences, but may include more than what is needed, potentially adding unnecessary complexity or cost. • Option C: This is for creating portals or communities and does not provide prebuilt process flows like a mortgage calculator. • Option D: Provides external data enrichment and insights, not prebuilt automated processes.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) is partnering with a used shoe store and second-hand bicycle emporium. CK has an automated business process it wants to run once a week to count the number of open cases related to an Account. Which flow should a Platform Administrator recommend automating within Flow Builder for this business process?

options.text: Scheduled flow
Record-triggered flow
Automation event-triggered flow
Autolaunched flow

sourceExplanation: A Scheduled Flow in Salesforce is designed to run automatically at a set time or interval, such as weekly. In this scenario: • CK wants to count open cases per account once a week. • A scheduled flow can query records, perform calculations, and update fields or generate reports without any user interaction. Key takeaway: Schedule-triggered flows run at a set frequency (once, daily, weekly) on a batch of records. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Runs only when a record is created or updated, not on a schedule. • Option C: Salesforce does not have a flow type called "automation event-triggered flow." This is not valid. • Option D: Runs on demand or from another process, but does not run on a schedule unless invoked by a scheduled flow or process.

stem: A sales manager at DreamHouse Realty wants sales users to have a quick way to view and update the opportunities in their pipeline expected to close in the next 90 days. What should a Platform Administrator do to accomplish this request?

options.text: Make a new Sales dashboard and add a component that shows all opportunities that meet the criteria.
Enable Sales Console and show users how to open a tab for each opportunity in the pipeline that meets the requirements.
Create a list view on the Opportunity object and recommend users switch the view to Kanban to edit by drag and drop.
Create a custom report and schedule the sales users to receive it each day as a reminder to update their opportunities.

sourceExplanation: List views allow users to quickly filter opportunities based on criteria, such as expected close date within the next 90 days. Switching the list view to Kanban gives a visual, interactive interface where users can update opportunity stages by drag-and-drop, making it easy to manage the pipeline. This approach is simple, real-time, and requires no extra automation. Key takeaway: Kanban list views let users drag opportunities between stages and update fields directly. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Dashboards are for viewing metrics, not directly updating records. • Option B: While the console can help navigate records, it's less efficient than a Kanban list view for updating multiple opportunities quickly. • Option D: Reports provide information but cannot be used to update records directly, and daily emails are not as interactive.

stem: A Platform Administrator for Cloud Kicks needs to ensure that only the financial records belonging to each individual user are visible on the report in order to meet some of the data privacy requirements. How should the administrator achieve this?

options.text: Create multiple reports, each filtered to show records owned by each user.
Use Apex sharing to hide records.
Set sharing model as Private for the respective object(s).
Set sharing model as Public Read/Write for the respective object(s).

sourceExplanation: Setting the Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD) to Private ensures that users can only see records they own (or records explicitly shared with them). This is the standard way in Salesforce to enforce data privacy and ownership-based access for sensitive records, such as financial data. Reports automatically respect these sharing settings, so each user will only see their own records. Key takeaway: OWD sets the baseline access; reports only show records the running user can see. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is manual and unscalable. Sharing settings should handle access automatically. • Option B: Apex sharing can enforce fine-grained sharing, but it is unnecessary for standard ownership-based privacy, and adds complexity. • Option D: This would allow all users to see and edit all records, violating the privacy requirement.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to make sure clients are getting the attention they need and cases are not sitting longer than the Service-Level Agreement (SLA) it has with its clients. Which standard feature helps route cases to a Tier2 team if they have not been addressed in a specific amount of time?

options.text: Auto-Response Rules
Omni-Channel Routing
Milestone and Entitlements
Escalation Rules

sourceExplanation: Escalation Rules are a standard Salesforce feature designed to monitor case aging against defined criteria, such as Service-Level Agreements (SLAs). They can automatically: • Alert managers or teams if a case has not been addressed within a specific time. • Reassign or escalate cases to a Tier 2 or higher-level team to ensure timely attention. Key takeaway: Escalation rules move aging cases to another queue or user when SLA times are exceeded. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Only send automatic email responses when a case is created; they do not manage timing or escalation. • Option B: Dynamically assigns cases to agents based on availability and capacity, not SLA-based escalation. • Option C: Track SLA compliance and timing, but do not automatically reassign cases unless combined with escalation rules.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has a custom picklist field on Lead, which is missing on the Contact when leads are converted. Which two steps should the administrator take to ensure these values are populated?

options.text: Update the picklist value with a validation rule.
Set the picklist field to be required on the Lead object.
Create a custom picklist field on Contact.
Map the picklist field on the Lead to the Contact.

sourceExplanation: • Create a custom picklist field on Contact: Lead fields do not automatically appear on Contact after conversion unless a corresponding field exists. To carry the value over, the same (or compatible) picklist field must exist on the Contact object. • Map the picklist field on the Lead to the Contact: Lead field mapping tells Salesforce which Lead field populates which Contact field during conversion, ensuring the picklist value is transferred correctly. Key takeaway: Lead field mapping requires matching fields of compatible type on the target object. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Validation rules enforce data entry but do not control lead conversion or field population. • Option B: Making the field required ensures it's filled on the Lead, but does not ensure it appears on the Contact after conversion.

stem: A manager wants the sales team to update their opportunities on a regular basis. Which feature should a Platform Administrator implement to help with this?

options.text: Scheduled Reports
Big Deal Alerts
Opportunity Update Reminders
Similar Opportunities

sourceExplanation: Opportunity Update Reminders automatically prompt sales reps to review and update their opportunities on a regular schedule (for example, weekly). This directly supports the manager's goal of keeping opportunity data current without manual follow-ups. Key takeaway: Opportunity Update Reminders send reps weekly emails listing opportunities needing attention. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Deliver information on a schedule but don't prompt users to update records. • Option B: Notify users about large opportunities, not routine updates. • Option D: Helps compare deals but doesn't encourage regular updates.

stem: Cloud Kicks has three teams of customer service reps that use a custom field on the Case object to populate the team assigned to manage the tickets. The customer support manager would like a Cases Dashboard to show data specific to each team. What should a Platform Administrator do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create separate Dashboards for each Customer Support team.
Add Cross Filters to switch between the three customer service teams.
Create a Dashboard with widgets specific to each team.
Create a Dashboard that uses Dashboard Filters to show specific team data.

sourceExplanation: Dashboard Filters allow users to dynamically filter dashboard data based on field values, such as the custom Case Team field. This lets the customer support manager (and others) switch between teams within a single dashboard, viewing team-specific metrics without maintaining multiple dashboards. Key takeaway: Dashboard filters (up to three) let viewers filter all components by a field value. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This increases maintenance and is unnecessary when one dashboard can serve all teams. • Option B: Cross filters are used in reports, not dashboards, and are meant to include or exclude related records—not switch between values. • Option C: This would clutter the dashboard and still wouldn't allow easy filtering by team.

stem: Users have reported that the new Lightning account record page is loading very slowly. Which feature should a Platform Administrator use to determine the cause of the performance issues?

options.text: Lightning App Builder Analyze
Lightning Page Visibility Rule
Lightning Analytics
Lightning Usage App

sourceExplanation: Lightning App Builder Analyze is the tool specifically built to analyze Lightning record page performance. It helps administrators: • Identify components or configurations that slow down page load times • Receive recommendations to optimize the Lightning page design This makes it the best choice for determining the cause of performance issues on a Lightning Account record page. Key takeaway: "Analyze" in Lightning App Builder evaluates page performance and suggests improvements. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Controls when components appear; it does not analyze performance. • Option C: Used for business analytics and reporting, not UI performance troubleshooting. • Option D: Shows usage and high-level performance trends, but does not pinpoint page-level causes.

stem: When Agentforce performs its grounding check, it examines source information, the topic instructions, and scope. Which additional information does the agent look for during its grounding check?

options.text: The web for information verification
Prompt injection risks
Encrypted fields
Incompatible data types

sourceExplanation: During Agentforce's grounding check, the agent evaluates whether it can safely and accurately respond by reviewing: • Source information • Topic instructions • Scope In addition to these, it also checks for prompt injection risks—attempts to manipulate the agent's behavior or override its instructions. This helps ensure responses remain safe, reliable, and aligned with the defined purpose. Key takeaway: Grounding checks ensure responses are based on source data and screen for prompt injection risk. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Agentforce does not automatically browse or verify information on the web during grounding. • Option C: These relate to data security and access, not grounding checks. • Option D: These are relevant to automation or integrations, not the grounding evaluation.

stem: A sales rep wants to be able to categorize multiple picklist values into a single value on a report. Which option should a Platform Administrator suggest to the sales rep to accomplish this?

options.text: Unique Count
Chart
Report Filter
Bucket Column

sourceExplanation: A Bucket Column in Salesforce reports allows users to group multiple picklist values into a single, custom category directly within the report. This is ideal when a sales rep wants to simplify reporting without changing the underlying data. Key takeaway: Bucket fields group picklist values into custom categories within a report. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Counts distinct values; it does not group or categorize them. • Option B: Visualizes report data but does not change or group values. • Option C: Filters records in or out but does not combine values into a single category.

stem: Cloud Kicks has been seeing exponential growth and will be hiring an additional 10 sales reps and 15 support reps to its teams. The support team will need access to the Service Console to manage cases. A Platform Administrator will be assigning the users to existing custom sales and support profiles. How should the administrator ensure the support reps have the appropriate access to the console?

options.text: Enable the Service Cloud User feature license for the support reps on the User Detail page.
Build a Service Console using Lightning App Builder for the custom service profile.
Create a permission set for the Service Console and assign it to the support reps.
Assign the Salesforce Platform User License to the support reps.

sourceExplanation: The Service Cloud User feature license is required for users to access Service Cloud features, including the Service Console, Knowledge, and Entitlements. Even if a Lightning console app exists and permission sets assign the app, users cannot access Service Cloud functionality without this feature license. This is especially important when assigning users to existing custom profiles, as the profile alone doesn't grant Service Cloud access. Key takeaway: Service Console access requires the Service Cloud User feature license on the user record. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Only configures the app itself; it does not grant access to Service Cloud features. • Option C: Permission sets can grant app/tab access, but cannot enable the Service Cloud User feature license—this must be done on the user record first. • Option D: Platform licenses do not support Service Cloud or Cases, so this would prevent console access.

stem: A user is unable to relate a task to the Course custom object. What should a Platform Administrator do to allow tasks to be related to courses?

options.text: Update the user's profile to grant them Edit access to the Task object.
Create a sharing rule for the Course object to grant the user Read/Write access.
Select Allow Activities on the Course object in Object Manager.
Add the Open Activities related list to the Course page layout.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, for tasks or events (activities) to be related to a custom object, the object must have "Allow Activities" enabled in Object Manager. Once enabled, users can relate tasks and events to records of that object type. Key takeaway: "Allow Activities" must be enabled on custom objects for tasks and events to be related. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Users already have access to tasks; the issue is that the Course object isn't configured to allow activities, not user permissions. • Option B: Sharing controls record visibility, not whether tasks can be related. • Option D: Useful for viewing related activities, but doesn't enable the ability to relate new tasks until "Allow Activities" is turned on.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks has a request from the finance team that all won opportunities over a certain value must be checked for accuracy before the deal can be considered fully closed. The assigned finance team member, as well as the seller's manager, both must sign off on the deal, with the manager doing so first. Then, the finance team member must sign off, for a total of up to three sign-offs per opportunity. How should the administrator address this request?

options.text: Add a Lightning web component to the opportunity page to capture the details in an approval record.
Create a screen flow that runs anytime an opportunity is closed.
Create an approval process with specific steps.
Create a quick action to send emails to both the manager and the finance team member.

sourceExplanation: An Approval Process in Salesforce is designed for multi-step, sequential approvals, which fits the scenario perfectly: • The seller's manager approves first. • The finance team member approves second. • Optional third approval if needed. Approval processes can also enforce conditions (like won opportunities over a certain value) before triggering the approvals. The process ensures auditability, automated routing, and record locking if desired, which is exactly what finance needs for accuracy checks. Key takeaway: Multi-step approval processes handle sequential approvals (manager then finance). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Can capture info, but does not provide structured, enforceable approvals. • Option B: Flows can automate processes, but this would require custom logic to replicate sequential approvals, which is more complex and less maintainable than using an approval process. • Option D: Only sends notifications; cannot enforce approval, track sign-offs, or lock the record until approvals are complete.

stem: A Platform Administrator is adding a new topic to an agent. What is best practice for topic instructions?

options.text: Keep instructions as minimal as possible to reduce agent latency.
Write the instructions generically to allow the agent maximum flexibility in its reasoning.
Include an extended list of example user questions so the agent can learn from patterns.
Add business-specific language rather than plain language.

sourceExplanation: Providing representative example user questions in topic instructions helps the agent recognise the kinds of requests that belong to the topic and how to handle them. Examples guide the agent's reasoning while keeping instructions clear and specific. Key takeaway: Topic instructions should be clear and specific, with examples to guide the agent. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Instructions that are too minimal leave the agent without enough context. • Option B: Generic instructions lead to off-topic or inconsistent answers. • Option D: Instructions should use plain, clear language rather than business jargon.

stem: Sales managers would like to know what could be implemented to surface important values based on the stage of the opportunity. Which tool should a Platform Administrator use to meet this requirement?

options.text: Dynamic Forms
Workflow Rules
Path Key Fields
Opportunity Processes

sourceExplanation: Path Key Fields allow administrators to highlight important fields and guidance on a record based on the stage of an opportunity. Sales reps see the key fields directly in the Path component as they move opportunities through stages, making it easier to focus on the most critical data at each stage. This is specifically designed to surface important values and provide stage-specific guidance, exactly what sales managers requested. Key takeaway: Path key fields show important fields for each stage directly in the path component. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Customize page layouts and field visibility but do not automatically highlight key fields by stage. • Option B: Automate actions based on criteria; they cannot display key fields dynamically on the page. • Option D: Define business processes and picklist values for different types of opportunities, but they don't surface key fields dynamically by stage.

stem: Marketing users at Cloud Kicks have been completing the Lead Source field inconsistently, with values like Web, Website, and Online. To ensure data quality, a Platform Administrator needs to standardize these records. Which Flow should the administrator use to clean up these inconsistent Lead Source values?

options.text: Schedule-triggered flow
Segment-triggered flow
Record-triggered flow
Screen flow

sourceExplanation: A Schedule-Triggered Flow runs automatically on a set schedule (e.g., daily or weekly) and can process multiple records at once. In this case, it can identify inconsistent Lead Source values (like Web, Website, Online) and update them to standardized values, ensuring data quality. This approach does not require user interaction and can clean up existing records in bulk. Key takeaway: Scheduled flows are ideal for batch data cleanup on existing records. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Salesforce does not have a flow type called "Segment-triggered flow"; this is invalid. • Option C: Runs only when a record is created or updated, so it won't clean up existing inconsistent data automatically on a schedule. • Option D: Requires user interaction, which is unnecessary for automated data cleanup.

stem: The sales director at Cloud Kicks wants to be able to predict upcoming revenue in the next several fiscal quarters so they can set goals and benchmark how reps are performing. Which two features should a Platform Administrator configure?

options.text: Forecasting
Opportunity List View
Sales Quotas
Opportunity Stages

sourceExplanation: • Forecasting: Salesforce Forecasts allow sales directors to predict upcoming revenue based on opportunities, expected close dates, and probability. Forecasts can be viewed by team, region, or individual rep, making it easier to set goals and monitor performance over fiscal quarters. • Sales Quotas: Quotas define the revenue targets for individual reps or teams. When combined with Forecasting, managers can compare predicted revenue to targets, benchmark performance, and identify gaps. Key takeaway: Collaborative Forecasts with quotas show revenue predictions and attainment against targets. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Provides a filtered view of opportunities, but does not provide predictive forecasting or benchmark metrics. • Option D: Track progress in the sales process but don't predict future revenue or provide goal comparisons.

stem: A Platform Administrator needs to enable Agentforce for the service team. What is the most critical prerequisite for ensuring the Service Agents have a complete and accurate view of their customers?

options.text: Activate Email-to-Case for the agent.
Create new user profiles for the agent.
Configure a new Service Console layout.
Verify Data Cloud is implemented.

sourceExplanation: Agentforce relies on a unified, complete view of the customer to provide accurate, AI-driven guidance. Data Cloud (or a similar data unification layer) ensures that all relevant customer data—from different systems and objects—is aggregated and accessible for the agent. Without Data Cloud, the agent may have incomplete or inconsistent customer information, reducing the effectiveness of AI recommendations. Key takeaway: Data Cloud unifies customer data from multiple sources for accurate grounding of agents. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Only captures email cases; does not provide a full view of the customer. • Option B: Profiles control access but do not unify customer data for the agent. • Option C: Useful for interface, but if the underlying customer data is incomplete, the console alone won't improve accuracy.

stem: One of the sales managers at Universal Containers will be going on leave for several months. The executives want to make sure the sales manager does not log in to Salesforce while on leave. What should a Platform Administrator do to ensure the user is not able to log in while on leave?

options.text: Freeze the user's account.
Change the Login Hours for the profile.
Reassign the user's license during leave.
Restrict Login IP Addresses for the profile.

sourceExplanation: Freezing a user immediately prevents them from logging into Salesforce without deactivating the account, preserving all ownerships, roles, and data associations. It is ideal for temporary situations, like a leave of absence. Once the user returns, the freeze can be removed, and normal access resumes. Key takeaway: Freezing a user blocks login without deactivation, keeping licenses and ownership intact. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Only restricts access during certain hours, not entirely while the user is on leave. • Option C: Not practical and could cause complications with record ownership; also, licenses may not be reusable immediately. • Option D: Only blocks access from certain locations, not globally.

stem: Cloud Kicks has the organization-wide defaults for Opportunity set to Private. Which two features should a Platform Administrator use to open up access to opportunity records for sales users working on collaborative deals?

options.text: Profiles
Role hierarchy
Sharing rules
Sharing set

sourceExplanation: • Role hierarchy: Opens access up the hierarchy, so managers and higher-level roles can see opportunities owned by users below them. Useful for collaborative deals where oversight is needed. • Sharing rules: Provide record-level access beyond role hierarchy, allowing certain groups, roles, or public groups to access specific opportunities. Can be based on criteria (e.g., deal type, region) or ownership. Key takeaway: Role hierarchy and sharing rules are the standard ways to open access beyond a Private OWD. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Control baseline object and field-level permissions, not record-level access. Profiles alone cannot open access to private opportunities. • Option D: Only applies to Experience Cloud (community) users, not internal sales users.

stem: Cloud Kicks needs to change the owner of a case when it has been open for more than 7 days. What should a Platform Administrator use to complete this requirement?

options.text: Assignment Rules
Auto-Response Rules
Validation Rules
Escalation Rules

sourceExplanation: Escalation Rules are specifically designed to take action on cases that meet certain criteria after a set period of time, such as reassigning the case to another user or queue. In this scenario, the case needs to change ownership after being open for more than 7 days, which is a classic use case for escalation rules. Escalation rules can also send email alerts to notify the new owner or manager. Key takeaway: Escalation rules can reassign cases after a specified age. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Assign a case when it is created, but do not reassign cases based on age or time elapsed. • Option B: Only send automatic email responses when a case is created; they cannot reassign cases. • Option C: Enforce data entry requirements but do not automate ownership changes.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks received a request from the head of sales operations to create a process in which opportunities must be validated by specific team leaders based on a mix of criteria. When the administrator analyzed the list of criteria, they found that there were 30 potential sets of criteria that would identify the proper person to route the request to. How should the administrator fulfill this request?

options.text: Create a record-triggered flow orchestration to properly route the requests.
Create a button on the opportunity that brings up an email template to send to the correct leader.
Use a screen flow to allow the seller to input the criteria in a form that is then sent to the appropriate leader.
Create an approval process with specific entry criteria and approval steps for each of the sets of criteria specified.

sourceExplanation: Flow Orchestration is designed to handle complex, multi-step, and branching business processes with multiple criteria and participants. With 30 potential sets of criteria, it is far more scalable and maintainable to use a record-triggered orchestration flow than creating dozens of separate approval processes. It can automatically route the opportunity to the correct team leader based on the combination of criteria, reducing manual effort and complexity. Key takeaway: Flow Orchestration handles complex, multi-step processes with many branching paths and participants. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This is manual and error-prone, not scalable for 30 criteria sets. • Option C: Requires manual user input each time and does not automate routing based on predefined criteria. • Option D: Managing 30 separate approval processes would be complex, hard to maintain, and inefficient.

stem: The client services and customer support teams share the same profile but have different permission sets. The custom object Retention related list needs to be restricted to the client services team on the Lightning record page layout. What should a Platform Administrator use to fulfill this request?

options.text: Component Visibility
Record Type Assignment
Page Layout Assignment
Sharing Settings

sourceExplanation: Component Visibility on a Lightning record page allows administrators to show or hide components or related lists based on user criteria, such as profile, permission set, or field values. Since the client services and support teams share the same profile, using Page Layout Assignment alone won't work. Component Visibility can differentiate access based on the permission set assigned to the client services team. This approach ensures that only users with the specific permission set see the Retention related list on the record page. Key takeaway: Component visibility can filter on permissions, allowing different users with the same profile to see different components. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Controls which page layout and picklist values are available per record type, not related list visibility per permission set. • Option C: Cannot differentiate users if they share the same profile. Page layouts are assigned by profile and record type, so it won't hide the related list for a subset of users. • Option D: Controls record-level access, not visibility of components on a page layout.

stem: A salesperson complains that the Log a Call button is missing from the highlights panel of an Opportunity page. What is the reason for this?

options.text: The Log a Call action will appear within the Activity Component as a standard behavior rather than the highlights panel.
The custom Log a Call permission has been disabled at the org level in Setup.
The Log a Call action has not been added to the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of the page layout.
The custom Log a Call permission is missing from the user's profile and assigned permission sets.

sourceExplanation: In Lightning Experience, the Log a Call action appears in the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of the page layout. If it's missing from the highlights panel, it usually means the action has not been added to that section. Once added to the page layout, it will appear in the highlights panel for users. Key takeaway: Actions in Lightning come from the "Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions" section of the page layout. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Incorrect. In Lightning, Log a Call can appear in the highlights panel if properly configured on the page layout. • Option B: There is no org-level permission for Log a Call; it is a standard action. • Option D: Again, Log a Call is a standard action, not a custom permission, so this does not apply.

stem: Users at Cloud Kicks want to see information that is more useful for their role on the Case page. How should a Platform Administrator make the pages more dynamic and easier to use?

options.text: Include more tab components with filters.
Remove fields from the record details component.
Add component visibility filters to the components.
Delete the extra components from the page.

sourceExplanation: Component visibility filters allow you to dynamically show or hide components on a Lightning page based on criteria such as user role, profile, record type, or field values. This makes the page more relevant and easier to use, because each user sees only the components that are useful for their role. It improves usability without removing functionality or cluttering the page for all users. Key takeaway: Component visibility filters let a single page adapt to user, record or device criteria. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Adding tabs alone does not make the page dynamic based on user role. • Option B: This permanently removes fields for all users and doesn't create dynamic visibility. • Option D: Permanently removing components reduces functionality rather than customizing the page dynamically for roles.

stem: The VP of sales at AW Computing would like sales reps to check in with their top account every Monday. The VP would like a dashboard component to show the status of the check-ins. What should a Platform Administrator configure to remind the reps to contact their top account?

options.text: Use a process email alert on the account.
Create a time-based workflow task.
Add the email action to the page layout.
Enable the creation of recurring tasks.

sourceExplanation: Recurring tasks allow sales reps to be reminded on a set schedule, such as every Monday, to check in with their top accounts. Tasks can be linked to accounts, opportunities, or contacts, and their completion status can feed into dashboards to track check-ins. This provides a structured, repeatable process without requiring manual creation of tasks each week. Key takeaway: Recurring tasks automate regular reminders such as weekly check-ins. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Sends emails but does not create tasks for tracking or dashboard reporting. • Option B: Workflow tasks can be scheduled, but cannot create truly recurring tasks; they are triggered once based on criteria. • Option C: Allows sending emails but does not create reminders or recurring check-ins.

stem: Universal Containers has two sales teams, sales team A and sales team B. Each team has their own role in the role hierarchy. Both roles are subordinates of the same Manager role. How should a Platform Administrator share records owned by sales team A with sales team B?

options.text: Criteria-based sharing
Owner-based sharing
Hierarchical sharing
Manual sharing

sourceExplanation: Owner-based sharing rules allow administrators to share records owned by users in a specific role, role & subordinates, or public group with other roles, groups, or users. In this case, records owned by sales team A can be shared with sales team B by creating an owner-based sharing rule targeting the role for team A and granting access to the role or group for team B. This approach works even though both teams report to the same manager, because OWD might restrict access between the teams. Key takeaway: Owner-based sharing rules share records owned by one role or group with another role or group. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Shares records based on field values, not ownership. • Option C: Only automatically shares records up the role hierarchy (e.g., manager sees subordinates' records), not across sibling roles. • Option D: Requires users to share individual records one by one, which is not scalable for a whole team.

stem: The Universal Containers sales team wants a visual way to manage their opportunity pipeline that allows them to see all deals at once, track progress through sales stages, and quickly move opportunities forward. Which feature should a Platform Administrator recommend to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure opportunity list views with custom filters and summary fields.
Create a custom dashboard with opportunity pipeline charts and stage metrics.
Use the Kanban view for opportunities with card fields and drag-and-drop functionality.
Set up opportunity reports with chart components and stage-based grouping.

sourceExplanation: The Kanban view provides a visual, interactive board that displays all opportunities in columns based on their sales stage. Users can see all deals at once, track progress, and move opportunities forward by dragging and dropping cards between stages. It's specifically designed for pipeline management and gives sales reps a quick, intuitive overview of their deals. Key takeaway: Kanban shows opportunities in stage columns with drag-and-drop movement. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Provides a filtered list but is not visual and doesn't allow drag-and-drop stage updates. • Option B: Dashboards show summary charts and metrics, but they are not interactive for moving opportunities. • Option D: Reports provide insights and grouping, but do not allow real-time pipeline management or drag-and-drop updates.

stem: In an approval process, what happens when a queue is selected as the approver?

options.text: The queue can only be used for objects that do not support individual user approvals.
Only the queue owner is notified about the approval request, not its members.
The queue requires unanimous approval from all of its members before the record is approved.
Any member of the queue can approve or reject the record and the queue is treated as a single entity.

sourceExplanation: When a queue is selected as the approver in an approval process, all members of the queue are notified of the pending approval. Only one member needs to take action (approve or reject) for the record to move forward. The queue is treated as a single entity in the approval workflow, simplifying group approvals without requiring action from every member. Key takeaway: When a queue is the approver, any member can approve or reject on behalf of the queue. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Incorrect; queues can be used for standard objects that support approvals as well. • Option B: Incorrect; all queue members receive notifications. • Option C: Incorrect; Salesforce does not require all members to approve, only one action is needed.
