stem: Universal Containers (UC) customers have provided feedback that their support cases are not being responded to quickly enough. UC wants to send all unassigned cases that have been open for more than 2 hours to an urgent Case queue and alert the support manager. Which feature should a Platform Administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Case Dashboard Refreshes
Case Assignment Rules
Case Scheduled Reports
Case Escalation Rules

sourceExplanation: Case Escalation Rules are designed to automatically take action on cases that meet certain criteria after a specified time period. In this scenario: • The case is unassigned and has been open for more than 2 hours. • The escalation rule can assign the case to the Urgent Case queue and notify the support manager automatically. Escalation rules ensure that cases are addressed within defined service levels and help improve response times. Key takeaway: Escalation rules can move unassigned aging cases to an urgent queue and notify a manager. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Only updates dashboards; does not perform actions on cases. • Option B: Assign cases when they are created, but do not reassign based on time elapsed. • Option C: Can notify users about cases but does not automatically reassign or escalate cases.

stem: An agent is being developed with several actions that all retrieve information from different databases. A Platform Administrator has named the actions as follows: - GetCustomerInfo - GetOrderDetails -GetShippingStatus Which best practice should the administrator follow to improve these names?

options.text: Use additional related verbs, such as Find, Retrieve, or Identify.
Add the word "Salesforce" to the beginning of each action name to improve context for the large language model.
Remove all verbs and use only nouns, such as CustomerInfo, OrderDetails, and ShippingStatus.
Use a consistent naming convention by starting each action with the verb "Get".

sourceExplanation: Consistency in naming actions helps both the agent developer and the AI model understand the purpose of each action. By starting each action with the verb "Get", it's immediately clear that these actions retrieve information. This improves readability, maintainability, and predictability for anyone using or updating the agent. Key takeaway: Consistent, descriptive action names help the agent choose the correct action. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Could introduce inconsistency, making it harder to quickly understand what each action does. • Option B: Adds unnecessary complexity; the agent already knows the context. • Option C: Makes it unclear that the actions perform retrieval, reducing clarity.

stem: What is the next step an agent performs when the tasks within an agentic loop are all unsatisfactory?

options.text: Routes to a live agent
Asks for additional information
Gives an error message
Provides the best answer possible with caveats

sourceExplanation: In an agentic loop, the agent iteratively tries to complete tasks based on the available information. If all attempted tasks are unsatisfactory, the agent's best next step is to ask the user for additional information to clarify the request or provide context. This prevents the agent from giving incorrect or incomplete answers and keeps the interaction productive. Key takeaway: When all attempted steps fail, the agent asks the user for clarification or more information. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is only done if the agent cannot proceed after requesting additional information. • Option C: Ending the interaction abruptly reduces user experience and doesn't attempt to resolve the issue. • Option D: The agent only does this if it has some usable information, but in this case, all tasks were unsatisfactory, so more information is needed first.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) has a new Platform Administrator who is asked to put together a memo detailing Salesforce usage to budget for upcoming license purchases. Where should the administrator go to find out what type of licenses CK has purchased and how many are available?

options.text: User licenses related list in company information
Usage-based entitlements related list in company information
User management settings in setup
Search for licenses types in setup

sourceExplanation: The Company Information page in Salesforce displays the User Licenses related list, which shows: • The types of licenses the organization has purchased (e.g., Salesforce, Platform, Service Cloud). • How many licenses are in use and how many are available. This is the most direct and accurate place to gather license data for budgeting or planning purposes. Key takeaway: Company Information shows purchased, used and remaining user licenses. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Tracks service entitlements, not license counts. • Option C: Allows managing users, but doesn't provide a summary of license counts. • Option D: May help locate license settings, but won't show how many are purchased or available.

stem: Ursa Major Solar wants to roll out the Salesforce mobile app, and the first information it wants its users to see is the Top Opportunities report. What should a Platform Administrator configure to achieve this?

options.text: Add the Dashboards tab to the Salesforce mobile app.
Enable Mobile Home for the Salesforce mobile app.
Enable Today for the Salesforce mobile app.
Add the Reports tab to the Salesforce mobile app.

sourceExplanation: Mobile Home is the customizable landing page of the Salesforce mobile app. The administrator can place components such as the Top Opportunities report on it so that it is the first information users see when opening the app. Key takeaway: Mobile Home can be customized with Lightning App Builder components. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Adding the Dashboards tab only adds a navigation item; it does not make the report the first thing users see. • Option C: Today is a calendar/meeting-focused page and does not display a chosen report first. • Option D: Adding the Reports tab only provides access to reports; it is not the landing page.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Ursa Major Solar has been asked to change the Work Item and Project custom object relationship from a master-detail to a lookup. Which scenario prevents the administrator from fulfilling this requirement?

options.text: A junction object is required to support the lookup.
Roll-up summary fields exist on the master object.
The lookup field is required for saving records.
The lookup field in all the records contains a value.

sourceExplanation: Master-detail relationships allow roll-up summary fields to aggregate data from the detail object to the master object. Salesforce does not allow a master-detail relationship to be changed to a lookup if the master object has any roll-up summary fields, because the aggregation depends on the master-detail link. To convert the relationship, the roll-up summary fields must first be removed. Key takeaway: Delete roll-up summary fields before converting a master-detail relationship to a lookup. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Not necessary; a lookup does not require a junction object. • Option C: This does not prevent conversion; you can make a lookup required. • Option D: This is acceptable; Salesforce can handle lookups with existing values during the conversion.

stem: A sales rep typically has several open opportunities for each of their accounts. Which tool should a Platform Administrator suggest to the sales rep to obtain the total number of accounts associated with open opportunities in a report?

options.text: Group Rows
Unique Count
Report Filter
Bucket Column

sourceExplanation: When a sales rep has multiple open opportunities per account, simply counting rows in a report would overcount the accounts. Using Unique Count allows the report to count each account only once, giving the total number of distinct accounts associated with open opportunities. This ensures the sales rep sees accurate account totals, even if multiple opportunities exist for the same account. Key takeaway: Unique Count counts distinct values (such as accounts) across multiple rows. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Groups data but does not provide a distinct count of accounts. • Option C: Limits which records are shown but does not calculate totals. • Option D: Categorizes data into ranges or buckets but does not perform unique counting.

stem: There are multiple system administrators at Cloud Kicks that make configuration changes. Which tool gives the system administrators the ability to track these changes?

options.text: History Tracking
Health Check
Feed Tracking
Setup Audit Trail

sourceExplanation: Setup Audit Trail tracks all configuration changes made in Salesforce, such as creating objects, fields, workflows, or changing settings. It records who made the change, what was changed, and when, making it ideal for organizations with multiple system administrators. Administrators can download 6 months of changes for review, auditing, or troubleshooting. Key takeaway: Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes for the last 180 days. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Tracks changes to record field values, not configuration changes. • Option B: Evaluates security settings and compares them to Salesforce best practices; it does not track changes. • Option C: Tracks changes in Chatter feeds on records, not in setup or configuration.

stem: Universal Containers wants to track all stakeholders involved in its sales opportunities to ensure proper relationship management. Sales reps need to identify who has decision-making authority, who influences the buying process, and who serves as the primary contact for each deal. The sales manager wants visibility into these relationships to help coach reps on stakeholder management strategies. Which feature should a Platform Administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Use standard fields on opportunities to track stakeholder information.
Use contact roles on opportunities to identify stakeholder involvement and influence.
Configure opportunity team members to track internal and external stakeholders.
Set up account teams to track stakeholders across multiple opportunities.

sourceExplanation: Contact Roles on Opportunities allow sales reps to associate multiple contacts with a single opportunity and define each contact's role, such as Decision Maker, Influencer, or Primary Contact. This gives visibility into who impacts the deal, supporting coaching and stakeholder management strategies. Sales managers can run reports and dashboards on contact roles to monitor engagement and relationships across deals. Key takeaway: Opportunity contact roles define each contact's role (decision maker, influencer, etc.). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Standard fields are limited, and cannot track multiple stakeholders or their roles for a single opportunity. • Option C: Tracks internal team members supporting the opportunity, not external stakeholders. • Option D: Tracks stakeholders across accounts, but does not provide role-specific visibility at the opportunity level.

stem: A Platform Administrator is building an agent to help an ecommerce support team. The agent needs to call an action, named updateShippingAddress, that modifies a customer's shipping address in the system. Which set of Action Instructions should the administrator use for the updateShippingAddress action, according to best practices?

options.text: "This action allows for the changing of a shipping address, and the goal is to make sure the address is current and accurate."

"Updates the shipping address for a customer order. The goal of the action is to modify the address on a customer's record. The agent should only use this action when the user explicitly requests to change their address."
"This action updates the customer's shipping address. It is to be used when a user wants to change their address. Only use this when a customer does not have an active order in the system."
"Use this to update shipping information. It's used for any changes to a customer's address in the system."

sourceExplanation: Action Instructions should be clear, specific, and provide guidance for proper use. Option B clearly states the purpose of the action, defines when the action should be used (only when the user explicitly requests it), and reduces the risk of the agent using the action inappropriately. This aligns with best practices for Agentforce, which emphasize precise instructions and constraints for AI-driven actions. Key takeaway: Action instructions should state what the action does and exactly when to use it. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Too vague; it describes the goal but does not specify when or how to use the action. • Option C: Adds unnecessary conditions (active order) that may limit correct usage without sufficient context. • Option D: Too generic; it doesn't define proper usage or constraints, which could lead to errors.

stem: A user at Northern Trail Outfitters is having trouble logging in to Salesforce. The user's login history shows that this person has attempted to log in multiple times and has been locked out of the organization. Which two steps should a Platform Administrator take to help the user log in to Salesforce?

options.text: Reset password on the user's record detail page.
Log in as the user to unlock the user and reset the password.
Use the unlock button on the user's record detail page.
Reset the password policies to allow the user to login.

sourceExplanation: • Reset password: Sends the user a new temporary password, allowing them to log in again. This is standard when a user is locked out due to failed login attempts. • Unlock button: Directly unlocks the user account without changing the password, letting them try logging in again immediately. Key takeaway: Administrators can unlock users and reset passwords from the user detail page. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Administrators cannot log in as a user if the account is locked out; this option is not possible in this scenario. • Option D: Changing password policies is unnecessary to unlock a single user and is not a best practice for addressing an individual lockout.

stem: When a sales rep clicks a button on an opportunity, a simple discount calculator screen should be launched. Which automation tool should a Platform Administrator use to build this discount calculator screen?

options.text: Flow Builder
Platform Event
Batch Apex
OmniStudio

sourceExplanation: Flow Builder allows administrators to create interactive screens that can collect input, perform calculations, and display results. In this scenario, a simple discount calculator screen can be built as a screen flow and launched via a button on the Opportunity. Flow Builder is click-based, requires no code, and is ideal for guided, user-facing interactions like calculators or data entry forms. Key takeaway: Screen flows launched by a button or quick action create interactive calculators. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Used for asynchronous event-driven integrations, not for user-facing interactive screens. • Option C: Handles large-scale, asynchronous processing in the background; not suitable for interactive UI. • Option D: Used for complex, enterprise-grade guided experiences and digital interactions, overkill for a simple calculator.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) wants to ensure new Contacts are validated before they can be saved. If a user selects that the LeadSource picklist value is Other, NTO also wants to populate a custom text field called Source__c. Which validation rule should a Platform Administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: AND(NOT(LeadSource = 'Other'), NOT(Source__c = ""))
AND(ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Other'), ISBLANK(Source__c))
AND(NOT(ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Other')), NOT(ISBLANK(Source__c)))
AND(LeadSource = 'Other', Source__c = "")

sourceExplanation: The requirement is: if LeadSource = "Other", then Source__c must be populated. A validation rule fires when a record is invalid, so we want it to trigger only when LeadSource is "Other" and Source__c is blank. ISPICKVAL(LeadSource,'Other') checks the picklist value. ISBLANK(Source__c) checks if the custom text field is empty. Using AND(...) ensures the rule triggers only when both conditions are true. Key takeaway: Use ISPICKVAL for picklists and ISBLANK for text in validation rule formulas. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This fires when LeadSource is not Other and Source__c is not blank, which is the opposite of the requirement. • Option C: Fires when LeadSource is not Other and Source__c is populated, irrelevant to the requirement. • Option D: Incorrect syntax: for picklists, must use ISPICKVAL, and Source__c = "" is less reliable than ISBLANK(Source__c) for text fields.

stem: A Platform Administrator deactivates an agent to add a new topic and action. What happens to any ongoing user conversations with the agent?

options.text: The agent window automatically closes to prevent new messages.
The agent will continue conversations using the deactivated agent until reactivated.
The agent will pause the conversation and resume once reactivated.
The agent will send a system error message as a response to any new messages.

sourceExplanation: When an agent is deactivated, it cannot handle new conversations or new messages. Ongoing conversations that started before deactivation continue normally using the version of the agent that was active. The agent does not automatically close the chat, pause, or send system errors during these active sessions. Key takeaway: Ongoing conversations continue on the prior agent version after deactivation; new conversations are not started. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: The chat window remains open; deactivation does not forcibly close ongoing conversations. • Option C: Conversations do not automatically pause; the session continues without interruption. • Option D: Only occurs for new conversations after deactivation, not for ongoing sessions.

stem: Which action should a Platform Administrator configure to reverse a submitted approval request and unlock the associated record when setting up an approval process?

options.text: Recall Actions
Initial Submission Actions
Final Rejection Actions
Final Approval Actions

sourceExplanation: Recall Actions are specifically configured to allow a user or administrator to recall (reverse) a submitted approval request. When an approval request is recalled, the associated record is unlocked so it can be edited again before resubmitting. This is the standard way in Salesforce to reverse a submission without rejecting or approving it. Key takeaway: Recall actions run when a submitter recalls a request, typically unlocking the record. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: These actions occur when the record is first submitted for approval, not when recalling it. • Option C: These actions run after a record is rejected, not when reversing a submission. • Option D: These actions run after a record is fully approved, so they don't affect reversing the request.

stem: A sales team is having difficulty understanding which stage their opportunity is in and what the company sales process requires of them in that stage. Which feature should a Platform Administrator implement to help the sales team quickly determine where they are in the sales process and what is required of them?

options.text: Opportunity Sales Path
Big Deal Alerts
Reports & Dashboards
List Views

sourceExplanation: Opportunity Sales Path provides a visual guide at the top of the Opportunity record that clearly shows the current sales stage, key fields that should be completed at each stage, and guidance and tips on what actions are required to move to the next stage. This helps sales reps immediately understand where they are in the sales process and what the company expects at that stage, without needing extra training or documentation. Key takeaway: Path shows stages with key fields and guidance for success at each step. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: These notify users about large or important opportunities, but they do not explain stages or required actions. • Option C: These provide historical and analytical insights, not real-time, in-context guidance on what to do in a specific opportunity stage. • Option D: These help filter and display opportunities but do not explain the sales process or stage requirements.

stem: Which feature gives a sales team the ability to prioritize deals with recent updates in the List view and Kanban view?

options.text: Big Deal Alerts
Deal Change Highlights
Report Filters
Opportunity Path

sourceExplanation: Deal Change Highlights visually surface recent and important changes to opportunities, such as updates to key fields. These highlights appear directly in both List View and Kanban View, making it easy for sales reps to quickly identify recently updated deals, prioritize opportunities that need attention, and focus on changes without opening each record. Key takeaway: Deal Change Highlights show recent changes to amount and close date in list and Kanban views. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: These notify users when opportunities exceed a certain amount, but they don't highlight recent updates or help prioritize work in List or Kanban views. • Option C: Filters help limit which records appear in a report, but they don't visually emphasize recent changes in List or Kanban views. • Option D: Path guides users through stages and required fields, but it doesn't indicate or prioritize recent updates.

stem: In an approval process, which feature allows a user to temporarily assign their approval responsibilities to another user for a predefined time period?

options.text: Manager
Queue
Approval Rule
Delegated Approver

sourceExplanation: A Delegated Approver allows a user to temporarily transfer their approval responsibilities to another user. The delegation can be set for a specific time period, which is ideal for situations like vacations or extended absences. During this time, the delegated user can approve or reject requests on behalf of the original approver. Key takeaway: Delegated approvers can approve requests on behalf of another user. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A manager can be set as an approver in an approval process, but this does not provide temporary delegation or time-based reassignment. • Option B: Queues allow multiple users to act as approvers, but they are not meant for temporary, time-bound delegation of an individual's approvals. • Option C: Approval rules define when a record is submitted for approval, not who temporarily takes over approval responsibilities.

stem: Which component of an approval process defines the chain of approval, determines which records can advance, and specifies where to assign approval requests?

options.text: Process Definition Detail
Approval Actions
Entry Criteria
Approval Steps

sourceExplanation: Approval Steps define the sequence (chain) of approval in an approval process. Each step determines who the approver is (user, role, queue, manager, etc.). Approval steps control whether a record can advance to the next step or to final approval or rejection. This is also where Salesforce specifies where to assign approval requests at each stage of the process. Key takeaway: Approval steps define who approves and in which order, with step-specific criteria. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This contains high-level information about the approval process (name, description, object) but does not define the approval chain or routing. • Option B: These define what happens after an approval, rejection, recall, or submission (for example, field updates or email alerts), not who approves or how the record progresses. • Option C: Entry criteria only determine which records are eligible to enter the approval process; they do not define the approval flow or approvers.

stem: The sales reps at Cloud Kicks should be able to report on each other's account and opportunity records with the organization-wide default for Account and Opportunity both set to Private. What should a Platform Administrator do to achieve this?

options.text: Create manual sharing to share specific account and opportunity records between the sales reps.
Utilize Apex sharing to programmatically share records between a group of Sales Rep users.
Create an owner-based sharing rule for Accounts with sharing between a Public Group of Sales Reps and Read Only Opportunity Access.
Create an Account and Opportunity report to show any owned by each member of the Sales Team and save the report into a shared report folder.

sourceExplanation: With organization-wide defaults set to Private, users can only see records they own unless additional sharing is configured. Owner-based sharing rules are designed specifically to automatically share records owned by certain users or groups with other users or groups. By using a Public Group of Sales Reps, all reps can gain visibility into each other's Accounts. When Accounts are shared, Salesforce can also grant Read-Only access to related Opportunities, allowing sales reps to report on both Accounts and Opportunities across the team. This approach is scalable, automatic, and report-friendly, which is exactly what reporting across peers requires. Key takeaway: Owner-based sharing rules can share accounts and related opportunities with a group. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Manual sharing is record-by-record and does not scale. It would be impractical for ongoing reporting needs and requires constant maintenance as records change. • Option B: Apex sharing is unnecessary here. Declarative tools like sharing rules already meet the requirement and are preferred unless the logic is extremely complex. • Option D: Reports do not override data access. If users don't have access to the underlying records, the report will not display them—regardless of the folder's sharing settings.

stem: At Cloud Kicks, when a rep needs to seek additional support help, there's a series of actions the company wants to ensure are taken. The steps include sending an email and changing the status and owner of the case. What should a Platform Administrator use to give the reps an easy way to make these updates?

options.text: Macros with Quick Actions
Autolaunched Flows with Email Alerts
Case Assignment Rules
Quick Text with Email Templates

sourceExplanation: Macros are designed specifically for service reps to perform multiple actions with a single click. They can combine several steps such as sending an email, updating field values (like Status), and changing record ownership. Quick Actions can be embedded inside the macro to update the case quickly and consistently. This gives reps an easy, repeatable, and guided way to follow the required support process without forgetting steps. Key takeaway: Macros perform a series of actions (email, field updates) with one click in the console. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Autolaunched flows run in the background and are not ideal when reps need to manually initiate a series of actions at a specific moment. They also don't provide a simple, one-click rep experience like macros do. • Option C: Assignment rules automatically change ownership based on criteria, not when a rep explicitly requests additional support. They also can't handle sending emails and updating multiple fields as a guided rep action. • Option D: Quick Text and Email Templates help with email content only. They do not update case status, change ownership, or enforce a sequence of actions.

stem: The call center manager at Ursa Major Solar wants to provide agents with a case dashboard that can be drilled down by case origin, status, and owner. What should a Platform Administrator add to the dashboard to fulfill the request?

options.text: Bucket Column
Combination Chart
Dashboard Filter
Dashboard Widget

sourceExplanation: A Dashboard Filter allows users to dynamically filter all dashboard components by selected fields such as Case Origin, Status, and Owner. This gives call center agents and managers the ability to drill down interactively without creating multiple dashboards or reports. They can change filter values on the fly and immediately see updated metrics across the entire dashboard. Key takeaway: Dashboard filters allow drill-down by field values across components. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Bucket columns are used inside reports, not dashboards. They help group report values (for example, grouping multiple case origins together) but do not provide interactive filtering at the dashboard level. • Option B: A combination chart only controls how data is visualized (for example, bars and lines together). It does not allow users to drill down or filter by origin, status, or owner. • Option D: Widgets are used to add static content such as images, text, or links. They do not provide data filtering or drill-down functionality.

stem: The sales and service teams at Cloud Kicks would like to have more visibility into their pipeline and stay on top of every case. A Platform Administrator needs to quickly create dashboards for each of the teams but does not know where to start. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Use the Salesforce Labs Field Service Dashboards for service teams from AppExchange.
Use the Salesforce Labs CRM Dashboards for sales teams from AppExchange.
Manually create dashboards without using any prebuilt templates or packages.
Enable Einstein Analytics and build custom dashboards using advanced analytics tools.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce Labs provides prebuilt CRM Dashboards on the AppExchange that are designed specifically for Sales and Service visibility, including pipeline performance and case management. These dashboards can be installed quickly, require minimal configuration, and give administrators a strong starting point without having to design dashboards from scratch. They are ideal when the administrator needs to move fast and "doesn't know where to start." Key takeaway: Salesforce Labs apps on AppExchange provide free pre-built dashboards. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Field Service dashboards are intended for Field Service Lightning use cases (work orders, technicians, appointments), not standard service cases. They are not a good fit for general service teams managing cases. • Option C: This contradicts the requirement to quickly create dashboards and the fact that the administrator doesn't know where to start. Prebuilt dashboards are more efficient and follow best practices. • Option D: Einstein Analytics (CRM Analytics) is powerful but requires additional licensing, setup time, and expertise. This is unnecessary when standard Salesforce dashboards or Salesforce Labs templates meet the requirement.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Universal Containers is trying to deactivate a user who has left the company but is unable to do so. What is preventing the administrator from deactivating this user?

options.text: The user is part of an Account team.
The user is part of an Opportunity team.
The user is the running user of a dashboard.
The user is part of an active case assignment rule.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, a user cannot be deactivated if they are set as the running user of a dynamic dashboard. The running user determines data visibility for the dashboard, and Salesforce requires that this user be active. To deactivate the user, the administrator must first change the dashboard running user to another active user or remove the dashboard. Key takeaway: Dashboards whose running user is deactivated cannot refresh; change the running user first. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Being on an Account Team does not prevent user deactivation. Salesforce allows deactivation even if the user is listed on teams. • Option B: Similar to Account Teams, Opportunity Team membership does not block deactivation. The user can be inactive and still referenced historically. • Option D: Assignment rules reference users or queues, but they do not prevent user deactivation. The rule may stop working as intended, but Salesforce still allows the user to be deactivated.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks is trying to set up a new user but receives an error about a duplicate username when trying to save the user record. What is causing this error to happen?

options.text: The username has a restricted domain name within it.
The username was not configured in the format of an email address.
The email address and username must be unique across all Salesforce orgs.
The username must be unique across all Salesforce orgs.

sourceExplanation: In Salesforce, every username must be globally unique across all Salesforce organizations, not just within your org. Even if the email address or the user record is different, using a username that already exists anywhere in Salesforce will cause a duplicate username error. Usernames are in email format, but Salesforce treats them as a unique identifier, not just as an email. Key takeaway: Usernames must be unique across all Salesforce orgs, including sandboxes and orgs of other companies. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Salesforce does not restrict usernames by domain; any valid email format is allowed for usernames. • Option B: While usernames must be in email format, the system error in this case is about duplication, not format. • Option C: Only the username needs to be globally unique. The email address does not need to be unique across orgs; multiple users can have the same email in different Salesforce orgs.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Cloud Kicks needs to temporarily remove one dashboard from a shared folder with several dashboards to make some required changes. How should the administrator achieve this?

options.text: Edit the dashboard properties and move it to a private dashboards folder.
Remove the permission set to the dashboard from the users.
Remove View access to the shared folder.
Create a private group and add the dashboard to it.

sourceExplanation: Dashboards live in folders, and folder sharing controls access to all dashboards inside. To temporarily remove a single dashboard from a shared folder without affecting other dashboards in the folder, the administrator should move it to a private folder. This allows the admin to make changes safely without exposing the dashboard to all users in the shared folder. Once updates are complete, the dashboard can be moved back to the shared folder. Key takeaway: Moving a dashboard to a private folder hides it from others while you work on it. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Dashboards do not use permission sets to control access; they rely on folder-level access. Removing a permission set would have no effect on viewing the dashboard. • Option C: This would block all dashboards in the folder for all users, not just the one dashboard you want to update. It's too broad. • Option D: Dashboard access is controlled via folders, not groups. Creating a private group would not remove the dashboard from the original shared folder.

stem: Ursa Major Solar wants to see collaboration and updates across various Chatter groups, records, and announcements from the CEO in a single place. What should a Platform Administrator configure to achieve this?

options.text: Chatter Group
Chatter Feed
Chatter Stream
Chatter Daily Digest

sourceExplanation: Chatter Stream allows users to view multiple feeds in a single place, including Chatter groups, records they follow, and company-wide announcements, like posts from the CEO. It consolidates all relevant updates, making it easier for users to stay on top of collaboration and activity without navigating multiple pages. Key takeaway: Chatter Streams combine feeds from groups, records and people into one view. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Groups are specific communities of users around a topic or team. They only show posts from that group, not a consolidated view across all relevant feeds. • Option B: A feed is tied to a specific record, user, or group, not a consolidated stream. It doesn't provide a unified view of multiple sources. • Option D: This is an email summary sent once per day. It is not a live, interactive view and cannot be used as a central dashboard of updates.

stem: The CTO of AW Computing has defined a new policy for cases to improve customer satisfaction. All cases submitted with a Case Reason of Installation must be acknowledged immediately through email and assigned to the appropriate agents. Any cases that are still in the New status after 4 hours must be escalated to support management. A Platform Administrator has implemented auto-response rules. Which additional case management tool is necessary to meet this requirement?

options.text: Support Processes
Escalation Rules
Formulas
Entitlements

sourceExplanation: Escalation Rules in Salesforce are specifically designed to monitor cases against defined criteria and time frames. In this scenario, any case with status New that remains unresolved after 4 hours needs to be escalated to support management. Escalation Rules can automatically reassign the case, notify the manager, or trigger other actions when the time threshold is reached. Auto-response rules already handle the immediate acknowledgment email, but they do not manage timed escalations. Key takeaway: Auto-response rules acknowledge cases; escalation rules act on cases that remain unresolved. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Support Processes define which picklist values are available for Status and other fields. They do not perform automated escalations or notifications. • Option C: Formula fields can calculate or display values but cannot automatically escalate or trigger notifications. • Option D: Entitlements define the service levels and support contracts for cases but do not automatically escalate cases after a set time unless paired with Milestones, which is different from the 4-hour rule defined here.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants Agentforce to adapt its behavior based on real-time customer input. Which feature directly enables this capability?

options.text: Screen flow
Data Cloud
Tableau
Custom actions

sourceExplanation: Custom actions in Agentforce allow the agent to perform specific tasks or make decisions dynamically based on real-time input from the user. They can call APIs, update records, or retrieve information as the conversation progresses, enabling the agent to adapt its behavior depending on the customer's responses. This is the primary way Agentforce responds dynamically rather than following a static script. Key takeaway: Custom actions let agents perform tasks dynamically based on customer input. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Flows guide a user through a predefined set of screens and steps. They are not inherently dynamic based on real-time agent reasoning—they require the user to follow the flow. • Option B: Data Cloud stores and aggregates data but does not directly enable adaptive behavior in conversations. It provides the data, but adaptation requires actions or logic. • Option C: Tableau is a visual analytics tool and does not control real-time agent behavior or responses.

stem: The marketing director at Northern Trail Outfitters has requested that the Budget field be populated in order for the Lead Status field to be marked as qualified. Which tool should a Platform Administrator use to fulfill this request?

options.text: Lead Conversion
Require Field
Workflow Rule
Validation Rule

sourceExplanation: Validation rules enforce data integrity by preventing a record from being saved if certain conditions are not met. In this case, the requirement is that the Lead Status can only be set to Qualified if the Budget field is populated. A validation rule can check: AND(ISPICKVAL(LeadStatus, "Qualified"), ISBLANK(Budget__c)). This prevents saving the record unless the Budget field has a value, ensuring compliance with the marketing director's requirement. Key takeaway: Validation rules enforce conditional requirements such as Budget required for Qualified status. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Lead Conversion is a process that converts leads into Accounts, Contacts, and Opportunities. It does not enforce field requirements on the Lead record itself. • Option B: Making a field "Required" in the page layout ensures the field is populated on that layout, but users could bypass it via API, import, or another layout. Validation rules enforce it system-wide. • Option C: Workflow rules can trigger actions (like emails, field updates, tasks) when conditions are met but cannot prevent saving a record if a required field is missing.

stem: When a qualified lead is converted, what happens to its related records?

options.text: Open activities only are attached to the resulting contact, account, and opportunity records.
Campaign history is attached to the resulting contact, account, and opportunity records.
Records from custom objects are attached to the resulting contact, account, and opportunity records.
All activities are attached to the resulting contact, account, and opportunity records.

sourceExplanation: When a lead is converted in Salesforce, both open and completed activities (tasks and events) associated with the lead are transferred to the resulting Contact, Account, and Opportunity. This ensures a full activity history is preserved for sales and service teams after conversion. Key takeaway: On conversion, all activities (open and closed) move to the new contact, account and opportunity. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is outdated information. Salesforce now transfers all activities, not just open ones, during lead conversion. • Option B: While campaign history is also retained, this option does not cover activities, which are explicitly required in this question. • Option C: Custom object records are not automatically transferred during lead conversion. They require manual reassociation or automation (Flow, Process Builder, Apex).

stem: Service reps in a call center do not have assigned desks. They sit at any available desk and use the computer on that desk to access Salesforce. A Platform Administrator has been asked to streamline the login process so the reps do not have to authenticate each time they log in at a different computer. Which function should the administrator use to implement this request?

options.text: Permission Set
Trusted IP Ranges
Multi-factor Authentication
Custom Profile

sourceExplanation: Trusted IP Ranges allow users to log in from specific network locations without being prompted for extra authentication, such as verification codes or multi-factor authentication (MFA). In a hot desk environment, where service reps use different computers but are on the same internal network, setting the organization's network IPs as trusted removes the need for repeated logins or MFA prompts. This streamlines access while still maintaining security within the trusted network. Key takeaway: Trusted IP ranges remove identity verification prompts when logging in from the office network. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Permission sets grant additional object, field, or app permissions to users, but they do not control login authentication behavior. • Option C: MFA actually adds an extra login step to increase security, which is the opposite of streamlining access. • Option D: Profiles control what users can see and do in Salesforce, but do not bypass authentication requirements or handle login from multiple computers.

stem: A Platform Administrator at Ursa Major Solar imported records into an object by mistake. Which two tools should the administrator use to undo this import?

options.text: Data Import Wizard
Data Loader
Mass Delete Records
Weekly Data Export

sourceExplanation: • Data Loader: Allows bulk deletion of records based on criteria or record IDs, making it ideal for undoing a mistaken import. • Mass Delete Records: Can also delete large numbers of records at once, depending on the object type (standard objects like Accounts, Contacts, Leads, Cases, or custom objects if supported). Key takeaway: Data Loader and Mass Delete Records can remove wrongly imported records. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: The Data Import Wizard can insert or update records but cannot bulk delete imported records, so it cannot undo the import. • Option D: Data Export only backs up data; it does not provide any mechanism to remove or delete records.

stem: Cloud Kicks' management team is hoping to increase user productivity by switching to consoles instead of the current traditional Salesforce user interface. What should a Platform Administrator use to implement this request?

options.text: Screen Flow
App Builder
Omni-Channel
App Manager

sourceExplanation: App Manager in Salesforce is used to create and configure apps, including Sales Console apps. Console apps provide a tab-based interface optimized for productivity, allowing users to work with multiple records at once, quickly navigate between cases, opportunities, or accounts, and use split views and sub-tabs to reduce repetitive clicks. By creating a Sales Console app in App Manager, the administrator can provide a streamlined interface for sales or service teams. Key takeaway: App Manager creates console navigation apps for Sales or Service. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Flows automate processes or guide users through steps but do not create the interface or console experience. • Option B: App Builder is used to customize Lightning pages, record pages, and home pages—not to create full console apps. • Option C: Omni-Channel is used to route work (like cases or leads) to agents, not to build the console UI.

stem: A Platform Administrator needs to import 65,000 new records into a custom object. Which tool should the administrator use?

options.text: Data Loader
Data Import Wizard
Rest API
Schema Builder

sourceExplanation: Data Loader is built for high-volume data operations, supporting tens of thousands to millions of records in a single batch. It can insert, update, upsert, delete, or export records, making it ideal for importing 65,000 records into a custom object. Key takeaway: Data Loader handles up to 5 million records and supports custom and standard objects. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Designed for smaller volumes (up to 50,000 records per import) and mainly for standard objects. It cannot efficiently handle 65,000 records. • Option C: While the REST API can handle record creation programmatically, it is not as user-friendly for bulk imports and would require custom development for this volume. • Option D: Schema Builder is only for viewing and modifying object schema and relationships, not for importing data.

stem: Ursa Major Solar is noticing a decrease in deals with a cross-sell opportunity type and want to share all cross-sell opportunities with a team of subject matter experts in their organization. The company has different roles, and the organization-wide default for Opportunity is set to Private. How should the administrator accomplish this?

options.text: Create a new role for the subject matter experts and give them access to the records with an owner based sharing rule.
Enable territory management, assign the subject matter experts to the same territory, and give them access to the records with manual sharing.
Change the organization-wide default for Opportunity from Private to Public Read/Write to open up access for the subject matter experts.
Add the subject matter experts to a public group and give them access to the records with a criteria-based sharing.

sourceExplanation: Criteria-based sharing rules allow the administrator to automatically share records that meet certain conditions (e.g., Opportunity Type = Cross-sell) with a specific set of users. Adding the subject matter experts to a public group makes it easy to manage access and ensures they get read/write or read-only access without changing role hierarchy or org-wide defaults. This approach is scalable and maintainable because any new cross-sell opportunities will automatically be shared with the group. Key takeaway: Criteria-based sharing rules share records meeting criteria with public groups or roles. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Owner-based sharing only shares records owned by specific users, not all cross-sell opportunities. Creating a new role just for this purpose is unnecessary and more complex. • Option B: Territory management is more suited for sales territories, not simply for sharing opportunities based on type. Manual sharing is also not scalable for ongoing cross-sell opportunities. • Option C: This opens access to all opportunities, not just cross-sell ones, which could violate security and data privacy policies.

stem: An administrator at Cloud Kicks is building a flow that needs to search for records that meet certain conditions and store values from those records in variables for use later in the flow. What flow element should the administrator add?

options.text: Create Records
Get Records
Update Records
Assignment

sourceExplanation: The Get Records element in Flow Builder is specifically used to search for existing records in Salesforce that meet certain conditions. It can store field values from the found records in variables for use later in the flow, making it ideal for decision-making, calculations, or further updates. Key takeaway: Get Records retrieves data from Salesforce records for use in a flow. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This element is used to create new records, not retrieve existing ones. • Option C: This element is used to modify existing records, but it does not perform a search or store values for later use. • Option D: Assignment is used to set or update variable values within the flow, but it does not search Salesforce records.

stem: Ursa Major Solar offers amazing experiences for all of its employees. The employee engagement committee wants to post updates while restricting other employees from posting. What should the administrator create to meet this request?

options.text: Chatter Recommendations
Chatter Stream
Chatter Broadcast Group
Chatter Unlisted Group

sourceExplanation: A Chatter Broadcast Group allows only group managers or selected members to post messages, while all other members can view but not post. This setup is ideal for company announcements, updates, or committee communications where broad visibility is needed without allowing everyone to contribute posts. Key takeaway: Broadcast groups allow only managers and owners to post. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This feature provides automated content suggestions to users; it does not control posting permissions. • Option B: Chatter Stream allows users to follow specific feeds but does not restrict posting. • Option D: Unlisted groups are private and invisible to users who are not members. While they can restrict access, they do not provide the broadcast-only posting feature needed here.

stem: An administrator has assigned a permission set group with the multi-factor authentication for User Interface Logins permission and the multi-factor authentication for API Logins permission to a group of users. Which two prompts will happen when one of the users attempts to log in to Data Loader for the first time?

options.text: Users need to download and install an authenticator app on their mobile device.
Users need to enter a verification code from email or SMS, whichever has higher priority.
Users need to get a security taken from a trusted network using Reset My Security Token.
Users need to connect an authenticator app to their Salesforce account.

sourceExplanation: The multi-factor authentication (MFA) for API Logins permission requires users to use an authenticator app (like Salesforce Authenticator or Google Authenticator) when logging in through API-based tools like Data Loader. Users must download the app and connect it to their Salesforce account the first time they log in to complete MFA setup. Key takeaway: MFA for API logins requires users to connect an authenticator app to their account. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Salesforce MFA does not rely on email or SMS codes as the primary method for API logins; it requires an authenticator app. • Option C: Security tokens are separate from MFA. While a security token may still be needed to access API tools like Data Loader from untrusted networks, it is not part of the MFA prompt itself.

stem: Support reps at Cloud Kicks (CK) are reporting that when they try to close a case, the Closed option in the Case Status picklist is missing. CK has asked the administrator to find a solution. Why are the support reps unable to see the Closed option in the specified picklist?

options.text: The Support Process being used omits Closed as a status choice.
The Close Case page layout must be used to close a case.
The Show Closed Statuses in Case Status Field checkbox is set to the default.
The Case record type is missing Closed as a picklist value.

sourceExplanation: Support Processes control which Case Status picklist values are available for a particular record type. If the Closed status is not included in the support process assigned to the case record type, users will not see it as an option when trying to close the case. Updating the support process to include Closed will make it available to the reps. Key takeaway: Support processes determine the case status values available per record type. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: There is no special page layout required to close a case; the visibility of picklist values is determined by the support process, not the layout. • Option C: This checkbox controls display of closed cases in lists/reports, not which statuses are available in the picklist. • Option D: While record types can restrict available picklist values, the actual control comes from the support process associated with the record type, so the root cause is the support process itself.

stem: Cloud Kicks has a customer success agent going on leave and needs to change ownership on multiple cases. Which two users are able to fulfill this request?

options.text: A user with Read permission on the account.
A user with the Manage Cases permission.
A user with a manager role above the agent.
A user with the System Administrator profile.

sourceExplanation: • Manage Cases permission: Users with this permission can transfer case ownership for cases they do not own, regardless of their role in the hierarchy. This is typically granted via profiles or permission sets. • System Administrator profile: System Administrators have full access to all records, including the ability to change ownership of any case, making them able to reassign multiple cases at once. Key takeaway: Case ownership can be changed by users with Transfer permissions such as Manage Cases or System Administrator. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Read access is not sufficient to change case ownership. Users need edit rights or the Manage Cases permission. • Option C: Being a manager in the role hierarchy does not automatically grant case ownership change rights unless they also have Modify All or Manage Cases permissions.

stem: AW Computing would like to improve its Case Lightning record page by including: A filtered component to display a message in bold font when a Case is saved as a critical record type. A quick way to update the Account status from the Case layout. Which two components should an administrator use to satisfy these requests?

options.text: Related record
Record detail
Rich text
Related list

sourceExplanation: • Rich Text: Allows the administrator to display custom messages, instructions, or alerts on a Lightning record page. You can apply formatting like bold font and even configure component visibility filters so it only appears for critical Case record types. • Related Record: Provides a quick way to update fields on a related record (like Account status) directly from the Case Lightning page without navigating away. Key takeaway: Rich Text components show formatted messages; Related Record components edit a parent record. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Shows all fields from the record but does not allow conditional formatting or selectively displaying a message. • Option D: Displays lists of child records (like contacts or activities) but cannot show or edit a single related record field in a quick, inline way.

stem: Cloud Kicks' executives have noticed the Opportunity Expected Revenue field displays incorrect values. How should the administrator correct this?

options.text: Modify the closed won value associated with the stage.
Update the expected revenue associated with the stage.
Change the probability associated with the stage.
Adjust the forecast category associated with the stage.

sourceExplanation: The Opportunity Expected Revenue is calculated as: Expected Revenue = Amount × Probability (%). Each Opportunity Stage has an associated default probability. If the Expected Revenue is incorrect, it usually means the probability percentage assigned to that stage is wrong. Updating the probability for the stage will automatically recalculate the Expected Revenue for all opportunities in that stage. Key takeaway: Expected Revenue = Amount × Probability; probability defaults come from the stage. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Closed Won is a stage name, not a numeric value; changing it does not affect calculations. • Option B: There's no static "expected revenue per stage" field. Expected Revenue is calculated dynamically based on Amount × Probability. • Option D: The forecast category affects forecasting reports, but it does not change Expected Revenue calculations.

stem: An administrator at Universal Containers has been asked to prevent some users from accessing Salesforce from outside of their network. What are two considerations for this configuration?

options.text: Assign single sign-on to a permission set to allow users to log in when outside the network.
Restrict U2F Security Keys on the user's profile to enforce login hours.
Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request on the profile must be selected to enforce IP restrictions.
IP address restrictions are set on the profile for the org.

sourceExplanation: • Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request: Selecting this option ensures that IP restrictions are enforced for every login attempt, not just the initial login. Without this, users may bypass restrictions during a session if they were initially inside the allowed range. • IP address restrictions are set on the profile for the org: IP ranges defined on a profile limit the network locations from which users can log in. Only users logging in from allowed IP ranges can access Salesforce. Key takeaway: Profile login IP ranges restrict access; "Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request" applies them to every request. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: SSO does not override IP restrictions; it only changes the authentication method. • Option B: U2F keys are used for multi-factor authentication, not for enforcing login IP ranges or network restrictions.

stem: Sales users at Cloud Kicks are requesting that the data in the Industry field on the Account Object display on the Opportunity page layout. Which type of field should an administrator create to accomplish this?

options.text: Cross-object formula field
Custom Account field
Standard Account field
Master-detail relationship field

sourceExplanation: A cross-object formula field allows you to pull data from a parent object (in this case, Account) onto a child object (Opportunity). By creating a formula field on the Opportunity object that references Account.Industry, the Industry value from the related Account will automatically display on the Opportunity page layout. Key takeaway: Cross-object formulas display parent record fields on child records. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Creating a new field on the Account does not automatically display it on the Opportunity. You would still need a way to reference it on Opportunity. • Option C: The Industry field already exists as a standard field on Account, but standard fields cannot be directly displayed on another object without a formula or related mechanism. • Option D: Master-detail relationships define ownership and roll-up summary capabilities, but they do not display field values from the parent on the child object by themselves.

stem: An administrator installed a managed package that contains a permission set group. The permission set group that was installed includes Delete access on several objects, and the administrator needs to prevent users in the permission set group from being able to delete records. What should the administrator do to control Delete access?

options.text: Edit the profile for the users to remove Delete access from the objects.
Use a muting permission set with a permission set group to mute selected permissions.
Create a new role that prevents Delete permissions from rolling up to the users.
Create a new permission set that has Delete access deselected for the objects.

sourceExplanation: A muting permission set is specifically designed to remove (mute) specific permissions within a permission set group. By creating and assigning a muting permission set that removes Delete access on the relevant objects, the administrator can prevent users from deleting records without modifying the original managed package permission set group. Key takeaway: Muting permission sets remove permissions within a permission set group. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Editing standard profiles is not recommended, and profiles cannot selectively remove permissions granted by permission set groups. • Option C: Roles control record-level access, not object-level Delete permissions. • Option D: Creating a new permission set with Delete access deselected does not override the Delete access granted by the permission set group. The permission set group's permissions take precedence unless muted.

stem: Users at Cloud Kicks want to be able to create a task that will repeat every two weeks. What should an administrator do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Flow to create recurring tasks
Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks
Workflow rule to create recurring tasks
Turn on Recurring Activities

sourceExplanation: Recurring tasks are enabled in Setup > Activity Settings with the "Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks" setting. Once enabled, users can set a recurrence (for example, every two weeks) when creating a task. Key takeaway: Recurring tasks are enabled in Activity Settings. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A flow is unnecessary; recurring tasks are a native feature. • Option C: Workflow rules are retired and cannot create a repeating series of tasks. • Option D: There is no setting with this exact name; the Activity Settings option is "Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks" (recurring events are a separate setting).

stem: An administrator at Universal Containers needs a simple way to trigger an alert to the director of sales when opportunities reach an amount of $500,000. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Key Deals component on the homepage
Opportunity warnings in Kanban View
Set up Big Deal Alerts for the amount.
Enable Opportunity Update Reminders.

sourceExplanation: Big Deal Alerts are designed to notify users when an opportunity meets or exceeds a defined amount. The administrator can configure the alert specifically for $500,000, and direct it to the director of sales via email or Salesforce notification. This provides a simple, automated notification without requiring custom development or manual monitoring. Key takeaway: Big Deal Alerts notify specified users when opportunities exceed a threshold. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This only displays high-value deals in a dashboard-like component. It does not send alerts automatically. • Option B: Kanban warnings highlight opportunities visually based on criteria but do not trigger notifications to specific users. • Option D: Update reminders prompt users to update opportunity fields but do not alert other users when an opportunity reaches a certain amount.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to calculate how much revenue has been generated for each of its marketing campaigns. How should an administrator deliver this information?

options.text: Design a standard Campaign report and add the Value Won Opportunities in Campaign field.
Perform periodic data jobs to update campaign records.
Create a roll-up summary field on Opportunity to Campaign.
Add a Total Value field on Campaign and use a workflow rule to update the value when an opportunity is won.

sourceExplanation: Salesforce provides standard campaign reports that allow administrators to see the total revenue generated by each campaign. The "Value Won Opportunities in Campaign" field automatically sums the amount of Closed Won opportunities associated with the campaign. This method is real-time, accurate, and requires no custom fields or manual updates. Key takeaway: Campaign statistics such as "Value Won Opportunities" measure campaign revenue. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Manual data jobs are inefficient and error-prone, and not needed because standard reporting handles this automatically. • Option C: Roll-up summary fields cannot be created directly on Campaigns for opportunities unless the Campaign is the master in a master-detail relationship, which is not standard for Opportunities → Campaigns. • Option D: Workflow rules cannot update fields based on related object totals; this would require Process Builder or Flow, making it unnecessarily complex compared to standard reports.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to use Contact Hierarchy in its org to display Contact association. What should the administrator take into consideration regarding the Contact Hierarchy?

options.text: Sharing settings are ignored by contacts displayed in the Contact Hierarchy.
Contact Hierarchy is limited to only display 3,000 contacts at one time.
Contacts displayed in the Contact Hierarchy are limited to record-level access by user.
Customizing hierarchy columns changes the Recently Viewed Contacts list view.

sourceExplanation: Contact Hierarchy is designed to visually display how contacts are related within an account, helping users understand reporting structures or associations between contacts. The administrator should take into consideration that contacts displayed in the Contact Hierarchy are limited to record-level access by user. Users will only see contacts they have permission to view based on sharing rules, role hierarchy, or other access controls. This ensures sensitive information is protected while still showing relevant relationships. Key takeaway: Contact hierarchy respects the user's record access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Incorrect. The Contact Hierarchy respects sharing rules and record-level access. Users cannot see contacts they don't have permission to access. • Option B: Incorrect. There is no hard limit of 3,000 contacts in the hierarchy. It can display all contacts that the user has access to. • Option D: Incorrect. Customizing columns in the hierarchy only changes the columns shown in the hierarchy view, not any list views like Recently Viewed Contacts.

stem: The service manager at Ursa Major Solar wants to let customers know that they have received their cases via email and their website. Medium-priority and high-priority cases should receive different email notifications than low-priority cases. The administrator has created three email templates for this purpose. How should an administrator configure this requirement?

options.text: Create one auto-response rule. Configure three rule entry criteria and set a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule entry.
Include three assignment rules that fire when cases are created. Add a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule.
Add three auto-response rules. Configure one rule entry criteria for each rule and set a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule entry.
Configure one workflow rule that fires when cases are created. Add a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for the rule.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should create one auto-response rule with multiple rule entries, each with a filter for case priority (low, medium, high) and select the appropriate email template for each entry. This ensures customers receive the correct email based on the priority of their case without manual intervention. Key takeaway: One auto-response rule can contain several entries with different templates. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Assignment rules determine who owns a case, not which email template is sent. They cannot send auto-response emails based on case priority. • Option C: Salesforce only allows one active auto-response rule per object. You cannot create multiple active rules; instead, you create multiple rule entries within a single rule. • Option D: Workflow rules can send email alerts, but auto-response rules are specifically designed for customer notifications. Using workflow is unnecessary and less efficient for standard case auto-response requirements.

stem: Users have noticed that when they click on a report in a dashboard to view the report details, the values in the report are different from the values displayed on the dashboard. What are the two reasons this is likely to occur?

options.text: The current user does not have access to the report folder.
The dashboard needs to be refreshed.
The report needs to be refreshed.
The running dashboard user and viewer have different permissions.

sourceExplanation: • The dashboard needs to be refreshed: Dashboards show the results from the last time they were run. If new data has been added since the last refresh, the dashboard totals may differ from the live report. • The running dashboard user and viewer have different permissions: Dashboards respect the running user's data access, while reports display data according to the viewer's permissions. Differences in access can cause numbers to vary. Key takeaway: Dashboard data reflects the last refresh and the running user's access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: If the user cannot access the report folder, they would not be able to view the report at all, so this cannot explain the discrepancy. • Option C: Reports always display live, real-time data, so refreshing the report does not change the underlying data shown versus the dashboard.

stem: An administrator wants to create a form in Salesforce for users to fill out when they lose a client. Which automation tool supports creating a wizard to accomplish this goal?

options.text: Process Builder
Flow Builder
Approval Process
Outbound Message

sourceExplanation: Flow Builder allows administrators to create screen flows, which act as interactive wizards with multiple screens, questions, and guided steps. With Flow Builder, the admin can design screens, input fields, and decision logic so users are guided step-by-step and all required information is captured efficiently. Key takeaway: Screen flows create guided multi-screen forms (wizards). Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Process Builder automates backend actions based on record changes but cannot create user-facing forms or wizards. • Option C: Approval Process routes records for approvals. It does not provide a form for users to fill out. • Option D: Outbound Message sends data to external systems automatically. It cannot create interactive forms or collect user input.

stem: An administrator wants to trigger a follow-up task for the opportunity owner when they close an opportunity as won, and another task after 60 days to check in with the customer. Which automation tool should the administrator use?

options.text: Flow Builder
Assignment Rule
Field Update
Outbound Message

sourceExplanation: The administrator can build a record-triggered flow on the Opportunity object: create a task immediately for the opportunity owner when the stage is set to Won, and schedule a follow-up task for 60 days later to check in with the customer. This approach is flexible, requires no code, and supports both immediate and time-based actions. Key takeaway: Record-triggered flows can schedule paths to create a task 60 days later. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Assignment rules are used to assign ownership of leads or cases automatically. They cannot create scheduled follow-up tasks. • Option C: Field updates can change the value of a field when a record meets certain criteria, but they cannot trigger tasks, either immediate or scheduled. • Option D: Outbound messages are used to send information to external systems, not to create tasks or follow-up actions within Salesforce.

stem: The administrator at Cloud Kicks created a new field for tracking returns on their new cloud shoe. A user has submitted a case to the administrator indicating that the new field is unavailable. Which two steps should an administrator do to troubleshoot this issue?

options.text: Run the setup audit trail for the organization.
Update the organization-wide defaults for the object.
Review the field-level security of the field for the user profile.
Ensure that the page layout for the user's profile has been updated.

sourceExplanation: • Review the field-level security of the field for the user profile: If the field is hidden via field-level security, users will not see it even if it exists on the object. • Ensure that the page layout for the user's profile has been updated: Fields must be added to the page layout assigned to the user's profile for them to appear on the record page. These steps ensure the field is both visible and accessible to the user. Key takeaway: Missing fields are usually caused by FLS or page layout configuration. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: The setup audit trail only tracks administrative changes in the org. It does not affect or reveal field visibility for users. • Option B: Organization-wide defaults control record-level access, not field-level visibility. Changing them will not make the field appear on the page.

stem: AW Computing has six sales teams in a region. These teams always consist of the same account manager, engineer, and assistant. What should the administrator configure to make it easier for teams to collaborate with the same customer?

options.text: Create a queue for each team and assign account ownership to the queue.
Enable account teams and show the users how to set up a default account team.
Enable and configure standard opportunity teams with splits.
Propose the users manually share all their accounts with their teammates.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should enable account teams and show users how to set up a default account team. This allows each sales team (account manager, engineer, and assistant) to automatically be added to new accounts with the proper roles, making collaboration consistent and efficient. Key takeaway: Default account teams automatically add the same team to accounts. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Queues are used for leads, cases, or custom objects, not standard accounts. Assigning account ownership to a queue is not supported. • Option C: Opportunity Teams manage collaboration at the opportunity level, not the account level. They do not automatically share account information among team members. • Option D: Manual sharing is inefficient and error-prone, especially for teams that consistently work together on the same accounts. Default account teams automate this process.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has a custom quick action on Account that creates a new Case. How should an administrator make the quick action available on the Salesforce mobile app?

options.text: Add the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience action to the page layout.
Create a custom Lightning App with the action.
Include the action in the Salesforce Mobile Navigation menu.
Modify compact Case page layout to include the action.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should add the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience action to the page layout. This ensures the custom quick action is visible and usable in both the Salesforce mobile app and Lightning Experience. Key takeaway: Quick actions appear in mobile from the page layout action section. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Creating a Lightning App does not automatically add quick actions to page layouts or make them available on mobile. Quick actions must be added to the page layout itself. • Option C: The mobile navigation menu controls which objects and tabs appear in the mobile app. It does not make quick actions available. • Option D: Compact layouts control which fields appear in highlights panels, not quick actions. Adding the action here will not make it usable in the mobile app.

stem: Universal Containers has a Contact Lightning record page with a component that shows LinkedIn data. The sales team would like to only show this component to those users who have the Sales User profile when they are on their mobile phones. Which two solutions should the administrator use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Filter the component visibility with User> Profile > Name = Sales User.
Filter the component visibility with User> Role > Name = Sales User.
Filter the component visibility with View = Mobile/Tablet.
Filter the component visibility with Form Factor = Phone.

sourceExplanation: • Filter by User > Profile > Name = Sales User: Ensures only users with the Sales User profile see the component. • Filter by Form Factor = Phone: Ensures the component only appears when the user is on a mobile device. These two filters together satisfy the requirement: showing the LinkedIn component only to Sales Users on mobile devices. Key takeaway: Component visibility can filter on User Profile and Form Factor. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Role is different from Profile. Users may have the Sales User profile but not the matching role. Using Role would not guarantee correct visibility. • Option C: View is not a valid filter for component visibility. The correct filter to detect device type is Form Factor, not View.

stem: Which two objects are customizable in the Stage Setup Flow?

options.text: Leads
Campaigns
Campaign Members
Opportunities

sourceExplanation: • Leads: Admins can define stages for Lead qualification and conversion. • Opportunities: Admins can define sales stages, probabilities, and guidance for opportunities to align with the sales process. Key takeaway: Stage setup flows help configure Lead and Opportunity stage values.
