Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Campaigns do not have sales stages; they track marketing initiatives, so they cannot be customized using Stage Setup Flow. • Option C: Campaign Members track Lead or Contact participation in campaigns. They do not have stages, so they cannot be modified in Stage Setup Flow.

stem: Which tool should an administrator use to identify and fix potential session vulnerabilities?

options.text: Setup Audit Trail
Field History Tracking
Organization-Wide Defaults
Health Check

sourceExplanation: Health Check is a Salesforce tool that scans an organization's security settings against Salesforce baseline security standards and identifies vulnerabilities, including session security issues. The administrator should use Health Check to review current security settings and implement recommended fixes to improve the organization's overall security posture. Key takeaway: Health Check compares security settings against a baseline standard. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: The Setup Audit Trail tracks administrative changes in the org but does not identify security vulnerabilities or provide recommendations. • Option B: Field History Tracking monitors changes to specific fields for auditing purposes. It does not assess session security or vulnerabilities. • Option C: Organization-Wide Defaults control record-level access but do not provide a comprehensive review of session settings or security vulnerabilities.

stem: AW Computing needs to capture a loss reason in a rich text field when an opportunity is closed lost. How should an administrator configure this requirement?

options.text: Select the required Checkbox next to the Loss Reason field on the page layout.
Create a validation rule to display an error if stage is closed lost and Loss Reason is blank.
Configure a workflow rule to display an error if Loss Reason is blank.
Check the required checkbox on the Loss Reason field in Object Manager.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should create a validation rule that displays an error if the Stage is "Closed Lost" and the Loss Reason field is blank. This ensures that users cannot save the opportunity without entering a reason for the loss. Key takeaway: Rich text fields cannot be required on layouts; validation rules enforce requirements. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Making a field required on the page layout does not enforce conditional requirements; users could still bypass it in other contexts, such as inline editing or API updates. • Option C: Workflow rules cannot display errors to users during record save; they are used to automate actions like field updates, emails, or tasks. • Option D: Making the field universally required forces users to fill it for all opportunities, not just when the Stage is Closed Lost. This does not meet the conditional requirement.

stem: The standard Lead Rating field has picklist values of Hot, Warm, and Cold. A list of new leads imported without errors even though several records had the value of Unrated in the Rating field. How were these records added without error?

options.text: A global picklist value set was used to populate the picklist.
The Restricted picklist checkbox was unchecked.
The Add to All Record Types checkbox was selected.
Field level security was set to Visible for all profiles.

sourceExplanation: The records with the value "Unrated" were added without error because the Restricted picklist checkbox was unchecked. This allows users and imports to include values that are not defined in the picklist, bypassing the standard options (Hot, Warm, Cold). Key takeaway: Unrestricted picklists accept values not included in the defined list. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Using a global value set does not allow undefined values if the picklist is restricted. It only centralizes picklist values across objects. • Option C: This ensures the picklist appears in all record types, but does not allow values outside the picklist. • Option D: Field-level security controls who can see or edit the field, but it does not affect which values are allowed.

stem: The administrator at Cloud Kicks updated the custom object Event to include a lookup field to the primary contact for the event. When running an event report, they want to reference fields from the associated contact record. What should the administrator do to pull contact fields into the custom report?

options.text: Edit the custom Event report type and add fields related via lookup.
Use a dashboard with filters to show Event and contact data as requested.
Configure formula fields on Event to populate contact information.
Create a new report type with Event as the primary object and Contact as a related object.

sourceExplanation: When the primary object of a custom report type has a lookup field, the administrator can edit the report type layout and use "Add fields related via lookup" to bring in fields from the looked-up record (here, the primary Contact). No new report type is required. Key takeaway: Custom report types can include fields related via lookup. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Dashboards display report data; they cannot add fields that the report type does not expose. • Option C: Formula fields work but require one field per value and are unnecessary maintenance. • Option D: Contact is the parent (lookup) of Event, not a child, so it cannot be added as the related "B" object in a report type; fields via lookup is the correct method.

stem: Cloud Kicks generates leads for its different product categories (shoes, apparel, and accessories) through many different sources. While some lead sources are used for all three categories, other lead sources are specific to a single category. The VP of marketing requests that only the proper lead sources be displayed based on the product category chosen. How should the administrator configure Salesforce to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a page layout for each category and filter the Lead Source field based on category.
Create business processes and record types for each of the three product categories.
Create a single lead process, then create record types for each product category.
Create a dependency between the Product Category field and Lead Source field.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should create a dependency between the Product Category field and the Lead Source field. This ensures that when a user selects a specific product category (shoes, apparel, or accessories), only the lead sources relevant to that category are displayed, improving data accuracy and user experience. Key takeaway: Dependent picklists filter values based on a controlling field. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Page layouts cannot dynamically filter picklist values. Multiple layouts would be cumbersome and do not enforce dynamic dependencies. • Option B: Business processes define stage picklists for objects like Leads, Opportunities, or Cases, not field-level picklist dependencies. • Option C: Record types can assign different picklist values, but using them for every category is more complex and requires users to select the record type before choosing the category. Field dependency is simpler and dynamic.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters uses web-to-case to convert support requests submitted through its website into cases. The support team wants to automatically send an email containing password reset instructions to customers when the case subject contains the words "forgot" and "password." What two options should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Auto-response rule
Email-to-case
Password reset template
Email template

sourceExplanation: The administrator should create an auto-response rule to automatically send emails when cases meet the specified criteria, and create an email template containing the password reset instructions to ensure consistent messaging. This combination provides automated, targeted responses for cases needing password assistance. Key takeaway: Auto-response rules with email templates send targeted replies to web-to-case submitters. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Email-to-case is for creating cases from incoming emails, not for sending automated responses based on case content. • Option C: The standard password reset template is for user password resets via login, not for sending custom instructions through case automation.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to track shoe designs by product because there can be multiple designs for one product across various stages. They need to know how many designs have been created for a given product on the product record. Which two steps should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Configure a custom lookup field for shoe designs on the Product object.
Use the standard object for designs.
Add a custom master-detail field for shoe designs on the Design object.
Create a custom object for shoe designs.

sourceExplanation: The administrator should create a custom Design object to store individual design records, then add a master-detail field on this object linking to the Product object. This structure enables roll-up summary fields on the Product record to count associated designs automatically. Key takeaway: Master-detail enables roll-up summary counts on the parent record. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Lookup fields don't support roll-up summaries, preventing automatic counting of designs per product. • Option B: There is no standard object for shoe designs in Salesforce; a custom object must be created.

stem: The business development team at Cloud Kicks thinks the Account creation process has too many fields to fill out and the page feels cluttered. They have requested the administrator to simplify the process. Which automation tool should an administrator use?

options.text: Flow Builder
Workflow Rule
Approval Process
Validation Rule

sourceExplanation: The administrator should use Flow Builder to create a screen flow for Account creation. This provides a guided, step-by-step interface where users enter only essential fields, reducing clutter and improving the user experience. Key takeaway: Screen flows simplify record creation by collecting only needed data. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Workflow rules automate backend processes but don't modify the data entry interface. • Option C: Approval processes manage record review workflows but don't simplify field entry. • Option D: Validation rules enforce data quality but don't reduce field count or page complexity.

stem: A team of support users at Cloud Kicks is helping inside sales reps make follow-up calls to prospects that filled out an interest form online. The team currently does not have access to the Lead object. How should an administrator provide proper access?

options.text: Configure permission sets
Set up Manual sharing
Create a new profile
Assign a new role

sourceExplanation: Permission sets allow an administrator to grant additional access to objects, fields, and permissions without changing a user's profile. Since the support team lacks access to the Lead object, assigning a permission set with the appropriate object-level permissions (e.g., Read, Create) is the most flexible and scalable solution. Key takeaway: Permission sets extend object access for specific users. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Manual sharing only grants access to specific records, not to the entire object. • Option C: While a new profile could be created, it is excessive and less flexible than using permission sets for granting object access to a specific team. • Option D: Roles control record visibility, not object-level permissions. Changing a user's role will not grant access to an object if their profile restricts it.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters has hired interns to enter Leads into Salesforce and has requested a way to identify these new records from existing Leads. What approach should an administrator take to meet this requirement?

options.text: Set up Web-to-Lead for the interns' use.
Update the active Lead Assignment Rules.
Define a record type and assign it to the interns.
Create a separate Lead Lightning App.

sourceExplanation: Creating a Lead record type specifically for interns allows administrators to differentiate and track intern-created Leads easily. Record types can also control page layouts, picklist values, and business processes, ensuring consistency and clear identification. Key takeaway: Record types can differentiate records and control layouts and picklists. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Web-to-Lead is for external web forms, not for manual entry by interns. • Option B: Assignment rules route Leads to owners but do not inherently differentiate who entered them. • Option D: A separate app changes the user interface but does not automatically tag or differentiate Leads by their creator.

stem: Cloud Kicks users are seeing error messages when they use one of their screen flows. The error messages are confusing but could be resolved if the users entered more information on the account before starting the flow. How should the administrator address this issue?

options.text: Uncheck the End User Flow Errors box in Setup.
Remove validation rules so that the users are able to proceed without complete records.
Use a fault connector and display a screen with text explaining what went wrong and how to correct it.
Create a permission set to allow users to bypass the error.

sourceExplanation: Implementing a fault connector with a custom error screen provides users with clear, actionable guidance when an error occurs, improving the user experience and ensuring they know how to correct the issue before proceeding. Key takeaway: Fault paths let flows handle errors gracefully with user-friendly messages. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Unchecking the End User Flow Errors box only hides error messages, which could lead to further confusion and data integrity issues. • Option B: Removing validation rules would compromise data quality and allow incomplete records to be saved. • Option D: Permissions do not address flow errors caused by missing or invalid data.

stem: The administrator at Cloud Kicks writes an assignment rule to send all cases created via email or the web to the Automated Cases Queue. Any manually created cases should be owned by the agent creating them; however, the manually created cases now show the administrator as the owner. What will the administrator find when troubleshooting this issue?

options.text: The Owner field is missing on the webform and email template.
The Assignment Rule checkbox is selected by default.
Another assignment rule is giving ownership to the administrator.
An escalation rule is changing the case owner on case creation.

sourceExplanation: When the Assignment Rule checkbox is selected by default on manually created cases, assignment rules are applied to all new cases—including those created manually—causing them to be reassigned per the rule instead of remaining with the creating agent. Key takeaway: "Assign using active assignment rules" default setting applies rules to manually created cases. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This issue applies to manually created cases, not web/email submissions. • Option C: While possible, the most common cause is the default checkbox being selected. • Option D: Escalation rules trigger after a case is created based on time-based criteria, not immediately upon creation.

stem: An administrator is on a tight deadline to create dashboards for the sales and marketing teams at AW Computing. What should the administrator do to meet the deadline without increasing the budget?

options.text: Check the AppExchange for a prebuilt solution that can be easily customized.
Train someone on the sales and marketing teams to build dashboards.
Hire a consultant to build the custom dashboards.
Build the dashboards manually to meet the deadline.

sourceExplanation: AppExchange offers prebuilt dashboard solutions that can be quickly installed and customized, saving significant time and resources while staying within budget. Key takeaway: AppExchange provides pre-built dashboard solutions at little or no cost. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Training takes time and would likely delay dashboard delivery. • Option C: Hiring a consultant would increase costs, violating the budget constraint. • Option D: Manual creation is time-consuming and may not be feasible under a tight deadline.

stem: An administrator supporting a global team of Salesforce users has been asked to configure company settings. Which two options should the administrator configure?

options.text: Default Language
Currency Locale
Login Hours
Password Policy

sourceExplanation: • Default Language – Sets the primary language for the organization, ensuring consistency across global users. • Currency Locale – Defines the default currency and formatting for monetary values, essential for international operations. Key takeaway: Company Settings include default language, locale and currency locale. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Login Hours control when individual users can log in, not a global company setting. • Option D: Password Policy is part of security settings, not a general company configuration.

stem: An administrator at Cloud Kicks wants to deactivate a user who has left the company. What are two reasons that would prevent a user from being deactivated?

options.text: The user is the highest role in the role hierarchy.
The user is the sole recipient of a workflow email alert.
The user is part of a territory hierarchy.
The user is in a custom hierarchy field.

sourceExplanation: • The user is the sole recipient of a workflow email alert – Salesforce prevents deactivation until another active user is added as a recipient. • The user is in a custom hierarchy field – If the user is referenced in a custom hierarchy field (e.g., Manager), that reference must be updated before deactivation. Key takeaway: Users referenced in workflow email alerts or custom hierarchy fields cannot be deactivated. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This does not block deactivation; the role can be reassigned or left empty. • Option C: Territory membership alone does not prevent deactivation.

stem: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar has created a custom report type and built a report for the sales operations team. However, none of the users are able to access the report. Which two options could cause this issue?

options.text: The custom report type is in development.
The user's profile is missing View access.
The org has reached its limit for custom report types.
The report is saved in a private folder.

sourceExplanation: • The custom report type is in development – Users cannot access reports based on a report type that is still in development. • The report is saved in a private folder – Reports in private folders are only visible to the owner, preventing other users from accessing them. Key takeaway: Report types in development are only visible to administrators; private folders limit access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: While this could restrict data visibility, it does not fully prevent access to the report itself. • Option C: This would prevent creation of new report types, not access to existing ones.

stem: The administrator has created new users for ten new employees at Northern Trail Outfitters. Why are these users unable to view the account tab in the Salesforce org?

options.text: Organization-wide defaults are set to private.
Users' profile requires permission to the Account object.
Users' profile requires a sharing rule for Accounts.
Users' roles are low on the role hierarchy.

sourceExplanation: Users cannot view an object tab unless their profile grants at least Read permission for that object. The issue is object-level access, not record visibility. Key takeaway: Object permissions on the profile or permission sets are required to see tabs. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: OWD controls record-level access, not tab visibility. • Option C: Sharing rules grant record access, not object-level permissions. • Option D: Role hierarchy affects record visibility, not object-level tab access.

stem: DreamHouse Realty regularly holds open houses for the selling of both houses and condominiums. For condominium open houses, there are a few extra steps that need to be taken. Agents need to be able to submit requests and receive approvals from the homeowners' association. How can the administrator ensure these extra steps only appear when creating open house records for condominiums?

options.text: Create one page layout. Use record types to ensure the proper status picklist values display.
Create two page layouts. Use processes and record types to display the appropriate picklist values.
Create one page layout. Use business processes to ensure the proper status picklist values display.
Create two page layouts, one with a House Status field and the other with a Condominium Status field.

sourceExplanation: Using record types to differentiate between house and condominium open houses allows the assignment of distinct page layouts and processes. This ensures that condominium-specific steps (like approvals) are only presented for condominium records. Key takeaway: Record types with different page layouts and processes tailor data entry. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A single layout cannot hide or show extra steps conditionally. • Option C: Business processes control picklist values but not layout visibility. • Option D: Without record types, Salesforce cannot automatically assign the correct layout.

stem: AW Computing (AWC) occasionally works with independent contractors, who the company stores as Contacts in Salesforce. Contractors often change agencies, and AWC wants to maintain the historical accuracy of the record. What should AWC use to track Contacts?

options.text: Enable Contacts to multiple Accounts.
Create a junction object to track many-to-many relationship.
Create a new Contact record for each agency.
Use a partner community to track the Contacts.

sourceExplanation: Enabling Contacts to Multiple Accounts allows a single Contact to be associated with multiple Accounts (agencies) over time, preserving historical relationships without duplicating records. Key takeaway: Contacts to Multiple Accounts tracks relationships with several accounts over time. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This adds unnecessary complexity; Salesforce already provides native functionality for this. • Option C: This duplicates Contact records and loses historical tracking. • Option D: Partner communities are for external user access, not for tracking Contact relationships.

stem: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is creating a validation rule. Which two functions should the administrator use when creating a validation rule?

options.text: Error condition formula
Error message location
Rule active date
Formula return type

sourceExplanation: • Error condition formula – Defines the logic that triggers the validation rule. • Error message location – Specifies where the error message appears (top of page or next to field). Key takeaway: Validation rules need an error condition formula and an error message location. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Validation rules do not have an active date setting; they are simply activated or deactivated. • Option D: Validation rule formulas must return a Boolean (true/false); the return type is not selectable.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to update a screen flow so that if the checkbox field High Value Customer is set to true, the first screen is skipped and the user is directed to the second screen. How should the administrator configure the decision element?

options.text: Use the contains operator and (!$GlobalConstant.False) as the value.
Use the equals operator and "High Value Customer" as the value.
Use the equals operator and (!$GlobalConstant.True) as the value.
Use the contains operator and "High Value Customer" as the value.

sourceExplanation: A checkbox is a Boolean field. In the Decision element, the outcome condition should be High Value Customer Equals {!$GlobalConstant.True}. When the condition is met, the flow routes directly to the second screen. Key takeaway: Checkbox conditions use {!$GlobalConstant.True} or {!$GlobalConstant.False}. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: "Contains" is a text operator, and testing for False would do the opposite of what is required. • Option B: The value must be the Boolean constant True, not the field label as text. • Option D: "Contains" is a text operator and the text value is incorrect.

stem: Cloud Kicks has the organization-wide sharing default set to private on the Shoe object. The sales manager should be able to view a report containing shoe records for all of the sales reps on their team. Which three items should the administrator configure to provide appropriate access to the report?

options.text: Role Hierarchy
Report Subscription
Custom Report Type
Field-Level Security
Folder Access

sourceExplanation: • Role Hierarchy – With private OWD, the role hierarchy allows managers to view subordinates' records. • Field-Level Security – Ensures the manager can see the necessary fields in the report. • Folder Access – The manager needs at least Viewer access to the folder where the report is stored. Key takeaway: Report access requires record access, FLS and folder access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Subscriptions automate report delivery but do not grant access. • Option C: Report types define available objects and fields, but do not control record or report access.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has deployed my domain. The Chief Marketing Officer wants to make sure that all of the Salesforce users log in using the branded login URL. There needs to be a grace period for the user's bookmarks to be updated. How should the administrator configure the policies in my domain settings?

options.text: Set the login policy to require login from https://nto.my.salesforce.com
Set the Redirect policy to Do Not redirect.
Set the login policy to prevent login from https://login.salesforce.com
Set the redirect policy to Redirect with a warning to the same page within the domain.

sourceExplanation: Setting the redirect policy to "Redirect with a warning" gradually transitions users to the branded URL while providing a grace period for them to update bookmarks. Key takeaway: "Redirect with a warning" gives users time to update bookmarks. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This immediately blocks non-branded URL logins, leaving no grace period. • Option B: Users would not be redirected, defeating the goal. • Option C: This also blocks access immediately without a transition period.

stem: What should an administrator use as an identifier when importing and updating records from a separate financial system?

options.text: Record ID
Rich Text field
External ID
Auto-Number field

sourceExplanation: An External ID field allows matching and updating records based on a unique identifier from the external system, ensuring data integrity during imports. Key takeaway: External ID fields match records from external systems in upsert operations. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Salesforce record IDs are not present in external systems. • Option B: Not designed as a unique identifier. • Option D: Auto-numbers are generated by Salesforce and cannot be set from an external system.

stem: The Support team at Ursa Major Solar occasionally views shipments from an application external to Salesforce. What is the best way to configure the UI to allow for this functionality?

options.text: Use external objects and add a custom tab to the Support App for support agents.
Filter by a single shipment record type in the list view.
Add the Manage List Views permission for support users.
Split views are only available on standard objects.

sourceExplanation: External objects (via Salesforce Connect) allow real-time access to external data. Adding a custom tab provides a seamless way for agents to view shipment data within Salesforce. Key takeaway: External objects with Salesforce Connect display external data in real time. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Record types only apply to Salesforce data, not external data. • Option C: This allows creating list views but does not provide access to external data. • Option D: Split views are available for both standard and custom objects, but not relevant for external data access.

stem: The marketing team wants a new picklist value added to the Campaign Member Status field for the upsell promotional campaign. Which two solutions should the administrator use to modify the picklist field values?

options.text: Modify the picklist value on the Campaign Member Statuses related list.
Mass modify the Campaign Member Statuses related list.
Add the Campaign Member Statuses related list to the Page Layout.
Edit the picklist values for the Campaign Status in Object Manager.

sourceExplanation: • Modify the picklist value on the Campaign Member Statuses related list – Campaign Member Status values are managed per campaign via this related list. • Add the Campaign Member Statuses related list to the Page Layout – Ensures the marketing team can view and edit status values. Key takeaway: Campaign member statuses are managed per campaign in the related list. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This updates existing member records, not the picklist values themselves. • Option D: Campaign Status is a different field; Campaign Member Status is not managed in Object Manager.

stem: At Universal Containers, users would like to be able to share Salesforce records with other members of their team, while collaborating around general topics as well. Which are two considerations for enabling this functionality?

options.text: An administrator needs to create a group to enable record sharing.
Object layouts should be configured to include the groups related list.
The Add Record action must be configured in the group publisher.
Collaboration groups are created automatically for every department.

sourceExplanation: To share records with Chatter groups, the administrator adds the Groups related list to the object's page layouts and adds the "Add Record" action to the group publisher layout. Users can then add records to groups and collaborate on them together with general topics. Key takeaway: Groups related list and Add Record publisher action enable record sharing in groups. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Users create their own groups; the administrator does not need to create a group to enable record sharing. • Option D: Collaboration groups are never created automatically for departments.

stem: Universal Containers created a new job posting on the first of the month. It triggered a process scheduled action that will send a Chatter post to the department VP in 30 days if the position is still open and the status is not equal to Interviewing. On the 10th of the month, an applicant interviews, and the job posting status is updated to Interviewing. What will happen to the Chatter post in this situation?

options.text: The pending Chatter post will be paused.
The pending Chatter post will be sent on the 10th of the month.
The pending Chatter post will be sent in 30 days.
The pending Chatter post will be canceled.

sourceExplanation: Scheduled actions evaluate the record's criteria at the execution time. Since the status changed to Interviewing, the criteria are no longer met, and the scheduled Chatter post is canceled. Key takeaway: Scheduled actions are removed if the record no longer meets criteria. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Scheduled actions do not pause; they are canceled if criteria are not met. • Option B: Scheduled actions run at the scheduled time, not when criteria change. • Option C: It will not be sent because the criteria are no longer satisfied.

stem: Cloud Kicks is working on a better way to track its product shipments utilizing Salesforce. Which field type should an administrator use to capture coordinates?

options.text: Geofence
Custom address
External lookup
Geolocation

sourceExplanation: A Geolocation field stores latitude and longitude coordinates, ideal for mapping and tracking shipment locations. Key takeaway: Geolocation fields store latitude and longitude. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Defines a geographic boundary but does not store coordinates on a record. • Option B: Stores street address details, not coordinates. • Option C: Links to an external object, unrelated to geospatial data.

stem: The administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters has been using a spreadsheet to track assigned licenses and permission sets. What feature can be used to track this in Salesforce?

options.text: Lightning Usage App
Permission Set Groups
User Report
Login History

sourceExplanation: User Reports allow administrators to report on assigned licenses, permission sets, profiles, and roles, replacing manual spreadsheets. Key takeaway: User reports can show licenses, profiles, roles and assigned permission sets. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Tracks feature adoption, not license assignments. • Option B: Simplifies assignment but does not provide tracking across all users. • Option D: Shows login activity, not license assignments.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to update data with information from their data warehouse. What should an administrator do to accomplish this?

options.text: Use a unique ID field to match records between the systems.
Use the data loader to match records between the systems.
Use an external object to match records between the systems.
Use an external ID field to match records between the systems.

sourceExplanation: An External ID field allows reliable matching and updating of records based on identifiers from the external data warehouse. Key takeaway: External IDs match records with a data warehouse during updates. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A standard unique ID (like Record ID) is not available externally. • Option B: The Data Loader is a tool, but it still requires an External ID for matching. • Option C: External objects are for real-time viewing, not for updating Salesforce records.

stem: Which tool should an administrator use to review recent configuration changes made in their org?

options.text: Field History Tracking
Debug Logs
Critical Updates
Setup Audit Trail

sourceExplanation: The Setup Audit Trail logs configuration changes (who made them, when, and what changed), providing a complete audit history. Key takeaway: Setup Audit Trail shows who changed what configuration and when. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Tracks changes to field values on records, not configuration. • Option B: Used for debugging Apex and system events. • Option C: Salesforce-released updates, not a log of admin changes.

stem: The administrator at AW Computing wants Account details, related lists, and Chatter feeds to each appear on separate tabs when viewing an Account. Which type of page should the administrator create?

options.text: Lightning home page
Lightning app page
Lightning page component
Lightning record page

sourceExplanation: A Lightning record page for the Account object can be customized with tabs to organize details, related lists, and Chatter feeds into separate sections. Key takeaway: Lightning record pages support tabs for details, related lists and Chatter. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Used for dashboards and general information, not record-specific layouts. • Option B: Designed for app navigation, not record detail organization. • Option C: A building block, not a page type.

stem: Which setting on a profile makes a tab hidden in the All App Launcher or visible in any app, but still allows a user to view records that would normally be found under this tab?

options.text: Org-wide Defaults
Object Permissions
App Permissions
Tab Settings

sourceExplanation: Tab Settings control tab visibility. Setting a tab to "Hidden" removes it from navigation, but users can still access records via other means if they have object permissions. Key takeaway: Tab settings control tab visibility; object permissions control record access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Control record-level sharing, not tab visibility. • Option B: Control access to objects, not tab visibility. • Option C: Control access to apps and features, not individual tabs.

stem: What is the order of execution when a Case record is saved?

options.text: Assignment rules, Auto-response rules, Workflow rules, Escalation rules
Validation rules, Escalation rules, Workflow rules, Auto-response rules
Assignment rules, Validation rules, Workflow rules, Escalation rules
Validation rules, Assignment rules, Escalation rules, Auto-response rules

sourceExplanation: For Cases, the automation execution order is: Assignment Rules → Auto-Response Rules → Workflow Rules → Escalation Rules. (Note: Validation rules execute before the record is saved.) Key takeaway: Case automation order: assignment, auto-response, workflow, escalation. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Incorrect order; auto-response rules execute before escalation rules. • Option C: Validation rules execute before assignment rules. • Option D: Auto-response rules execute before escalation rules.

stem: Which three items are available in the mobile navigation menu?

options.text: Utility Bar
Dashboards
Lightning Home Page
Chatter

sourceExplanation: Dashboards, Lightning Home Pages, and Chatter can all be added to the Salesforce mobile navigation menu for user access. Key takeaway: The mobile navigation menu can include dashboards, home and Chatter. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: A desktop-only feature, not available in mobile.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to encourage employees to choose secure and appropriate passwords for their Salesforce accounts. Which three password policies should an administrator configure?

options.text: Prohibited password values
Number of days until expiration
Maximum invalid login attempts
Require use of Password Manager App
Password complexity requirements

sourceExplanation: • Prohibited password values – Blocks weak or common passwords. • Number of days until expiration – Ensures regular password changes. • Password complexity requirements – Enforces strong password creation. Key takeaway: Password policies include complexity, expiration and prohibited values. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Controls account lockout, not password strength. • Option D: Not a Salesforce password policy setting.

stem: DreamHouse Realty needs to use consistent picklist values in the Category field on Accounts and Cases, with values respective to record types. Which two features should the administrator use to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Custom picklist
Global picklist
Dependent picklist
Multi-select picklist

sourceExplanation: • Global Picklist – Ensures consistent picklist values across multiple objects. • Dependent Picklist – Allows control of which values appear based on record type or another field. Key takeaway: Global value sets share picklist values across objects. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Would need to be duplicated manually, risking inconsistency. • Option D: Allows multiple selections but does not enforce cross-object consistency.

stem: What are three settings an administrator should configure to make it easy for approvers to respond to approval requests?

options.text: Enable the organization's email approval response setting.
Update the organization's Chatter settings to allow approvals.
Specify initial submission actions within the approval process.
Add the Items to Approve component to the approvers' home page.
Create a flow to automatically approve all records.

sourceExplanation: • Enable email approval response – Allows approvers to respond via email. • Update Chatter settings to allow approvals – Enables approval actions within Chatter. • Add Items to Approve component – Provides a centralized view of pending approvals. Key takeaway: Email approval response, Chatter approvals and the Items to Approve component make responding easier. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Defines what happens when a record is submitted, not how approvers respond. • Option E: Bypasses the approval process entirely.

stem: An analytics user at Cloud Kicks needs Read, Create, and Edit access for objects and should be restricted from deleting any records. What should the administrator do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Give the user View All access and assign them to the highest role in the role hierarchy.
Assign the standard System Administrator profile to the analytics user.
Create and assign a custom profile with Delete access removed for each object.
Create and assign a permission set that includes Read, Create, and Edit access.

sourceExplanation: A permission set can grant Read, Create, and Edit object permissions without granting Delete access, providing precise control without modifying the user's profile. Key takeaway: Permission sets grant specific permissions without delete access. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: View All is read-only; does not grant Create/Edit. • Option B: Includes Delete access and excessive privileges. • Option C: While possible, it's less flexible and more maintenance than a permission set.

stem: Currently, when support reps at Ursa Major Solar close a case, they manually send an email notification to the customer. The support manager would like to automate this process, as too many reps are forgetting this step. Which two settings should the administrator use to meet this request?

options.text: Case close template in the support settings
Notify contact checkbox on close page layout
Add the Knowledge component to the closed layout
Auto-response rule step set for status of closed

sourceExplanation: • Case close template – Defines the email content sent upon case closure. • Notify contact checkbox – When checked during closure, automatically sends the close email. Key takeaway: Support settings include a case close notification template. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: Provides article access, not email automation. • Option D: Auto-response rules trigger on case creation, not closure.

stem: When users log in to Salesforce via the user interface, which two settings does the system check for authentication?

options.text: The role IP address restrictions
The user's multi-factor authentication for User Interface Logins permission
The user's profile login hours restrictions
The user's multi-factor authentication for API Logins permission

sourceExplanation: • Multi-factor authentication for User Interface Logins – Enforces MFA for UI access if required. • Profile login hours restrictions – Enforces allowed login times. Key takeaway: UI logins check MFA requirements and profile login hours. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: IP restrictions are set at the profile or network level, not by role. • Option D: Applies only to API logins, not UI.

stem: Ursa Solar Major is evaluating a brand new Salesforce org for its service team and would like to know what objects will be made available with out of the box Service Cloud. Which three of the standard objects are available to an administrator considering a support use case?

options.text: Request
Ticket
Case
Contract
Account

sourceExplanation: • Case – Core object for tracking customer issues. • Contract – Manages customer agreements and entitlements. • Account – Stores customer information. Key takeaway: Case, Account and Contract are standard objects used in service. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Not a standard Salesforce object. • Option B: Not a standard object; Cases are used instead.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants its reports to show a Fiscal Year that starts on February 1 and has 12 months. How should the administrator address this requirement?

options.text: Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the starting month as February.
Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the duration to 4 quarters.
Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the starting month as February.
Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the duration to 12 months.

sourceExplanation: A custom fiscal year with a February start month properly aligns reporting periods to the company's financial calendar. Key takeaway: Custom fiscal years allow non-standard start months and structures. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Standard fiscal year starts in January; cannot be changed to February. • Option B: Duration is automatically 12 months; specifying quarters is unnecessary. • Option D: Standard starts in January, not February.

stem: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to track ROI for contacts that are key stakeholders for opportunities. The VP of sales requested that this information be accessible on the opportunity and available for reporting. Which two options should the administrator configure to meet these requirements?

options.text: Add the Campaign Member related list and customize Campaign Role.
Customize Campaign Member Role and add the Opportunity Contact Role related list.
Customize Opportunity Contact Role and add the Campaign Member related list.
Customize Opportunity Contact Role and add the Opportunity Contact Role related list.

sourceExplanation: Customizing the Opportunity Contact Role object allows for tracking key stakeholders, and adding its related list to the Opportunity layout makes this information accessible directly on the record. Key takeaway: Opportunity contact roles track stakeholders for reporting. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: These are related to marketing campaigns, not opportunity stakeholders. • Option B: Campaign Member Role is for marketing campaigns, not opportunity roles. • Option C: The Campaign Member related list does not display opportunity stakeholder information.

stem: At Ursa Major Solar, a flow is in place that sends a reminder email 30 days before the warranty expiration date. A customer renews their warranty for another three years. What is the expected behavior of the email element in the flow?

options.text: The email is locked in the job queue until it meets the criteria.
The email is sent with the 30 day reminder criteria.
The email is not sent because the record no longer meets the criteria.
The email is not sent because the customer's email address was missing.

sourceExplanation: Scheduled flows evaluate the record's criteria at the scheduled runtime. Since the warranty was renewed, the original expiration date is no longer valid, and the record does not meet the criteria for sending the reminder, so the email is canceled. Key takeaway: Scheduled paths check the record criteria at execution time. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Scheduled flows do not pause; actions are executed or canceled based on the record state at the scheduled time. • Option B: The flow checks the current record data, which no longer satisfies the send criteria. • Option D: The scenario indicates the cancellation is due to criteria, not missing data.

stem: AW Computing wants to prevent users from updating the Account Annual Revenue field to be a negative value or an amount more than $100 billion. How should an administrator accomplish this request?

options.text: Enable Account Revenue limits in Setup, with 0 as the minimum and 100 billion as the maximum.
Build a scheduled report displaying Accounts with Account Revenue that is negative or greater than 100 billion.
Make the Account Revenue field required on the page layout.
Create a validation rule that displays an error if Account Revenue is below 0 or greater than 100 billion.

sourceExplanation: A validation rule can enforce data integrity by preventing a record save if the Account Annual Revenue field is outside the specified range (below 0 or above 100 billion). Key takeaway: Validation rules restrict values outside allowed ranges. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: No such standard setting exists in Salesforce Setup. • Option B: Reports only identify existing bad data; they do not prevent users from entering invalid values. • Option C: This only ensures a value is entered, not that the value is within a valid range.

stem: A new sales rep at Ursa Major Solar has a qualified lead that is ready for conversion. When using the Lead conversion process, which two records can be created?

options.text: Case and Campaign
Campaign and Account
Account and Contact
Contact and Case

sourceExplanation: During lead conversion, Salesforce can create an Account (for the company) and a Contact (for the individual) from the lead's information. Key takeaway: Lead conversion creates an account, a contact and optionally an opportunity. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Cases are not auto-created during conversion. Campaigns are marketing objects, not created by conversion. • Option B: Campaigns are not auto-created during conversion. • Option D: Cases are not auto-created during conversion.

stem: Ursa Major Solar provides a 1-year warranty on all of the panels it installs. Installation details, along with the warranty information, are captured on a custom object called Installation. The installation record is created by the installer from the mobile app. Customers sometimes receive a longer warranty as a way of increasing customer satisfaction when an installation gets delayed or has issues. How should the administrator configure Salesforce to capture the expiration date of the warranty?

options.text: Include the warranty Expiration Date field on the mobile page layout.
Add a validation rule to ensure the Expiration Date field is populated.
Create a formula field to display 1 year from the warranty purchased.
Use a formula as the default value of the warranty Expiration Date field.

sourceExplanation: Using a formula as the default value of the Expiration Date field pre-populates it with the standard 1-year date (for example, TODAY() + 365) when the installer creates the record, but the field remains editable so a longer warranty can be entered when needed. Key takeaway: Formula default values provide a starting value while remaining editable. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Placing the field on the layout without a default relies entirely on manual entry. • Option B: A validation rule forces entry but does not calculate the date. • Option C: A formula field is read-only, so it could not be changed when a customer receives a longer warranty.

stem: The marketing team at Ursa Major Solar wants to send a personalized email whenever a lead fills out the web-to-lead form on their website. They want to send different messages based on the Lead Industry field value. What should an administrator configure to meet this requirement?

options.text: Use a validation rule to trigger workflow to email the lead.
Create an assignment rule to email the lead.
Configure an auto-response rule to email the lead.
Add a public group and Process Builder to email the lead.

sourceExplanation: Auto-response rules are designed to send automated, personalized emails immediately after a lead is created (e.g., via web-to-lead) and can have different rule entries based on field values like Lead Industry. Key takeaway: Auto-response rules send different templates based on criteria. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Validation rules prevent data entry; they cannot trigger emails. • Option B: Assignment rules assign record ownership, they do not send emails. • Option D: While possible, it is less efficient than using the native auto-response rule feature built for this purpose.

stem: Cloud Kicks wants to give credit to Opportunity team members based on the level of effort contributed by each person toward each deal. What feature should the administrator use to meet this requirement?

options.text: Queues
Splits
List Views
Stages

sourceExplanation: Opportunity Splits allow administrators to distribute revenue or overlay credit among multiple team members based on their contribution to the deal. Key takeaway: Opportunity splits distribute credit among team members. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Queues assign record ownership, not credit. • Option C: List Views display records; they do not assign credit. • Option D: Stages track sales progress; they do not distribute credit.

stem: Cloud Kicks has a screen flow with two questions on the same screen, but only one is necessary at a time. The administrator has been asked to show only the question that is needed. How should an administrator complete this?

options.text: Use branching in the flow screen to show the proper scenario.
Use conditional visibility to hide the unnecessary question.
Use a decision element and a new screen to show the proper question.
Use a new version of the flow for each scenario.

sourceExplanation: Conditional visibility allows an administrator to dynamically show or hide individual screen components (like questions) based on the values of other fields or variables in the flow. Key takeaway: Conditional visibility shows only the relevant question. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Branching determines the next screen, not visibility of components on the current screen. • Option C: This creates extra screens and complexity, making the flow less efficient. • Option D: This is inefficient and unnecessary for dynamic screen behavior.

stem: The sales team at Ursa Major Solar has asked the administrator to automate an outbound message. What should the administrator utilize to satisfy the request?

options.text: Process Builder
Case Auto Response Rule
Task Assignment
Record-triggered flow

sourceExplanation: A record-triggered flow is the modern, recommended automation tool that can send an Outbound Message when a record is created or updated and meets specific criteria. Key takeaway: Flows can send outbound messages as actions. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Process Builder is being retired and should not be used for new automation. • Option B: This sends email responses for cases, not outbound messages to external systems. • Option C: This creates tasks for users; it does not send outbound messages.

stem: DreamHouse Realty wants to offer a form on its Experience Cloud site where inspectors will submit findings from a property inspection. Which feature should an administrator place on the page to fulfill this requirement?

options.text: Autolaunched Flow
Screen Flow
Record Detail
Related List

sourceExplanation: A Screen Flow provides a guided, interactive form that can be embedded in an Experience Cloud page to collect data (like inspection findings) and create or update Salesforce records. Key takeaway: Screen flows can be placed on Experience Cloud pages to collect data. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This runs in the background without a user interface. • Option C: This displays fields from an existing record. • Option D: This displays child records related to a parent.

stem: The administrator for AW Computing is working with a user who is having trouble logging in to Salesforce. What should the administrator do to identify why the user is unable to log in?

options.text: Reset the security token for the profile.
Check the attempted logins by running the setup audit trail.
Pull the password history to ensure the password policy was followed.
Review the login history for the user.

sourceExplanation: The Login History page provides detailed records of all login attempts, including failures and their reasons (e.g., wrong password, IP restriction), making it the direct tool to diagnose login issues. Key takeaway: Login History shows login attempts and failure reasons. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This is for API access issues, not standard UI login problems. • Option B: This tracks configuration changes, not user logins. • Option C: This shows past passwords but not the reason for a failed login attempt.

stem: DreamHouse Realty regularly processes customer requests for warranty work and would like to offer customers a self-serve option to generate cases. Which two solutions should an administrator use to meet this request?

options.text: Email-to-Case and Case Queues
Case Queues and Case Escalation
Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case
Web-to-Case and Case Escalation

sourceExplanation: • Web-to-Case: Allows customers to submit cases via a web form. • Email-to-Case: Allows customers to submit cases by sending an email to a designated address. Both provide self-service channels for case creation. Key takeaway: Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case let customers create cases. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Case Queues are for internal assignment, not customer self-service. • Option B: These are internal case management tools. • Option D: Case Escalation manages existing cases, it does not create new ones from customers.

stem: Cloud Kicks has decided to delete a custom field. What will happen to the data in the field when it is deleted?

options.text: The data associated with the field is removed.
The data in the field is stored for 20 days.
The data is restorable from the recycle bin.
The data is permanently deleted.

sourceExplanation: When a custom field is deleted, it enters a 15-day "soft delete" period. During this time, the field and its data can be restored from the Recycle Bin. Key takeaway: Deleted custom fields can be restored within 15 days. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: The data is not immediately removed; it is recoverable. • Option B: The soft delete period is 15 days, not 20. • Option D: Permanent deletion occurs only after the 15-day period.

stem: Cloud Kicks (CK) captures whether an opportunity should be reviewed by someone in product engineering with a checkbox field called Needs Review. CK also has a picklist field on the opportunity for Product Type. When a sales rep saves an opportunity, they need to select the Product Type or check the Needs Review box. What should an administrator use to accomplish this?

options.text: Required fields
Before Save flow
Workflow rule
Validation rule

sourceExplanation: A validation rule can enforce conditional logic (an "either/or" requirement) by preventing the record save if both the Product Type is blank AND the Needs Review checkbox is unchecked. Key takeaway: Validation rules enforce either/or data requirements. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: This enforces that a specific field is always populated, not conditionally. • Option B: While it can set field values, it is not the primary tool for preventing a save based on validation logic. • Option C: Workflow rules perform actions after a record is saved; they cannot prevent the save itself.

stem: The VP of sales at DreamHouse Realty has requested a dashboard to visualize enterprise sales across the different teams. The key piece of data is the total of all sales for the year and the progress to the enterprise sales goal. What dashboard component will effectively show this number and the proximity to the total goal as a single value?

options.text: Donut
Gauge
Table
Stacked Bar

sourceExplanation: A Gauge component is designed to display a single key metric (like total sales) against a defined target or goal, visually indicating progress. Key takeaway: Gauge components show progress toward a goal. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Shows proportions of a whole, not a single metric vs. a goal. • Option C: Displays detailed data, not a summarized progress indicator. • Option D: Compares values across categories, not progress to a single goal.

stem: Sales and Customer Care at Ursa Major Solar need to see different fields on the Case related list from the Account record. Sales users want to see Case created date and status while Customer Care would like to see owner, status, and contact. What should the administrator use to achieve this?

options.text: Page Layout Editor
Related Lookup Filters
Compact Layout Editor
Search Layout Editor

sourceExplanation: The columns displayed in a related list are configured per page layout (related list properties in the Page Layout Editor). By using separate Account page layouts for Sales and Customer Care, each with different Case related list columns, and assigning them by profile, each team sees its own fields. Key takeaway: Related list columns are set per page layout. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: Lookup filters restrict which records can be selected in a lookup field; they do not change related list columns. • Option C: Compact layouts control the highlights panel and record previews, not the columns of a related list. • Option D: Search layouts control search results and lookup dialogs.

stem: Universal Containers requires a different Lightning page to be displayed when Accounts are viewed in the Sales Console and in the Service Console. How should an administrator meet this requirement?

options.text: Define multiple record types.
Create different user profiles.
Update page layout assignments.
Assign Lightning pages as app default.

sourceExplanation: In the Lightning App Builder, an administrator can assign a specific Lightning Record Page as the default for an object (like Account) on a per-app basis (e.g., Sales Console vs. Service Console). Key takeaway: Lightning record pages can be assigned as app defaults. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Record types can control page layouts, but the requirement is based on the app used, not the record type. • Option B: Profiles control permissions, not app-specific page assignments. • Option C: Page layouts are assigned by record type and profile, not by app.

stem: What are two considerations an administrator should keep in mind when working with Salesforce objects?

options.text: Custom and standard objects have standard fields.
Standard objects are included with Salesforce.
A new standard object can be created.
Only standard objects support master-detail relationships.

sourceExplanation: • Option A: Custom and standard objects have standard fields: Both object types come with standard system fields like CreatedDate, OwnerId, etc. • Option B: Standard objects are included with Salesforce: Standard objects (like Account, Contact) are pre-built and part of the Salesforce platform. Key takeaway: Standard objects are included with Salesforce; all objects have standard fields. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option C: A new standard object can be created: Administrators can only create custom objects, not new standard ones. • Option D: Only standard objects support master-detail relationships: Both custom and standard objects can be part of master-detail relationships.

stem: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar wants to add prepopulated subjects for Tasks and Events. Tasks should have the subjects Schedule Site Visit and Send Contract, while Events should have the subjects Site Visit and Ride Along. How can this requirement be configured?

options.text: Add the new values to the predefined field values for the global actions New Event and New Task.
Include Schedule Site Visit, Send Contract, Site Visit, and Ride Along picklist values for the Activity subject field.
Create a new custom Subject picklist field on Activity and add the field values.
Add Schedule Site Visit and Send Contract picklist values for the Task subject field. Add Site Visit and Ride Along picklist values for Event subject field.

sourceExplanation: The Task Subject and Event Subject fields each have their own picklist values, configured separately in Object Manager (Task fields and Event fields). Adding Schedule Site Visit and Send Contract to the Task Subject and Site Visit and Ride Along to the Event Subject meets the requirement. Key takeaway: Task and Event Subject picklists are configured separately. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option A: Predefined field values set a single default value on an action; they do not provide multiple subject choices. • Option B: Adding all values to a shared field would show event subjects on tasks and vice versa. • Option C: A custom field is unnecessary because the standard Subject fields can be configured.

stem: At Universal Containers, there is a custom field on the Lead named Product Category. Management wants this information to be part of the Opportunity upon lead conversion. What action should the administrator take to satisfy the request?

options.text: Create a custom field on the Opportunity and map the two fields.
Configure the product categories picklist field on the product.
Create a workflow to update Opportunity fields based on the lead.
Map the lead custom field to the product's product category field.

sourceExplanation: During lead conversion, custom fields from the Lead can be mapped to custom fields on the Account, Contact, or Opportunity. The administrator must first create a matching custom field on the Opportunity object, then establish the mapping in the Lead conversion settings. Key takeaway: Custom lead fields map to custom opportunity fields during conversion. Why the other options are incorrect: • Option B: This relates to the Product object, not the Opportunity created from the lead. • Option C: This is inefficient and unnecessary when native field mapping during conversion is available. • Option D: The requirement is to map to the Opportunity, not to a Product field.
